# Storage design — Stage 2 implementation plan: agents work in the project's own folder

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Build Part II of the storage design: in a project conversation an agent lists, reads, writes and edits the project's real files and runs commands there — each write and each command asking first, the card naming the folder — a file written for the person lands in the project with a pointer row that the chat card, the Library, Open and Reveal show, drafts and hand-offs stay under `~/.openalpaca` as by-products, and a conversation with no project works in its own scratch folder.

**Architecture:** Eight slices built in order, guards before the root moves. S1 tightens confinement before any tool acts on a project (R31's link rule, R32's `.git`/`.openalpaca` rule built and off, `send` confined, the `../` filter narrowed to tools whose arguments reach a program, and the kill of a command that times out or is cancelled). S2 makes the approval card name the folder and stops the by-product writers asking. S3 moves the tools onto the call's working folder — the project's root, or `~/.openalpaca/scratch/<session-id>/` — with the session id on every sandboxed context and the model told its folder. S4a adds the pointer row (migration 004) and lets `file_write` write the real file; S4b adds the pre-edit copy's new home and `file_edit`. S5 adds `file_list` and `artifact_read` and settles who holds which tool. S6a brings the app's surfaces to result files; S6 rewrites the words and documents, runs the one gate, the live check and the records.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 1.93.0 (edition 2024), rusqlite, serde, tokio (process groups via `libc::killpg` on unix), axum; React 19 + TypeScript + Vitest (bun) for the app; `cargo test` per crate; the local Ollama `qwen3.8:27b-mlx` for the live check only.

**Spec:** `tasks/storage-design/design.md` rev 0.9 (approved 2026-10-05; Stages 0 and 1 built) — §0.1 (owner decisions ST-1…ST-22; this stage builds ST-10, ST-11, ST-12, ST-14's card, ST-15, ST-16, ST-17, ST-18, ST-22), §0.4's two Stage 2 items, Part II §10–§15, §16 *Order*, §17 *Records*, §18's Stage 0 item for Stage 2's wording pass. **The lead's rulings on the drafts:** R-T1…R-T16, in *Rulings* below — binding on every implementer; R-T2 and R-T3 are for the owner to confirm with this plan.

**Where this plan came from:** an interfaces sheet and eight slice drafts, each written against the tree at `d484a56a` by an Opus drafter and corrected in place by an Opus verifier against the code; a cross-slice consistency check (eight mismatches fixed in the drafts, fourteen items ruled as R-T1…R-T14); the lead's rulings applied. Line numbers are of that tree and drift as slices land: **locate code by content**. Inside the slices the drafting stage's references stand: `interfaces.md` §N is *Shared interfaces* §N below; `spec-stage2.md` is the excerpt of design rev 0.9 in `tasks/storage-design/plan-drafts/stage2/`; "the S1…S6 drafts" (`S1.md`…`S6.md`, "in this folder") are this plan's slices of those names, whose sources sit in that folder; and a slice's "draft's *Spec conflicts*" is that slice's *Spec conflicts* section here.

## Global Constraints

- **Model policy (owner, 2026-10-06):** Opus 5.5 does every job — implementing, each review, the final review. Fable 5.1 only as the advisor.
- **Order:** S1 → S2 → S3 → S4a → S4b → S5 → S6a → S6, tasks in their numbered order except S3, whose slice gate S3.12 runs after S3.13 (R-T2's task; numbers kept), and S4a, which lands S4a.11 last (R-T1). Each commit leaves the workspace compiling and its own crate's tests green; a symbol built before its first non-test user carries an `allow` that the user's commit removes.
- **One cargo process at a time**, always (`pgrep -x cargo` before each). Per task: `cargo test -p <crate> <filter>` as the task gives it. The workspace run happens **once**, at the stage gate (S6), then `pkill -f "sleep 3600"`.
- **The owner's store is never touched.** `~/.openalpaca` is never read, written, listed or pointed at — not by a command, not by a test, not even read-only. Every test that touches a store uses a tempfile directory and the crate's home-store guard.
- **From this stage on the tools act on real files.** Every test that writes, edits, lists, reads or runs a command does it in a tempdir project registered under the crate's guard (`GuardedProject`), never in the repository and never in a folder outside a tempdir. A test that spawns a process kills it: no child may outlive its test (each slice gate checks `pgrep -fl '^sleep 30$'` prints nothing).
- **No test reaches `localhost:11434`** (a test enabling a provider uses a mock or `127.0.0.1:1`). The live check is the one place the local model is used, under the owner's standing authorization, with the daemon under `scripts/eval/memory/loopback-only.sb` from its first launch and the scratch root canonicalized when it is made.
- **Clippy baseline 78** (`CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never cargo clippy --workspace --exclude openalpaca_gui --all-targets`, lines starting `warning` minus the `generated N warnings` lines). A slice may not add one.
- **Routes and migrations:** a commit that changes a route, a refusal code or a migration regenerates `docs/api` with `python3 scripts/gen_api_docs.py` in the same commit; `--check` is clean at every slice's end. Migration `004_project_files.sql` follows CLAUDE.md's recipe (it registers 4; the `MIGRATIONS` entry; the comment bump to 5; `gen_api_docs` parity), and CLAUDE.md's *Storage* paragraph moves with it in the same commit.
- **GUI:** a commit under `apps/openalpaca-gui/` runs all four bun gates (`bun run check`, `bun run test`, `bun run format:check`, `bun run build` in `apps/openalpaca-gui`); a change under `src-tauri` runs `cargo check -p openalpaca_gui` (CI compiles nothing there).
- **Tool definitions:** a builtin marked strict passes `openai_tools::strict_mode_compatible` and is listed in the builtins' strict test, or is named in its `NOT_STRICT` exemption (CLAUDE.md Gotchas). An approval surface shows tool- or model-controlled text escaped through `utils::text` / `lib/hidden-chars`, with its count line; its test plants a U+202E and a U+200B.
- **Code rules:** no `&s[..n]` string cut; `std::env::set_var`/`remove_var` only inside `unsafe { }` where no other thread can touch the environment, with a `// SAFETY:` comment; snake_case sentence test names; anchored edits (never BSD `sed -i`); a new `.md` under `tasks/` is git-ignored unless whitelisted.
- **Commits:** conventional prefix, a `Verified:` line naming the command and its result, last line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Stage explicit paths only (an untracked `tasks/deps-upgrade/` belongs to another session).
- **Scope:** a task does what its text and the spec ask, nothing more. A spec conflict a draft records is settled by R-T15 or a named ruling; anything new is reported, not improvised.

## Review Focus

Input classes the spec implies that are most likely to bite a person; each is pinned by a test in the owning task.

1. **A path that leaves the project** — a link inside the project pointing outside it, `..`, an absolute path, a `.git` or `.openalpaca` component in any letter case — on a read, a list, a write, an edit or a `send`: refused, and a link is never written through (S1.1–S1.5, R31, R32, R23; S3 switches the project rule on).
2. **A command that hangs, times out or is cancelled while it has started children** — the whole process group is killed and nothing keeps running in the person's project after the tool reported it stopped (S1.9–S1.12, R45).
3. **Replacing or editing a person's file** — the old content is copied under `sessions/<id>/snapshots/` before the change; a file over 10 MiB, or one with no session log to copy into, is refused for replacement; `file_edit` keeps every other byte, line endings included (a CRLF file stays CRLF, R-T11), and refuses a non-UTF-8 file, a missing file (naming `file_write`) and an ambiguous `old_string` (S4a.10, S4b, ST-17, R46, R47).
4. **A result file the person edits, deletes, moves or replaces with a link after the agent wrote it** — a read refreshes the row's hash and size and records no version, a missing file is marked and found again, a link is never followed out of the project, deleting the project's data and re-pointing it never touch the real file (S4a, R37, R39's seven tests).
5. **A conversation with no project** — it works in its own scratch folder, which no other conversation's file tools can see and which goes with the conversation; its `file_write` is still a by-product (ST-10); a run parked through `POST /v1/tasks` gets a conversation and so a folder (S3, R-T2, R44).

## Rulings (the lead's; binding on every implementer)

Numbered R-T1… so they never collide with the design's R1–R49, Stage 1's R-S1…R-S18 or the final review's R-F1…R-F8. Source: `consistency.md` §4 (L1–L14), the drafters' and verifiers' notes. Two of them add an enforcement point or move when a row is created (R-T2, R-T3); they are listed for the owner to confirm with the plan.

- **R-T1 (L1) — S4a lands S4a.11 last:** order 1–10, 12–17, 18, 11 (task numbers kept — later slices cite "S4a.11"). The slice gate runs after the last task. Reason: no commit offers Open on an agent-written script, or follows a link out of the project, before the readers that guard it exist (§16's "guards before the root moves", inside the slice).
- **R-T2 (L2) — a run parked by `POST /v1/tasks` on a lane with no session gets one:** the dispatcher's fallback (`dispatcher/lead_agent.rs`, where it reads `active_session_id(lane_key)`) calls `get_or_create_active_session(lane_key, source, None)` — the same call the run's finalisation already makes when it posts the report (`dispatcher/outcome.rs`, the report step), only earlier — so the run has a conversation, a session log and a scratch folder (spec §10). One new task in S3 beside S3.11; S3.4's test then pins the scratch folder instead of the refusal, and `NoConversation`'s sentence stays for a call that has neither. *For the owner to confirm with the plan (a session row is created at dispatch rather than at report).*
- **R-T3 (L3) — `send` by `artifact_id` refuses another project's by-product,** with `artifact_read`'s sentence (S5.2), in S4a.17, which already rewrites `SendTool::artifact`. One rule then governs which by-products a conversation may name. *For the owner to confirm with the plan (a new refusal on a path that already asks for approval).*
- **R-T4 (L4) — the S3.3 → S4a.11 window is accepted and recorded:** R33 leaves `file_write` in S3.3 while its startup root moves in S4a.11; production writes a by-product in between (the startup root is the home store); only a hand-started development daemon above `~/.openalpaca` could `file_write` into `state/` or the persona, after an approval card. Unreleased commits only (Stage 1's "no build ships mid-stage"). S6.6 lists it in §18 with C8.
- **R-T5 (L5) — `file_write` with neither project nor conversation is a by-product,** as S4a built it (ST-10: a by-product's place is the owner's store, not a folder).
- **R-T6 (L6) — `file_list` comes wherever `file_read` is on the main loop's surface** (by keyword, or on a project turn), in S5.6 — R42's "comes with `file_read`"; one hint text.
- **R-T7 (L7) — the relay rules gain one sentence:** "When no tool that writes a file is on your surface, a file the user asks for is `start_workflow`'s." (S5, beside §15's rewrite of the bullet that said chat cannot write a file.)
- **R-T8 (L8) — a pointer row attached to a chat turn is refused** with `artifact_read`'s sentence (a file in the project; read it with `file_read`) — new task S4a.18, the last reader R37 did not cover (`chat/service.rs::load_attachment_assets`, `orchestrator/handler_attachments.rs`).
- **R-T9 (L9) — `GET /v1/status`'s `produced_bytes` counts by-products only:** `AND in_project = 0` in `storage_bytes_by_origin`, beside S4a.6's filters (the number is what the store holds).
- **R-T10 (L10) — `no_artifact_reason` stays** ("No artifacts were produced."); the report's runtime line names the result files.
- **R-T11 (L11) — `file_edit` keeps CRLF:** in S4b.1 `apply_edit` converts `new_string`'s `\n` to `\r\n` when the file holds `\r\n` and no lone `\n`; one test (a one-line `old_string`, a two-line `new_string`, the file stays all-CRLF).
- **R-T12 (L12) — both hidden-character counts stay on a card:** the card's own count line under its text and the surface's count under the arguments (each escaped block carries its own count — the Gotcha's rule).
- **R-T13 (L13) — `file_write`'s description gains one sentence** in S4b.1: "To change part of an existing file in the project, use file_edit."
- **R-T14 (L14) — one "project turn" predicate:** computed once in `simple_query_handler.rs` (`scope_from_context`'s project arm) and handed to S4b.4 (`file_edit`) and S5.6 (the readers).
- **R-T15 — every recorded spec conflict in the drafts stands as drafted** (consistency.md §4 *Accept as drafted*: S1 C1–C8, S2 C1–C3, S3 C1 and C3–C6, S4a C1–C7 and C9–C11, S4b C-S4b-1…6, S5 C-S5-1…7, S6a C1–C6, S6's conflicts), and the sheet rows the drafts departed from (consistency.md §6) are the contract — the plan's *Shared interfaces* carries them.
- **R-T16 — recorded, not built (S6.6 writes them into design §18):** S4b's stale card between plan and body; the bytes read vs copied; R35's row follows its latest writer; the delete card counts no result rows; plugin agents and plugin skills get no R28 line; R45's residue (a process that leaves its group — `setsid`, a double fork — is out of reach; Windows kills the direct child only; the force-exit path runs no drop; commands in their own process group no longer get a terminal Ctrl-C; a background-group command reading `/dev/tty` stops until its timeout); an `ensure` test-build tripwire; R-T4's window; S2's C8 (the shell card names the project before the shell runs there).

**Rules each slice carries** (CLAUDE.md is the authority):

- One cargo process at a time (`pgrep -x cargo` first); per task `cargo test -p <crate> <filter>`; never the workspace
  (S6's gate is the one workspace run, then `pkill -f "sleep 3600"`).
- `~/.openalpaca` is never read, listed, written or pointed at. Every test that touches a store holds its crate's
  guard: `crate::store::tests::HomeStoreGuard::set` (storage), `crate::test_util::HomeStoreGuard::set` (core, daemon),
  `crate::test_util::EnvSandbox::enter` (CLI). A project in a test is a tempdir registered under the guard
  (`openalpaca_storage::store::projects::register`). **From Stage 2 on the file tools and the shell act on real files
  in the project**: every test that writes, edits, lists or runs a command does it in a tempdir project (core and the
  daemon: `GuardedProject`, §1.6), never in the repository and never in the process's current directory.
- A test that spawns a process kills it: every R45 test kills its own children through the helper under test and
  carries a `Drop` guard that `SIGKILL`s the recorded pid if an assertion fails first (§3.3). No `sleep 3600`.
- No test reaches `localhost:11434`. No `&s[..n]` on a `str` (`utils::text::byte_prefix`, `floor_char_boundary`,
  or `escape_hidden_within`'s budget). `std::env::set_var` only inside the guards (`unsafe`, `// SAFETY:` comment).
- Snake_case sentence test names; anchored edits (no BSD `sed -i`); conventional commit prefix, a `Verified:` line
  naming the command and its result, last line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`; stage
  explicit paths (an untracked `tasks/deps-upgrade/` belongs to another session).
- **Clippy baseline 78** (`CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never cargo clippy --workspace --exclude openalpaca_gui --all-targets`,
  lines starting `warning` minus the `generated N warnings` lines). A slice may not add one.
- **docs/api:** a commit that changes a route's request struct, a refusal code, a migration, a storage `lib.rs`
  re-export or a GUI `lib/api/*.ts` export runs `python3 scripts/gen_api_docs.py` and stages `docs/api/` in the same
  commit; `--check` is clean at every slice's end. In this stage: S4a (migration 004, `ListArtifactsParams.in_project`,
  the `NewProjectFile` re-export, `OPEN_NOT_OFFERED`), S6a (the GUI exports). Core lists only its top-level modules,
  so `tools::working_folder` changes no generated doc.
- **live-eval compile check** (`cargo check -p openalpaca_core --features live-eval --tests`, compile only, never
  run): S2 (`ToolContext`), S3, S4a, S5.
- **GUI:** a commit under `apps/openalpaca-gui/` runs all four bun gates in `apps/openalpaca-gui`: `bun run check`,
  `bun run test`, `bun run format:check`, `bun run build`.
- A new builtin marked `strict: Some(true)` must pass `openai_tools::strict_mode_compatible` and be counted in
  `every_builtin_goes_to_openai_with_strict_only_where_strict_mode_accepts_it` (§7.4).
- An approval surface shows third-party text escaped through `openalpaca_core::utils::text` (Rust) /
  `lib/hidden-chars` (GUI): §4.
- The memory index's `SCHEMA_VERSION` does not move in this stage (no memory row changes).

### 1. The working folder

#### 1.1 The context field (S2 adds, S3 sets)

`crates/openalpaca_core/src/tools/registry/mod.rs`, `ToolContext`, after `session_id`:

```rust
/// The conversation (the `session` row) this call belongs to, whether or not
/// its loop writes a session log — what names a conversation's scratch folder
/// when the turn has no project (design §10, R44). Distinct from
/// [`session_id`](Self::session_id), whose `Some` means exactly "the session
/// writer indexes this call" and which the agentic loop overwrites from its
/// own log handle. Inherited by every context cloned from this one (nested
/// skills, plugin agents).
pub conversation_id: Option<String>,
```

Every `ToolContext { .. }` literal in the tree uses `..Default::default()` (checked at HEAD: 0 exhaustive literals), so
the field is additive. S2 adds it and sets it nowhere outside tests; S3 sets it (§1.5).

#### 1.2 The function (S2), new module `crates/openalpaca_core/src/tools/working_folder.rs`

`crates/openalpaca_core/src/tools/mod.rs` gains `pub mod working_folder;`.

```rust
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use crate::tools::registry::ToolContext;

/// Where a tool call's files and commands live (design §10).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum WorkingFolder {
    /// The turn's registered project: its canonical root (`Project::root`).
    Project { root: PathBuf },
    /// No project: `<home>/scratch/<session_dir_name(conversation_id)>`.
    Scratch { dir: PathBuf, conversation_id: String },
}

impl WorkingFolder {
    /// The folder itself.
    pub fn path(&self) -> &Path;
    pub fn is_project(&self) -> bool;
    /// The folder, ready to act in (S3): a scratch folder is created when
    /// absent — `<home>/scratch` and the folder, each 0700 on unix — and a
    /// project root is required to be a directory (it was found to be one by
    /// `working_folder`). Errors are `WorkingFolderRefusal::Unavailable`.
    pub fn ensure(&self) -> Result<&Path, WorkingFolderRefusal>;
}

/// Why a call has no working folder. `Display` is the one sentence the model,
/// the card and the report read.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum WorkingFolderRefusal {
    /// A tool reached through `execute` (no context) — R26.
    NoContext,
    /// R27: the project is registered and its folder is gone (ST-7).
    ProjectMissing { root: String },
    /// The turn's root names no folder under `projects/` any more — re-pointed
    /// or deleted while the conversation ran.
    NotAProject { root: String },
    /// R44: neither a project nor a conversation id.
    NoConversation,
    /// `projects/` or the home root could not be read, or the scratch folder
    /// could not be made.
    Unavailable { reason: String },
}
impl std::fmt::Display for WorkingFolderRefusal { /* §1.3 */ }
impl std::error::Error for WorkingFolderRefusal {}

/// Pure — reads two small files at most and **creates nothing** (S2).
/// 1. `ctx.request_workspace_root` non-empty and absolute →
///    `openalpaca_storage::store::projects::lookup(Path::new(root))`:
///    `Ok(Some(p))` with `!p.missing` → `Project { root: p.root }`;
///    `Ok(Some(p))` with `p.missing` → `ProjectMissing`; `Ok(None)` →
///    `NotAProject`; `Err(e)` → `Unavailable { reason: format!("{e:#}") }`.
///    A non-empty relative value → `NotAProject`.
/// 2. Else `ctx.conversation_id` `Some(id)` → `Scratch { dir:
///    store::home_root()?.join(ContentKind::Scratch.dir_name())
///    .join(crate::session_log::session_dir_name(id)), conversation_id: id }`
///    (`home_root` failing → `Unavailable`).
/// 3. Else `NoConversation`.
pub fn working_folder(ctx: &ToolContext) -> Result<WorkingFolder, WorkingFolderRefusal>;

/// R28 (S3): the one line a turn's context carries — `Some` for a folder and
/// for `ProjectMissing` / `NotAProject` (their sentence, so the model knows up
/// front), `None` for the other refusals. Text in §1.3.
pub fn working_folder_note(ctx: &ToolContext) -> Option<String>;

/// S3: the scratch folder of a conversation — the path only, nothing created.
pub fn scratch_dir(conversation_id: &str) -> anyhow::Result<PathBuf>;

/// S3: removes a conversation's scratch folder. `Ok(false)` when it was not
/// there. Never follows a link: a link at the folder's name is removed as a
/// link (`symlink_metadata`), a directory with `remove_dir_all`.
pub fn remove_scratch(conversation_id: &str) -> std::io::Result<bool>;
```

`lookup` is used, not `by_recorded_root`: `request_workspace_root` is the canonical root the gateway resolved and
recorded (R-F7's residue in design §18 stands as recorded).

#### 1.3 The sentences (S2 writes the refusals; S3 writes the note)

| What | Text (exact) |
|---|---|
| `NoContext` | `This tool acts in the conversation's working folder, and this call carries no conversation to name one.` |
| `ProjectMissing` | `The project folder {root} is missing — its folder is gone: re-point the project to where its folder is now (Settings → Connection → Projects → Re-point…, or openalpaca store rebase {root} <new path>), or delete its data (Delete data…, or openalpaca store purge {root}). No file tool or command runs until then.` (§6's one sentence naming the two actions; its first clause is `store list`'s, `commands/store.rs:309`.) |
| `NotAProject` | `ProjectError::NotRegistered { root }.to_string()` verbatim — `{root} is not a project OpenAlpaca knows: no folder under projects/ records it` |
| `NoConversation` | `This call has neither a project nor a conversation, so it has no working folder: file tools and commands run only inside a conversation or a project.` |
| `Unavailable` | `The working folder could not be read: {reason}` |
| note, project | `<working_folder>Your working folder is the project folder {root}. Paths in file_read, file_list, file_write, file_edit and send are relative to it, and a shell command starts in it.</working_folder>` |
| note, scratch | `<working_folder>This conversation has no project. Your working folder is its scratch folder {dir}: paths in file_read, file_list and send are relative to it, and a shell command starts in it. file_write saves a by-product in OpenAlpaca's artifact store instead.</working_folder>` |
| note, missing / not a project | `<working_folder>{the refusal's sentence}</working_folder>` |

The root and the scratch path are printed unescaped: the owner's own path and OpenAlpaca's (Stage 1's recorded choice).

#### 1.4 What it returns before and after S3

The function is the same from S2 on; what changes is who sets `conversation_id` and who calls it.

| | S2 (and S2→S3 window) | From S3 |
|---|---|---|
| A project turn | `Project { root }` | same |
| A turn with no project | `NoConversation` — nothing sets `conversation_id` yet | `Scratch { dir }` on every path of §1.5; `NoConversation` only for a run with neither (below) |
| Callers | the S2 previews only (§4.2) — which map any refusal to `Ok(None)`, today's ordinary card, never `Err` | the tools' bodies (S3: `file_read`, `shell_execute`, command tools, `send`; S4a: `file_write`; S4b: `file_edit`; S5: `file_list`), their previews (refusal → `Err(sentence)`, no card), the R28 note |

**Recorded window (§10 C8):** between S2 and S3 a project turn's shell card names the project folder while the
command still runs in the daemon's folder. Unreleased commits only; S3 closes it. No drafter "fixes" it in S2.

#### 1.5 Who sets `conversation_id` (S3, R44)

| Path | Site (locate by content) | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Main loop | `orchestrator/query_handler/simple_query_handler.rs`, the `let tool_ctx = ToolContext {` literal (~:140) | `ConversationRepository::new(db).active_session_id(lane_key)` read **once** before the literal and reused for the `session_log` open (~:258) that reads the same value today |
| File-skill tier | `orchestrator/skill/invocation.rs`, the first `let tool_ctx = ToolContext {` (~:763) | the same `active_session_id(lane_key)` read (`self.db`) |
| Plugin skill | `orchestrator/skill/invocation.rs`, the second (~:1261) | same |
| Nested skills | `orchestrator/skill/invoke_executor.rs`, `child_tool_ctx` (~:272) | inherited by `.cloned()` — no edit |
| Lead | `runner/lead_agent/mod.rs`, `let tool_ctx = ToolContext {` (~:286) | the `session_id: Option<&str>` parameter `run_lead_agent` already takes, `.map(str::to_string)` |
| Subagents | `runner/lead_agent/tools.rs`, `let subagent_tool_ctx = ToolContext {` (~:338) | a new last parameter of `SpawnSubagentTool::new(.., unattended: bool, conversation_id: Option<String>)`, stored on the struct; the lead passes its own; every other caller (tests) passes `None` |
| Plugin agents | `runner/plugin_agent.rs` `run_plugin_agent_loop(.., tool_ctx: &ToolContext)` | inherits the subagent's context — no edit |
| Agentic loop | `runner/agentic_loop/mod.rs` (~:1086–1103) | untouched: it overwrites `session_id`/`session_log` only, never `conversation_id` |

Every gateway turn has a session row: `GatewayPersistence::resolve_turn_session` (`gateway/persistence.rs:116`) calls
`get_or_create_active_session` — so connector lanes and scheduled skills (which enter through `Gateway::handle_event`)
get a scratch folder. A run's session is resolved at dispatch (`dispatcher/lead_agent.rs:330-337`: resume's, the
turn's, else the lane's active one). **A run parked by `POST /v1/tasks` on a lane with no session and with no project
has neither: every file tool and command in it is refused `NoConversation`.** S3's test pins that sentence.
*Superseded by R-T2 (S3.13): such a run now gets a session at dispatch, and so a scratch folder; `NoConversation` stays
for a call that has neither — see the settled table below.*

#### 1.6 The scratch folder's life

- **Created** on first use by `WorkingFolder::ensure()`, which every acting tool calls before it touches the folder
  (S3: `file_read`, `shell_execute`, command tools, `send`; S4a/S4b/S5 the rest). The previews and the R28 note call
  only `working_folder` (pure), so a conversation that never uses a tool gets no folder.
- **Removed** with the conversation, by `working_folder::remove_scratch(id)` (S3), at the two paths that delete a
  conversation: `apps/openalpacad/src/routes/sessions.rs::delete_session` (beside `remove_session_log`, after the rows
  went) and `apps/openalpacad/src/routes/workspaces.rs::remove_session_dirs` (for each id; a session that once had no
  project before it was bound can hold one). A failure is one `warn!` naming the path, as `remove_session_log` does.
- **Not removed** by clearing a conversation (`routes/chat.rs::after_history_cleared` empties it; it survives), by
  archiving one, by the session-log byte caps (`session_log::sweep`), or by the factory reset (which leaves
  content folders as orphans, as it leaves `sessions/`).
- `ContentKind::Scratch`'s doc (`store/mod.rs:407`, "Reserved: nothing creates it until Stage 2") → S3 rewrites it.
- The factory reset's preview (`apps/openalpaca/src/commands/config_factory_reset.rs`, the *Left on disk, and from
  now on unreferenced* list, a Rust string its tests pin) gains `  - {root}/scratch/` after `{root}/sessions/` → S3.

#### 1.7 Shared test helper (S2 in core; S4a adds the daemon's twin)

`crates/openalpaca_core/src/test_util.rs` (S2) and `apps/openalpacad/src/test_util.rs` (S4a), same shape:

```rust
/// A guarded temp home store and one temp project folder registered under it:
/// every Stage 2 test that writes, edits, lists or runs a command does it here.
/// `_guard` is declared first so it drops first (the variable is restored
/// before the folders go).
pub(crate) struct GuardedProject {
    _guard: HomeStoreGuard,
    pub(crate) home: tempfile::TempDir,
    pub(crate) project: tempfile::TempDir,
    /// The project's canonical root, as `projects::register` recorded it.
    pub(crate) root: std::path::PathBuf,
}

impl GuardedProject {
    /// Two tempdirs; `HomeStoreGuard::set(&home.path().canonicalize())`;
    /// `projects::register(&project.path().canonicalize())`.
    pub(crate) fn new() -> Self;
    /// `owner_id: Some("owner-test")`, `request_workspace_root` and
    /// `workspace_id` = `root`, `conversation_id: Some("conv-test")`.
    pub(crate) fn ctx(&self) -> ToolContext;          // core only
    /// The same with no project: `conversation_id: Some("conv-test")` only.
    pub(crate) fn scratch_ctx(&self) -> ToolContext;  // core only
    /// `home.path().canonicalize()`.
    pub(crate) fn home_root(&self) -> std::path::PathBuf;
}
```

### 2. The path resolvers (S1 builds; S3, S4a switch the rule on)

`crates/openalpaca_core/src/tools/builtins/helpers/mod.rs`. Names kept (minimal churn: 26 test call sites); each
gains a third parameter.

```rust
/// What R32 adds to confinement (design §11).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum FolderRules {
    /// The folder is a project: `.git` refused for writing, `.openalpaca`
    /// refused for reading and writing — any component, compared without case,
    /// on the path relative to the canonical root after resolution.
    Project,
    /// A scratch folder, and until S3/S4a every startup-root caller: no extra rule.
    Plain,
}

/// R31's read side (unchanged rule): relative, no `..`, the whole path
/// canonicalized (every component, the last included) and under the
/// canonical root; then R32's read rule when `rules == Project`.
pub(super) fn resolve_workspace_path(
    relative_path: &str,
    workspace_root: &Path,
    rules: FolderRules,
) -> Result<PathBuf, String>;

/// R31's write side: as today (nearest existing ancestor of the parent
/// canonicalized, the missing directories re-appended), **plus the leaf**:
/// when a directory entry stands at the leaf (`symlink_metadata` Ok), the
/// whole path is canonicalized and must be under the root — a link out of the
/// root is refused, a dangling link is refused (canonicalize fails). Then
/// R32's write rule when `rules == Project`.
pub(super) fn resolve_workspace_path_for_write(
    relative_path: &str,
    workspace_root: &Path,
    rules: FolderRules,
) -> Result<PathBuf, String>;
```

Refusals (exact; the boundary sentence is unchanged and tests pin it):

| Case | Text |
|---|---|
| outside the root (R31, both) | `Path '{relative_path}' resolves outside the workspace boundary` |
| `.git` on write (R32) | `Writing '{relative_path}' is refused: it is inside the project's .git folder, which git keeps. Run git through shell_execute instead.` |
| `.openalpaca` read or write (R32, ST-9) | `'{relative_path}' is refused: a .openalpaca folder inside a project is an older OpenAlpaca's, and nothing in it is read or written any more.` |

Who passes what: S1 every existing caller passes `FolderRules::Plain`. S3: `file_read` and `send` pass
`if folder.is_project() { Project } else { Plain }`. S4a: `file_write`'s real write passes `Project`. S4b: `file_edit`
`Project`. S5: `file_list` as `file_read`.

**R33 (S3), all five rules from both file tools:** `file_read` loses `is_store_owned_path(.., Read)` and
`is_store_owned_resolved(.., Read)`; `file_write` loses the three persona checks, `is_store_owned_path(.., Write)`
and `is_store_owned_resolved(.., Write)`. Deleted with their last caller in S3: `is_store_owned_resolved`,
`is_soul_path`, `is_user_path`, `is_identity_path` and their tests (`helpers/tests.rs::test_is_soul_path_variants`).
`is_store_owned_path` and `StoreAccess` stay for `workspace_write`'s key check (`tools/builtins/mod.rs:183`).

### 3. R29 (the filter) and R45 (the kill) — S1

#### 3.1 R29: telling a first-party builtin from a program-reaching tool

`ToolBackend` alone cannot tell: skill scripts (`ScriptToolBuiltIn`) and nested `invoke_skill:<id>` adapters are
registered as `ToolBackend::BuiltIn` with `author: "skill:<id>"`, and `RegisteredTool::extension_id`'s doc forbids
deriving identity from `author` (a TOML command tool sets its own author, `tools/config/mod.rs:151`).

```rust
// tools/registry/mod.rs — BuiltInTool gains one provided method:
/// Whether this tool's arguments reach a shell line or another program, so
/// the sanitizer's `../` rule still applies to them (R29). `false` — every
/// first-party builtin, whose path arguments carry their own `..` refusal and
/// whose other arguments are content.
fn arguments_reach_a_program(&self) -> bool { false }

// ScriptToolBuiltIn (tools/builtins/mod.rs) overrides it: `true`
// (config/skills/create-skill/scripts/write_skill_md.sh builds a path from --id
// and relies on the filter).

impl ToolRegistry {
    /// R29: the `../` rule for `tool_name`. `Allow` only for a `BuiltIn`
    /// whose handler answers `arguments_reach_a_program() == false`; `Refuse`
    /// for `Command`, `Http`, `Plugin`, `Mcp`, a script, and a name not registered.
    pub fn traversal_rule(&self, tool_name: &str) -> TraversalRule;
}

// security/sanitizer/mod.rs
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum TraversalRule { Refuse, Allow }

impl InputSanitizer {
    /// `sanitize_tool_args` with the `../` check governed by `traversal`; the
    /// null-byte and shell-injection checks are unchanged.
    pub fn sanitize_tool_args_with(
        tool_name: &str,
        arguments: &serde_json::Value,
        allowed_tools: &[String],
        extra_shell_tools: &[String],
        traversal: TraversalRule,
    ) -> Result<(), SecurityViolation>;
    // `sanitize_tool_args` keeps its signature and delegates with
    // `TraversalRule::Refuse` — its 20 test call sites are untouched.
}
```

`SandboxManager::execute_tool` step 2 (`security/sandbox/mod.rs:253-263`) calls `sanitize_tool_args_with(..,
self.registry.traversal_rule(&tool_call.name))`. Consequence stated, not a conflict: `shell_execute` is a builtin, so
`../` in a command is allowed — the shell is a working directory, not a confinement (ST-14); `cd ..` without a slash
already passed. The injection checks for `shell_execute` and command tools are unchanged.

#### 3.2 R45: the shared kill helper

`crates/openalpaca_core/Cargo.toml` gains (S1; `libc` 0.2.180 is already in `Cargo.lock` through storage and the
daemon, so the lock does not change):

```toml
[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]
libc.workspace = true
```

`crates/openalpaca_core/src/tools/platform.rs`:

```rust
/// Why [`run_bounded`] produced no output.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum RunFailure {
    /// The program could not be started.
    Spawn(std::io::Error),
    /// `timeout` passed; the process (and its group, on unix) was killed.
    TimedOut,
    /// Reading its output or waiting for it failed.
    Io(std::io::Error),
}

/// Run `cmd` to its end with stdin null and stdout/stderr captured, and kill
/// it when `timeout` passes **or the returned future is dropped** (the
/// sandbox's per-tool timeout, a run cancelled mid-call — both drop the tool's
/// future, `runner/agentic_loop/mod.rs:1153-1167`).
///
/// unix: the child is started in a new process group (`process_group(0)`), and
/// a guard owning the `Child` sends `libc::killpg(pgid, SIGKILL)` on every exit
/// that is not a normal end — before it lets the `Child` drop — so the
/// processes the command started go too. A normal end disarms the guard, so a
/// group id that may be reused is never signalled. Windows: `kill_on_drop(true)`
/// kills the direct child only; processes it started survive ("where the
/// platform allows", R45).
pub async fn run_bounded(
    cmd: tokio::process::Command,
    timeout: std::time::Duration,
) -> Result<std::process::Output, RunFailure>;
```

The three call sites (S1), each keeping its own message text:

| Site | Today | After |
|---|---|---|
| `tools/builtins/shell_execute.rs` `ShellExecuteTool::execute` | `timeout(300s, shell_command(command).output())` | `run_bounded(shell_command(command), 300s)`; `TimedOut` → `Command timed out after 300s`, `Spawn`/`Io` → `Failed to execute command: {e}` |
| `tools/registry/mod.rs` `execute_command` | `timeout(.., shell_command(&full_command).output())` | `run_bounded(shell_command(&full_command), timeout)`; `Command timed out after {timeout_secs}s` / `Failed to execute command: {e}` |
| `tools/builtins/mod.rs` `ScriptToolBuiltIn::execute` | `timeout(.., cmd.output())` | `run_bounded(cmd, timeout)`; `Script timed out after {timeout_secs}s` / `Failed to execute script: {e}`; `current_dir(&self.skill_dir)` kept |

#### 3.3 The kill test pattern (S1; every later spawning test follows it)

`#[cfg(unix)]`. The command records its grandchild: `sh -c 'sleep 30 & echo $! > {pidfile}; wait'` in a tempdir.
Assert after the timeout (`run_bounded(.., 1s)` → `TimedOut`) or after dropping the future (spawn the call on a
`tokio::spawn`, wait for the pidfile, `abort()` the handle): poll up to 2 s until `libc::kill(pid, 0)` fails with
`ESRCH`. The test holds `struct KillOnFail(i32)` whose `Drop` sends `libc::kill(pid, SIGKILL)`, so a failed assertion
leaves no orphan.

### 4. The approval preview (S2, extended by S4a and S4b) and ST-15

#### 4.1 The hook (unchanged)

`BuiltInTool::confirmation_preview(&self, arguments, ctx) -> Result<Option<String>, String>`
(`tools/registry/mod.rs:308`): `Ok(Some(text))` rides the card as its preview, `Ok(None)` the ordinary card,
`Err(reason)` refuses the call with **no card**. The sandbox asks only when it is about to raise a card (not on a
cache hit, `auto_approve` or an unattended refusal — `sandbox/mod.rs:350-365`).

#### 4.2 The text module — new `crates/openalpaca_core/src/tools/builtins/approval_preview.rs` (S2)

```rust
/// Where a write lands, for its card (R34).
pub(super) enum WriteLanding<'a> {
    /// A real file in the project (S4a on). `replaces`: a file is there now.
    Project { root: &'a Path, replaces: bool },
    /// A by-product in `store`, the artifact store directory
    /// (`store_root(scope)?.join("artifacts")` — creates nothing).
    ByProduct { store: &'a Path },
    /// S2–S4a only: the plain write at a startup root that is not the home
    /// store (a daemon started by hand in a folder). Removed by S4a.
    StartupFolder { dir: &'a Path },
}

pub(super) fn command_card(folder: &WorkingFolder) -> String;                 // S2
pub(super) fn write_card(path: &str, landing: WriteLanding<'_>) -> String;     // S2
pub(super) fn edit_card(                                                        // S4b
    path: &str, root: &Path, first_line: usize, replacements: usize,
    old_string: &str, new_string: &str,
) -> String;
/// R49's per-string budget, in bytes of escaped text.
pub(super) const EDIT_PREVIEW_BYTES: usize = 1_000;                            // S4b
```

`EDIT_PREVIEW_BYTES = 1000`: two strings and the frame stay a card a person reads at a glance (~25 lines each), and the
full arguments are drawn below the preview anyway.

Texts (exact). `{path}` is `escape_hidden_line(path)`; folders print as they are (§1.3). Lines are joined with `\n`;
the GUI renders the preview `whitespace-pre-wrap`.

| Card | Text |
|---|---|
| shell, project | `Runs in the project folder {root}. The command itself can reach files outside it.` |
| shell, scratch | `Runs in this conversation's scratch folder {dir}. The command itself can reach files outside it.` |
| write, project, new | `Writes {path} in the project folder {root}.` |
| write, project, replaces | `Replaces {path} in the project folder {root}; its current content is kept in this conversation's log.` |
| write, by-product | `Saves {path} as a by-product in {store}, OpenAlpaca's artifact store — not in a folder of yours.` |
| write, startup folder (S2–S4a) | `Writes {path} in {dir}, the folder the daemon was started in.` |
| edit (S4b) | line 1 `Edits {path} in the project folder {root}: {n} replacement{s}, the first at line {line}. Its current content is kept in this conversation's log.`; line 2 `Replace:`; then `escape_hidden_within(old_string, EDIT_PREVIEW_BYTES).text`; then `cut_notice(left_out)` when `Some`; then `With:`; the same for `new_string`; then `hidden_notice(hidden of path + old + new)` when `Some` |
| any card whose `{path}` held a hidden character (shell/write) | the card's line, then `hidden_notice(count)` on its own line |

#### 4.3 Who implements which preview, and what it refuses

| Tool | Slice | `Ok(Some)` | `Err` (no card) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shell_execute` | S2 → S3 | `command_card(&folder)` from `working_folder(ctx)` | S2: never — any refusal → `Ok(None)`. S3: the refusal's sentence |
| `file_write` | S2 → S4a | S2: `write_card` with `ByProduct` (Round G's routing predicate `!Project \|\| is_the_home_root(root)`, `file_ops.rs:335`) or `StartupFolder`; S4a: `Project { replaces }` or `ByProduct { store: <home>/artifacts }` | S2: never. S4a: every refusal the body would give before writing (missing/not-a-project folder, R32, size limit, ST-17's cap, R46) — one shared `plan` function (§6.1) answers both |
| `file_edit` | S4b | `edit_card(..)` | every R47/R48 refusal, ST-17's cap, R46 — from the same plan as the body |
| `send` (R23) | S1 | `Sends {file} ({bytes} bytes) to {channel} recipient {recipient} as {filename}.` — `{file}` the resolved absolute path, `{channel}`, `{recipient}`, `{filename}` each `escape_hidden_line`, then `hidden_notice` | the file does not resolve, or the artifact id is not the turn owner's |

### 5. Pointer rows (S4a)

#### 5.1 Migration `004_project_files.sql` (registers 4)

```sql
-- Project files, version 4: a result file an agent writes into its project gets a pointer row (owner decision ST-12, design §13 R35) — the real file's address, no copy, no versions.
-- `in_project = 1` marks such a row: `project_root` is the project, `rel_path`
-- the file's path relative to it (an exact suffix of `storage_path`), `origin`
-- 'produced', `status` 'ready'. Every other row is 0. The unique address
-- index gains the column, so a pointer path equal to a by-product's or an
-- upload's address is a different row.

ALTER TABLE file_assets ADD COLUMN in_project INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_file_assets_addr;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_file_assets_addr ON file_assets(COALESCE(project_root, ''), in_project, rel_path) WHERE rel_path IS NOT NULL;

INSERT INTO schema_version(version) VALUES (4);
```

`migrations/mod.rs`: append `Migration { version: 4, name: "project_files", sql: include_str!("004_project_files.sql") }`
and change the comment above `MIGRATIONS` to "Future schema changes start at version 5: add `005_<name>.sql` ending in
`INSERT INTO schema_version(version) VALUES (5);`". Tests reading the newest version move by themselves
(`newest_version()`). One new test: a version-3 database migrates to 4 with every existing row `in_project = 0`.

#### 5.2 Which type carries it

`ArtifactRecord` (`artifacts/mod.rs:400`) gains `pub in_project: bool`; `RECORD_COLUMNS` (`:1719`) appends
`, in_project` (index 22) and `row_to_record` reads `row.get::<_, i64>(22)? != 0`; and

```rust
impl ArtifactRecord {
    /// ST-18: Open is offered — every by-product; a result file only when its
    /// name has an extension a kind keeps (`store::opens_in_default_app`).
    pub fn openable(&self) -> bool;
}
// store/artifact.rs, beside kind_for_file_name:
/// ST-18: `kind_for_file_name(name).is_some()`. `false` for `.sh`, `.command`,
/// `.svg`, `.exe`, and every name with no extension (`Makefile`, `.env`).
pub fn opens_in_default_app(name: &str) -> bool;
```

`FileAsset` gets **no** field (§10 C12): its readers are the upload writer and dedup (`origin = 'upload'`), the text
extractor (`status = 'uploaded'`), the orphan sweep (`origin = 'upload'`) and connector delivery (fed only by
`produced_for_task`, filtered below) — none can meet a pointer row. `GET /v1/files/{id}` is unchanged.

`ArtifactQuery` gains `pub in_project: Option<bool>` (`None` both; `list` adds `in_project = ?`).

#### 5.3 R35 — the method (storage) and its caller (core)

```rust
// crates/openalpaca_storage/src/artifacts/mod.rs; re-exported from lib.rs beside NewArtifact.
/// One result file an agent wrote into its project (ST-12, R35).
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct NewProjectFile<'a> {
    pub owner_id: &'a str,
    /// The project's canonical root (`store::project_root_of`'s string).
    pub project_root: &'a str,
    /// The file relative to `project_root`, `/`-separated — `store::relative_to`
    /// of the **resolved** path, so a write through a link inside the root
    /// records where it landed.
    pub rel_path: &'a str,
    /// The bytes now in the file; hashed here, before the connection is taken.
    pub content: &'a [u8],
    pub task_id: Option<&'a str>,
    pub agent_id: Option<&'a str>,
}

impl ArtifactStore<'_> {
    /// R35: insert or update the row keyed on (project_root, in_project = 1,
    /// rel_path), in one transaction: SELECT the id at that key; an existing
    /// row of another owner → `bail!` ("… belongs to another owner"); else
    /// UPDATE sha256, size_bytes, storage_path, filename, kind, mime_type,
    /// task_id, agent_id, metadata_json (the head stamp), origin = 'produced',
    /// status = 'ready', missing_since = NULL, updated_at; or INSERT with
    /// version = 1, version_count = 0, pinned = 0. Never calls `put`, writes no
    /// `artifact_versions` row, touches no file. Returns the row and `true`
    /// when it inserted.
    pub fn record_project_file(&self, file: NewProjectFile<'_>) -> Result<(ArtifactRecord, bool)>;
}
```

Row values: `filename` = `rel_path`; `storage_path` = `Path::new(project_root).join(rel_path)` as a string;
`kind` = `kind_for_file_name(rel_path).unwrap_or(ArtifactKind::Code)` (Round G's rule); `mime_type` = the kind's
`default_mime`; `summary` NULL.

Core wrapper, `crates/openalpaca_core/src/tools/builtins/artifact_write.rs`, beside `put_tool_artifact` (S4a):

```rust
/// R35 for a tool: the owner (`ctx.owner_id`, else the task's `created_by`),
/// `record_project_file`, then `announce_artifact_written` — storage has no
/// bus, so the announcement is the caller's, as for `put` (§10 C5).
pub(super) fn record_tool_project_file(
    db: &Database,
    ctx: &ToolContext,
    project_root: &Path,   // the WorkingFolder::Project root (canonical)
    resolved: &Path,       // the file as the write resolver returned it
    content: &str,
) -> Result<ArtifactRecord, String>;
```

`SystemEvent::ArtifactWritten` (`crates/openalpaca_core/src/events.rs:488`) and `ServerEvent::ArtifactWritten`
(`crates/openalpaca_api/src/events/mod.rs:367`) gain, after `path`:

```rust
// ServerEvent (both derive Serialize + Deserialize) and on the CLI mirror (`tail.rs`):

#[serde(default)]
in_project: bool,
/// A frame from an older daemon carries neither field and is a by-product.
/// ST-18: whether Open is offered for it (`ArtifactRecord::openable`).
#[serde(default = "openable_by_default")]

// fn openable_by_default() -> bool { true }   — private, beside each enum
```

Every arm updated in the same commit: `announce_artifact_written` (`artifact_write.rs:86`), `announce_user_edit`
(`apps/openalpacad/src/routes/artifacts.rs:415`), the bridge arm (`event_bridge.rs:567`), `EventBroadcaster::artifact_written`
(`events/handlers.rs:46`, two parameters more), the persistence arm (`events/persistence.rs:459`, `detail` gains both),
the CLI mirror (`apps/openalpaca/src/commands/tail.rs:29`, `#[serde(default)]`, its line says `in the project` for a
pointer row). The GUI mirror is S6a's (§5.8).

#### 5.5 The `in_project = 0` filters and R37 (S4a)

| Reader | Where | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `put`'s identity scan | `dir_rows` (`artifacts/mod.rs:2131`) | `AND in_project = 0` |
| `put`'s name reservation | `rel_path_is_referenced` (`:2269`) | both arms `AND … in_project = 0` |
| the sweep | `verify` (`:1655`) | `AND in_project = 0` |
| the hand-edit probe | `probe_for` (`:1877`) | a pointer row is never a version: `check_head` branches before it (below) |
| run counts / chips / delivery (R38) | `FileAssetRepository::produced_for_task`, `produced_ids_for_task`, `produced_counts_for_tasks` (`repository/file_asset/mod.rs:325`, `:350`) | `AND in_project = 0` |
| ST-19's delete | `project_life/delete.rs`: `kept_rows` (`:238`), the plan's `kept.artifacts` (`:161`) and `counts.artifacts` (`:190`) | `AND in_project = 0` — a pointer row is never kept (copied to the root store) and never counted as a by-product; step 2's `DELETE … WHERE project_root = ?1` takes its row, never its file (§10 C13) |
| upload dedup, orphan sweep, extractor | `uploads/mod.rs::load_by_sha256`, `FileAssetRepository::list_orphaned`, `list_by_status` | none: `origin = 'upload'` / `status = 'uploaded'` already exclude a pointer row |
| re-point | `repoint_rows` (`:1483`) | none: Stage 1 built the second prefix for these rows |

R37, in `ArtifactStore`:

- `check_head(id)` keeps its signature. For a row with `in_project`, it does not call `probe_for`; it runs the private
  `refresh_project_file`: stat the file at `storage_path` (via `resolve_version_path`); when the stamp differs, hash
  off the lock and, under it, compare-and-set `sha256`, `size_bytes`, the stamp — **no version, no rotation** — and
  answer `Ok(None)`.
- `resolve_version_path` for a pointer row: root = `PathBuf::from(project_root)`, path =
  `confine_to_root(&root, &root.join(rel_path))` — the storage-side resolver of R31 (it canonicalizes an existing
  path whole, the last component included; §10 C9); a found file clears `missing_since`; a version other than the
  head is `VersionNotFound` (there are none); an absent file stamps `missing_since` and is `Gone`, as for a head.
- `versions(id)` answers `[]` and `diff_paths` `VersionNotFound` for a pointer row with no change of code.

#### 5.6 R36 and `file_write`'s real-write result (S4a)

Result strings (exact):

| Case | Text |
|---|---|
| new file | `Wrote {path} in the project ({bytes} bytes), at {abs}. It is listed in the Library with the project's results. Tell the user the file is at that path. To change it, call file_write with "{path}" again.` |
| replaced | `Replaced {path} in the project ({bytes} bytes), at {abs}; its previous content is kept in this conversation's log. It is listed in the Library with the project's results. Tell the user the file is at that path. To change it, call file_write with "{path}" again.` |
| R36 (the row failed) | the sentence above with `It is listed in the Library with the project's results.` replaced by `The file is written, but the app could not list it ({e}).` |

The functions are named apart so one slice owns each: `FileWriteTool::project_write_result(..)` (S4a) and
`FileWriteTool::save_as_artifact(..)` (Round G's, §8.3).

#### 5.7 The wire (S4a daemon; S6a mirrors)

`GET /v1/artifacts` and `GET /v1/artifacts/{id}` (`artifact_json`, `routes/artifacts.rs:182`) gain
`"in_project": bool` and `"openable": bool`. `ListArtifactsParams` (`:55`) gains `pub in_project: Option<bool>`
(absent = both), copied to `ArtifactQuery::in_project`. `POST /v1/files/{id}/open` (`routes/files_types.rs`,
`open_asset_for_user`) refuses a row whose `openable()` is false: `OpenFileApiError::NotOffered { name }` →
`409 OPEN_NOT_OFFERED`, message `{name} is not a kind of file OpenAlpaca opens in another app; show it in its folder
instead (Reveal in Finder, or Show in folder).` A pointer row is opened unstaged (as every produced row is). The
content route (`artifact_content`, `routes/artifacts.rs:406`) passes a pointer row's **base name**
(`Path::new(&record.name).file_name()`) to `content_response` rather than `src/main.rs`, so the
`Content-Disposition` filename carries no `/`.

### 6. The pre-edit copy (S4a creates; S4b consumes)

#### 6.1 API — new `crates/openalpaca_core/src/tools/builtins/pre_edit.rs`

Moved out of `FileWriteTool::snapshot_before_overwrite` / `is_snapshotable` / `store_root` (`file_ops.rs:146-237`).

```rust
/// Which verb a refusal names.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum EditVerb { Overwrite, Edit }

/// What the copy step found.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum PreEdit {
    /// Nothing stands at the target, or it is not a regular file: nothing to keep.
    NewFile,
    /// The current bytes are in `sessions/<session>/snapshots/`, committed by a
    /// `file_snapshot` record, before the caller writes.
    Kept,
}

/// Whether a write of `target` may go ahead without losing bytes, without
/// writing anything (the previews' half): `Ok(true)` a file is there and will
/// be replaced, `Ok(false)` a new file; `Err` R46 or ST-17's cap.
pub(super) fn check_pre_edit(
    path: &str, target: &Path, ctx: &ToolContext, snapshot_max_bytes: u64, verb: EditVerb,
) -> Result<bool, String>;

/// ST-17 + R46 (the body's half): `check_pre_edit`, then the copy. `target`
/// is the resolved path under `project_root`; a target outside it, or inside
/// the home store, is never copied (a project never overlaps the home store,
/// R13). Fail closed: `Err` means the caller must not write.
pub(super) async fn keep_pre_edit_copy(
    path: &str, target: &Path, project_root: &Path, ctx: &ToolContext,
    snapshot_max_bytes: u64, verb: EditVerb,
) -> Result<PreEdit, String>;
```

`snapshot_max_bytes` is `[orchestrator.sessions] snapshot_max_bytes` read from the tool's `daemon_config` (default 10
MiB, `SessionsConfig::default()`), as today.

#### 6.2 Refusals (exact; `{verb}` = `overwrite` | `edit`)

| Case | Text |
|---|---|
| ST-17 cap | `Refusing to {verb} '{path}': it is {n} bytes, above the {cap} byte [orchestrator.sessions] snapshot_max_bytes limit, so no pre-edit snapshot can be kept for it. The file is unchanged. Raise snapshot_max_bytes, or copy the file aside yourself first.` (today's text for `overwrite`) |
| ST-17 copy failed | `Refusing to {verb} '{path}': its pre-edit snapshot could not be taken ({e}). The file is unchanged.` (today's) |
| R46 no session log, file exists | `Refusing to {verb} '{path}': it already exists, and no copy of its current content can be kept here — a skill or a plugin agent keeps no conversation log. The file is unchanged. Write the result to a new file, or ask for the change in the conversation itself.` |

R46's discriminator is `ctx.session_log.is_none()` (the copy needs the log's emit side; `conversation_id` is not it).

### 7. The new tools

#### 7.1 `file_edit` (S4b)

`crates/openalpaca_core/src/tools/builtins/file_ops.rs` (beside `file_write`), registered by `builtin_tools`.

```rust
pub(super) fn file_edit_tool(
    db: Option<Database>,
    daemon_config: Option<Arc<ArcSwap<DaemonConfig>>>,
) -> RegisteredTool;
```

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| name | `file_edit` |
| schema | `{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"string","description":"The file, relative to the project folder (e.g. 'src/main.rs'). It must exist."},"old_string":{"type":"string","description":"The exact text to find, whitespace and line breaks included. It must occur exactly once, unless replace_all is true."},"new_string":{"type":"string","description":"The text to put in its place. It must differ from old_string."},"replace_all":{"type":"boolean","description":"Replace every occurrence instead of exactly one. Default false."}},"required":["path","old_string","new_string"]}` |
| strict | `None` — `replace_all` is optional with a default, and a strict schema would have every key required (§7.4) |
| annotations | `destructive_local_annotations()` (asks like `file_write`, R49) |
| `provides_capabilities` | `vec!["file_write".into(), "file_edit".into()]` (R48: comes with `file_write`) |
| description | `Change part of one file in the project: give the exact text to find (old_string) and the text to put in its place (new_string), instead of writing the whole file back. old_string must occur exactly once unless replace_all is true. The rest of the file is kept byte for byte, line endings included. Its current content is kept in the conversation's log first. In a project only — to create a file, or with no project, use file_write.` |

Refusals (exact):

| Case | Text |
|---|---|
| no project (R48) | `file_edit changes a file in a project, and this conversation has no project. Use file_write to save a file instead.` |
| no context / missing / not a project | the `WorkingFolderRefusal` sentence |
| missing file | `'{path}' does not exist in the project. file_edit changes an existing file; use file_write to create it.` |
| a folder | `'{path}' is a folder, not a file.` |
| not UTF-8 | `'{path}' is not UTF-8 text, so file_edit cannot change it.` |
| empty `old_string` | `old_string is empty. Give the exact text to replace; to create a file, use file_write.` |
| identical | `old_string and new_string are the same, so there is nothing to change.` |
| not found | `old_string was not found in '{path}'. Read the file with file_read and copy the exact text, whitespace and line breaks included.` |
| several, no `replace_all` | `old_string occurs {n} times in '{path}'. Give more of the surrounding text so it occurs once, or set replace_all to true to change every one.` |
| R32, ST-17, R46 | §2, §6.2 with `{verb}` = `edit` |

Matching: exact substring over the file's text. **CRLF:** when the file holds `\r\n` and `old_string` holds `\n` but no
`\r\n`, the match is retried with `\n` → `\r\n` in both strings — a model writes LF, and the replacement then keeps the
file's endings (R47's "line endings included"). `first line` = 1 + the number of `\n` before the first match.

Result: `Edited {path} in the project: {n} replacement{s}, the first at line {line}; {bytes} bytes at {abs}. Its
previous content is kept in this conversation's log.` — R36's variant appends `The file is written, but the app could
not list it ({e}).`

Order of work (R47): resolve (`FolderRules::Project`) → read + match (refusals) → `keep_pre_edit_copy(.., Edit)` →
write → `record_tool_project_file`.

#### 7.2 `file_list` (S5)

```rust
pub(super) fn file_list_tool() -> RegisteredTool;   // tools/builtins/file_ops.rs, registered by builtin_tools
```

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| schema | `{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"string","description":"The folder to list, relative to the working folder; '.' is the working folder itself."}},"required":["path"],"additionalProperties":false}` |
| strict | `Some(true)` — closed and fully required, so `strict_mode_compatible` accepts it |
| annotations | `read_only_annotations()` (never asks, ST-16) |
| `provides_capabilities` | `vec!["file_read".into(), "file_list".into()]` (R42: comes with `file_read`) |
| description | `List one folder under the working folder (the project, or this conversation's scratch folder): its files with their sizes, its folders marked with a trailing /, links with @. Not recursive — list a subfolder to go deeper. Read a file with file_read.` |

Resolution: `working_folder(ctx)?.ensure()?`, then `resolve_workspace_path(path, root, rules)`; not a directory →
`'{path}' is a file, not a folder; read it with file_read.` Output (exact shape):

```text
{path} ({abs}): {n} entries
src/
Cargo.toml  1234 bytes
link@
```

Entries sorted by name (byte order), dotfiles included, at most 500; past that, a last line `... and {k} more entries
not shown — list a subfolder`. Names are `to_string_lossy` and unescaped (a tool result, not an approval surface).

#### 7.3 `artifact_read` (S5)

```rust
pub(super) fn artifact_read_tool(db: Option<Database>) -> RegisteredTool;  // new tools/builtins/artifact_read.rs
```

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| schema | `{"type":"object","properties":{"artifact_id":{"type":"string","description":"The id of a by-product, as artifact_write's result, a workspace entry's file_asset_id or task_status names it."},"offset":{"type":"integer","description":"Byte offset to start from. Defaults to 0; a partial page tells you the next offset."},"limit":{"type":"integer","description":"Maximum bytes to return. Defaults to 8192, capped at 65536."}},"required":["artifact_id"]}` |
| strict | `None` (optional `offset`/`limit`, as `read_result`) |
| annotations | `read_only_annotations()` |
| `provides_capabilities` | `vec!["read_result".into(), "artifact_read".into()]` (R42: comes with `read_result`) |
| description | `Read a by-product back by its id: a draft, a hand-off or another file saved with artifact_write (or with file_write when there is no project). Pages like read_result. A file written into the project is not a by-product — read it with file_read.` |

Scope: the turn's owner (`ctx.owner_id`, required), and a by-product of the turn's project or of no project
(`record.project_root` equal to `store::project_root_of(&scope_from_context(ctx))`, or `None`). Reads through
`ArtifactStore::resolve_content(id, None)` on `spawn_blocking`, then `read_result::read_page_bytes` (already
`pub(super)`) and `page_bounds` (made `pub(super)` by S5). Footer: `[artifact_read: bytes {a}–{b} of {n} from {name}, version {v}; next
offset={b}]` (the `next offset` part only when more remains).

Refusals: `artifact_read: no artifact '{id}' of yours.` / `artifact_read: '{id}' is a file in the project
({rel_path}); read it with file_read.` / `artifact_read: '{id}' belongs to another project ({root}); read it from a
conversation in that project.` / `artifact_read: the bytes of '{id}' are gone ({path}).` / `artifact_read: '{id}' is a
{kind} artifact; artifact_read returns text only.` (kinds `image`, `binary`) / `artifact_read cannot read this turn's
artifacts: it has no owner.`

| Surface | `file_read` | `file_list` | `file_write` | `file_edit` | `artifact_read` | `shell_execute` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Main loop, `core_union` | by keyword (today); **always on a project turn** (S5, `main_loop_tool_set`, `ctx.request_workspace_root.is_some()`) | always on a project turn (S5, same) | by keyword (today) | **beside `file_write` on a project turn** (S4b, `simple_query_handler.rs` right after `suggest_tools`: `if tool_names` holds `file_write` and `scope_ctx.request_workspace_root.is_some()`, push `file_edit`) | **every turn** with a database (S5, `main_loop_tool_set`, as `read_result`'s definition is added) | by keyword (today) |
| Main loop, `full` | every globally registered tool, as today | | | | | |
| Lead (hand-built, `runner/lead_agent/mod.rs`) | in code (S5) | in code (S5) | never | never | in code (S5) | never |
| Subagents | by template: `file_list` with `file_read`, `file_edit` with `file_write`, `artifact_read` with `read_result` (`resolve_capabilities`, no code change); `writing_agent` gains `file_read` in `config/agents/writing_agent.md` (S5) | | | | | |

*The main-loop rows of this table are superseded by R-T6 and R-T14 (S4b.4, S5.6): one `is_project_turn` computed in
`simple_query_handler.rs`; `offer_file_readers` adds `file_read` on a project turn and `file_list` wherever `file_read`
is; `main_loop_tool_set` adds only `artifact_read` — see the settled table below.*

Capability denial is by tool **name** in the sandbox (`check_agent_capability`); a template denying `file_write` keeps

### 9. Choices this sheet made where the spec is open

- `conversation_id` is a new field, not `session_id` (§10 C3).
- `working_folder` is pure; `ensure()` creates the scratch folder, so the card and the R28 note create nothing.
- R32's `.git` rule refuses writes only; reading `.git` stays allowed (ST-16).
- The pointer row's `version_count` is `0` (no `artifact_versions` row), `version` `1` (NOT NULL default).
- `openable` is computed by the daemon and carried on the wire and the frame, so the app needs no copy of R21's
  extension table.
- `EDIT_PREVIEW_BYTES` 1,000; `file_list` caps at 500 entries; `project_files_note` names at most 20 paths.
- `file_list` is strict (closed, one required key); `file_edit` and `artifact_read` are not (optional parameters).
- `file_edit` retries an LF `old_string` against a CRLF file (§7.1).
- The lead gets `file_read`, `file_list`, `artifact_read` unconditionally in code (R42 "in code"), not per template.
- The connector prompts get the preview (§10 C6).
- A conversation cleared (not deleted) keeps its scratch folder.

### 10. Spec conflicts

- **C1 — R26 moves `file_write`'s root in step (3); it moves in S4a.** §16 says "until (4) lands, `file_write` on a
  project turn stays a by-product". Moving its root in S3 would mean routing every project write to the artifact store
  for one slice and taking §5.7's twelve snapshot tests off the plain write they exercise, only for S4a to bring them
  back. Correction: `FileWriteTool.workspace_root`, its `is_the_home_root` use and `builtin_tools`'s `workspace_root`
  parameter go in S4a with the real write; in production (startup root = the home store) the S3→S4a window is exactly
  §16's "stays a by-product". `is_the_home_root` (`store/mod.rs:478`) is removed in S4a with its last caller.
- **C2 — the lead's list puts ST-17 and R46 in S4b; they land in S4a.** S4a removes the startup root the copy tier
  judges against (`file_ops.rs:170`), so it must re-point the tier, and S4a's real write would otherwise replace a
  project file from the skill tier with no copy kept. S4a creates `pre_edit.rs` (§6) and S4b only consumes it.
- **C3 — R44 says "puts the turn's session id on the context".** `ToolContext.session_id`'s `Some` means "the session
  writer indexes this call": the sandbox forwards it on `ToolExecuted` into `tool_execution_log.session_id`
  (`events/persistence.rs:609`), `read_result` scopes spills by it, and the agentic loop overwrites it from its log
  handle (`agentic_loop/mod.rs:1095`). Correction: a new field, `conversation_id` (§1.1).
- **C4 — R28 names `prompt_ctx/sources/workspace.rs` as the stub to fill.** `ContextRequest` carries a
  `MemoryScopeContext` and no conversation id, and neither the lead's nor a subagent's prompt is built through the
  context manager. Correction: `working_folder_note(ctx)` inserted as a `ChatMessage::user` before the turn's last
  message at the four sites (main loop beside the relay rules, `simple_query_handler.rs` ~:740; the file-skill tier
  beside its memory insert, `invocation.rs`; the lead after its objective, `runner/lead_agent/mod.rs`; the subagent
  beside its memory insert, `runner/lead_agent/tools.rs` ~:549). `WorkspaceSource` stays the stub it is.
- **C5 — R35 "announces `artifact_written`".** Storage has no bus; the core wrapper announces (§5.3), as `put`'s callers
  do.
- **C6 — ST-14 / R34 "the card names the folder".** Connector prompts (`format_confirmation_prompt`) never carried the
  preview, so on a connector lane — a scratch conversation — a shell card would not name its folder. Correction: §4.5.
- **C7 — R41 "Round G's `read_back_path` and its pinned test go" with `artifact_read` (S5).** S3 moves `file_read`'s
  root, after which the path `read_back_path` names no longer opens; S3 removes it and pins the fixed sentence, S5
  adds the `artifact_read` sentence (§8.3).
- **C8 — the S2→S3 window** (§1.4): recorded, unreleased, closed by S3.
- **C9 — R37 "the resolver of R31".** Core's resolver cannot be called from storage; storage's `confine_to_root`
  canonicalizes an existing path whole, which is R31's rule, and is what `resolve_version_path` uses for a pointer row.
- **C10 — R38 "listed as written in the project".** A pointer row is never linked to the report message: ST-19's delete
  keeps (copies to the root store) a file a surviving message links, which for a pointer row would copy the user's
  real file. The list is the report's runtime line (§5.9) and the Work view's split (S6a).
- **C11 — ST-18 is under *Surfaces* (S6a).** The daemon's Open would hand a `.command` or `.sh` result file to the
  system's default app from S4a's first commit; the refusal lands with the rows in S4a, the app's hiding in S6a.
- **C12 — the lead asked for "the FileAsset model field".** `FileAsset` needs none (§5.2); `ArtifactRecord` carries it.
- **C13 — ST-19's delete is not in §13's filter list.** Its kept-file step must skip pointer rows (§5.5), or "Deleting a
  project's data leaves its real files" (R39) fails by copying them.

## Stage 2 — slice S1: confinement, the filter and the kill

Read at `d484a56a` (`feat/markdown-memory`). Spec: `spec-stage2.md` (design rev 0.9) §11, §16 Stage 2 step (1);
contract: `interfaces.md` §0, §2, §3, §4.3 (the `send` row), §8.2 (S1's flipped tests). Line numbers below are from
`d484a56a` and only help you find the place — **locate every edit by the content quoted**.

### What this slice does

S1 lands the guards before anything moves (design §16, Stage 2 step (1)). **R32** gives both path resolvers in
`tools/builtins/helpers/mod.rs` a third parameter, `FolderRules`; its `Project` arm refuses a `.git` component for
writing and a `.openalpaca` component for reading and writing, compared without case on the path relative to the
canonical root after resolution. The rule is built and tested directly, and **no caller passes `Project` yet**: every
existing caller passes `Plain`, S3 switches it on for reads and S4a for writes (interfaces §2). **R31** makes the write
resolver resolve the last component too, so a `file_write` through a link that leaves the root is refused, and the test
that pinned the hole (`a_symlink_out_of_the_workspace_is_not_imaged`) flips. **R23** confines `send`: a `file_path` is
resolved the way `file_read` resolves one, under the same startup root (S3 moves both to the working folder), with
`file_read`'s two `state/` refusals; or the call names an `artifact_id` of the turn's owner. The approval card names the
resolved file. **R29** narrows the sanitizer's `../` rule to tools whose arguments reach a shell line or another
program: skill scripts and command, HTTP, MCP and plugin tools. First-party builtins may carry `../` in content. That
includes `shell_execute` (ST-14: the shell is a working directory, not a confinement) and the nested `invoke_skill:*`
adapters, whose query goes to a nested model loop that sanitizes its own calls. R29 lands after R23, so when the filter
stops covering a builtin, every builtin path argument already has its own `..` refusal. **R45** adds
`tools::platform::run_bounded`. A shell command, a command tool or a skill script that times out, or whose call is
dropped (the sandbox's per-tool timeout, or a run that is cancelled), is killed together with its process group on
unix.

**Not in S1: R33.** The five home-store rules (`state/`, `.history/`, `MEMORY.md`, `memory/.gitignore`, the persona
names) stay on `file_read` and `file_write`. `send` gets the two `state/` read checks here. All of them go in S3, after
the root has moved. Removing them now would let `file_read`, and from this slice `send`, reach `state/`
(`discovery.json`, the database, `.master_key`) from an app-launched daemon, because both launchers start the daemon in
the home store and that is the tools' startup root (`apps/openalpacad/src/services/tools.rs`,
`let workspace_root = std::env::current_dir().ok();`).

Nothing in S1 changes a route, a refusal code, a migration, a storage `lib.rs` re-export or a GUI export. The only
crate touched is `openalpaca_core`, plus `Cargo.lock`, which gains one line in S1.9.

```rust
// --- R32: a project's .git and .openalpaca (storage design §11, ST-9) ---

/// A project folder with a `.git`, an older OpenAlpaca's `.openalpaca` and
/// some source in it.
fn project_folder() -> (tempfile::TempDir, PathBuf) {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.path().join(".git/hooks")).unwrap();
    std::fs::write(dir.path().join(".git/config"), "[core]\n").unwrap();
    std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.path().join(".openalpaca/memory")).unwrap();
    std::fs::write(dir.path().join(".openalpaca/memory/note.md"), "old\n").unwrap();
    std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.path().join("src")).unwrap();
    std::fs::write(dir.path().join("src/main.rs"), "fn main() {}\n").unwrap();
    let canonical = dir.path().canonicalize().unwrap();
    (dir, canonical)
}

#[test]
fn in_a_project_the_git_folder_is_refused_for_writing_and_read_freely() {
    let (dir, root) = project_folder();
    assert_eq!(
        resolve_workspace_path_for_write(".git/hooks/pre-commit", dir.path(), FolderRules::Project)
            .unwrap_err(),
        "Writing '.git/hooks/pre-commit' is refused: it is inside the project's .git folder, \
         which git keeps. Run git through shell_execute instead."
    );
    resolve_workspace_path_for_write(".git/new/deeper/x", dir.path(), FolderRules::Project)
        .expect_err("a new directory under .git is refused too");
    resolve_workspace_path_for_write(".git", dir.path(), FolderRules::Project)
        .expect_err("and the folder's own name");
    assert_eq!(
        resolve_workspace_path(".git/config", dir.path(), FolderRules::Project).unwrap(),
        root.join(".git/config"),
        "reading .git stays allowed (ST-16)"
    );
}
```

```rust
/// What R32 adds to confinement (storage design §11): the rules a folder
/// carries beyond "relative, no `..`, resolved under the root".
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum FolderRules {
    /// The folder is a project (ST-10): a component named `.git` is refused
    /// for writing — git keeps that folder, and reading it stays allowed
    /// (ST-16) — and one named `.openalpaca` for reading and for writing, an
    /// older OpenAlpaca's folder nothing reads any more (ST-9). Any
    /// component, compared without case, of the path relative to the
    /// canonical root **after** resolution, so a link into either folder is
    /// judged by where it lands.
    // Built in Stage 2's S1 and passed by no caller until S3 (reads) and
    // S4a (writes); S3 removes this attribute with the first caller.
    #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
    Project,
    /// No rule beyond confinement: a conversation's scratch folder, and until
    /// S3 and S4a every caller whose root is the daemon's starting directory.
    Plain,
}

impl FolderRules {
    /// R32 over `resolved`, the path a resolver landed on. The resolvers
    /// refused anything outside `canonical_root` first, so the fallback below
    /// only keeps this fail-closed.
    fn check(
        self,
        relative_path: &str,
        resolved: &Path,
        canonical_root: &Path,
        access: StoreAccess,
    ) -> Result<(), String> {
        if self == FolderRules::Plain {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let Ok(inside) = resolved.strip_prefix(canonical_root) else {
            return Err(format!(
                "Path '{relative_path}' resolves outside the workspace boundary"
            ));
        };
        let has = |name: &str| {
            inside.components().any(|component| {
                matches!(
                    component,
                    std::path::Component::Normal(part) if part.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name)
                )
            })
        };
        if has(".openalpaca") {
            return Err(format!(
                "'{relative_path}' is refused: a .openalpaca folder inside a project is an older \
                 OpenAlpaca's, and nothing in it is read or written any more."
            ));
        }
        if access == StoreAccess::Write && has(".git") {
            return Err(format!(
                "Writing '{relative_path}' is refused: it is inside the project's .git folder, \
                 which git keeps. Run git through shell_execute instead."
            ));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

```rust
/// Resolve a relative path within the workspace and verify it doesn't escape
/// the workspace boundary via symlinks or normalization.
///
/// `workspace_root` is the explicit workspace directory (captured once at
/// startup). This avoids depending on the process-global `current_dir()`,
/// which can change or be unavailable.
///
/// Returns the canonicalized absolute path on success — every component, the
/// last included, resolved (R31's read side) — after R32's read rule when
/// `rules` is [`FolderRules::Project`].
pub(super) fn resolve_workspace_path(
    relative_path: &str,
    workspace_root: &Path,
    rules: FolderRules,
) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    validate_workspace_path(relative_path)?;

    let full_path = workspace_root.join(relative_path);

    // Canonicalize to resolve symlinks. For reads the file must exist;
    // for writes the parent must exist (caller handles dir creation).
    let canonical = full_path
        .canonicalize()
        .map_err(|e| format!("Path resolution failed for '{}': {}", relative_path, e))?;

    let canonical_root = workspace_root
        .canonicalize()
        .map_err(|e| format!("Workspace root canonicalization failed: {}", e))?;

    if !canonical.starts_with(&canonical_root) {
        return Err(format!(
            "Path '{}' resolves outside the workspace boundary",
            relative_path
        ));
    }
    rules.check(relative_path, &canonical, &canonical_root, StoreAccess::Read)?;

    Ok(canonical)
}
```

```rust
/// Like `resolve_workspace_path` but for write targets where the file, and
/// any of the directories above it, may not exist yet (the caller creates
/// them).
///
/// Resolves the **nearest existing ancestor** of the parent directory — the
/// parent itself when it exists — and re-appends the missing directories and
/// the file name, so the path returned is where `create_dir_all` and the
/// write will actually land. A link on the way is therefore followed here,
/// not only later by the caller: `link -> state` plus `link/newdir/x.json`
/// resolves to `<root>/state/newdir/x.json`, which the boundary check below
/// and the caller's store check (`is_store_owned_resolved`) both see, and
/// `link -> /anywhere` plus a new directory resolves outside the root and is
/// refused (S3-R1, plan §7a). The missing directories cannot redirect
/// anything: they do not exist, and `validate_workspace_path` refused `..`.
///
/// "Exists" means a directory entry is there — `symlink_metadata`, not
/// `exists`, which answers no for a dangling link and would let the walk
/// step past it; a dangling link then fails to canonicalize and the write
/// is refused. The leaf is resolved the same way (R31, storage design §11):
/// an entry already standing there — a file, a folder, a link — is
/// canonicalized whole and must stay under the root, as
/// [`resolve_workspace_path`] does for a read, so a link at the leaf that
/// leaves the root is refused instead of written through, and the path
/// returned for a link inside the root is its target. Then R32's write rule
/// when `rules` is [`FolderRules::Project`].
```
