```rust
use super::ConnectorSendLock;
use super::annotations_for_builtin;
use super::helpers::{
    FolderRules, StoreAccess, is_store_owned_path, is_store_owned_resolved, resolve_workspace_path,
};
use crate::tools::registry::{BuiltInTool, RegisteredTool, ToolBackend};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use openalpaca_llm::ToolDefinition;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;

struct SendTool {
    provider: ConnectorSendLock,
    /// The folder a relative `file_path` is resolved under (R23, storage
    /// design §11): the file tools' root, the daemon's starting directory,
    /// until S3 moves both to the turn's working folder.
    workspace_root: PathBuf,
}

impl SendTool {
    fn acquire_provider(
        &self,
    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn crate::orchestrator::ConnectorSendProvider>, String> {
        let guard = self
            .provider
            .read()
            .map_err(|_| "Failed to read connector send provider".to_string())?;
        guard.clone().ok_or_else(|| {
            "No connector send provider configured. External messaging is not available.".to_string()
        })
    }

    /// R23: the absolute path of the file `file_path` names, resolved as
    /// `file_read` resolves one — relative, no `..`, every component (the
    /// last included) canonicalized and under the root — and refused, before
    /// and after resolution, inside the store's `state/`, as `file_read`
    /// refuses it until S3 takes both tools' store rules away with the root
    /// (R33). This path, not the argument, is what the connector is handed.
    fn resolve(&self, file_path: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
        let refuse = |what: &str| {
            format!(
                "Sending '{file_path}' is refused: it is inside {what}, which belongs to the \
                 daemon's own state/ and is not workspace content."
            )
        };
        if let Some(what) = is_store_owned_path(file_path, StoreAccess::Read) {
            return Err(refuse(what));
        }
        let resolved = resolve_workspace_path(file_path, &self.workspace_root, FolderRules::Plain)?;
        if let Some(what) =
            is_store_owned_resolved(&resolved, &self.workspace_root, StoreAccess::Read)
        {
            return Err(refuse(what));
        }
        let metadata = std::fs::metadata(&resolved)
            .map_err(|e| format!("Cannot access file '{file_path}': {e}"))?;
        if !metadata.is_file() {
            return Err(format!("'{file_path}' is not a file."));
        }
        resolved.into_os_string().into_string().map_err(|_| {
            format!(
                "'{file_path}' resolves to a path that is not UTF-8 text, which no channel can send."
            )
        })
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl BuiltInTool for SendTool {
    async fn execute(&self, arguments: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<String, String> {
        let action = arguments
            .get("action")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
            .ok_or_else(|| "Missing required parameter: action".to_string())?;

        let channel = arguments
            .get("channel")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
            .ok_or_else(|| "Missing required parameter: channel".to_string())?;

        let recipient = arguments
            .get("recipient")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
            .ok_or_else(|| "Missing required parameter: recipient".to_string())?;

        // Validate action-specific parameters before acquiring the provider.
        match action {
            "message" => {
                let content = arguments
                    .get("content")
                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                    .ok_or_else(|| {
                        "Missing required parameter: content (required for action=\"message\")"
                            .to_string()
                    })?;

                let provider = self.acquire_provider()?;
                provider.send_message(channel, recipient, content).await
            }
            "file" => {
                let file_path = arguments
                    .get("file_path")
                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                    .ok_or_else(|| {
                        "Missing required parameter: file_path (required for action=\"file\")"
                            .to_string()
                    })?;
                let filename = arguments
                    .get("filename")
                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                    .ok_or_else(|| {
                        "Missing required parameter: filename (required for action=\"file\")"
                            .to_string()
                    })?;
                let mime_type = arguments
                    .get("mime_type")
                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                    .unwrap_or("application/octet-stream");
                let caption = arguments
                    .get("caption")
                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                    .map(String::from);
                // R23: resolved before anything is handed on, so a path that
                // leaves the folder is refused before the provider is asked.
                let file = self.resolve(file_path)?;

                let provider = self.acquire_provider()?;
                if !provider
                    .file_capable_channels()
                    .contains(&channel.to_string())
                {
                    return Err(format!(
                        "Channel '{}' does not support file sending. File-capable channels: {:?}",
                        channel,
                        provider.file_capable_channels()
                    ));
                }
                provider
                    .send_file(
                        channel,
                        recipient,
                        &file,
                        filename,
                        mime_type,
                        caption.as_deref(),
                    )
                    .await
            }
            other => Err(format!(
                "Invalid action '{}'. Must be \"message\" or \"file\".",
                other
            )),
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
use super::ConnectorSendLock;
use super::annotations_for_builtin;
use super::helpers::{
    FolderRules, StoreAccess, is_store_owned_path, is_store_owned_resolved, resolve_workspace_path,
};
use crate::tools::registry::{BuiltInTool, RegisteredTool, ToolBackend, ToolContext};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use openalpaca_llm::ToolDefinition;
use openalpaca_storage::repository::TaskRepository;
use openalpaca_storage::{ArtifactStore, Database};
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;

struct SendTool {
    provider: ConnectorSendLock,
    /// The artifact store an `artifact_id` is looked up in (R23). Absent
    /// (tests, the CLI) refuses an artifact id at call time.
    db: Option<Database>,
    /// The folder a relative `file_path` is resolved under (R23, storage
    /// design §11): the file tools' root, the daemon's starting directory,
    /// until S3 moves both to the turn's working folder.
    workspace_root: PathBuf,
}

/// The file a `send` with action `file` delivers (R23).
struct SendFile {
    /// Its resolved absolute path: what the connector is handed.
    path: String,
    /// A by-product's own MIME type, used when the call names none.
    mime_type: Option<String>,
}

/// Whose by-products a call may send: the turn's owner, else, on a run's
/// context that threaded none, the run's `created_by`, as `artifact_write`
/// attributes what it saves (`put_tool_artifact`).
fn turn_owner(db: &Database, ctx: &ToolContext) -> Result<String, String> {
    if let Some(owner) = ctx.owner_id.as_deref() {
        return Ok(owner.to_string());
    }
    let task = match ctx.task_id.as_deref() {
        Some(task_id) => TaskRepository::new(db)
            .get(task_id)
            .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to load task: {e}"))?,
        None => None,
    };
    task.map(|task| task.created_by).ok_or_else(|| {
        "send cannot send an artifact on this turn: it has no owner context (it was not sent \
         on a person's behalf), and every artifact belongs to an owner."
            .to_string()
    })
}

impl SendTool {
    fn acquire_provider(
        &self,
    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn crate::orchestrator::ConnectorSendProvider>, String> {
        let guard = self
            .provider
            .read()
            .map_err(|_| "Failed to read connector send provider".to_string())?;
        guard.clone().ok_or_else(|| {
            "No connector send provider configured. External messaging is not available.".to_string()
        })
    }

    /// R23: the file a `send` with action `file` delivers, named by
    /// `file_path` or by `artifact_id` (exactly one).
    fn locate(
        &self,
        arguments: &serde_json::Value,
        ctx: &ToolContext,
    ) -> Result<SendFile, String> {
        let file_path = arguments.get("file_path").and_then(|v| v.as_str());
        let artifact_id = arguments.get("artifact_id").and_then(|v| v.as_str());
        match (file_path, artifact_id) {
            (Some(_), Some(_)) => Err("Give file_path or artifact_id, not both.".to_string()),
            (None, None) => Err(
                "Missing required parameter: file_path or artifact_id (required for action=\"file\")"
                    .to_string(),
            ),
            (Some(file_path), None) => Ok(SendFile {
                path: self.resolve(file_path)?,
                mime_type: None,
            }),
            (None, Some(id)) => self.artifact(id, ctx),
        }
    }

    /// R23: the absolute path of the file `file_path` names, resolved as
    /// `file_read` resolves one — relative, no `..`, every component (the
    /// last included) canonicalized and under the root — and refused, before
    /// and after resolution, inside the store's `state/`, as `file_read`
    /// refuses it until S3 takes both tools' store rules away with the root
    /// (R33). This path, not the argument, is what the connector is handed.
    fn resolve(&self, file_path: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
        let refuse = |what: &str| {
            format!(
                "Sending '{file_path}' is refused: it is inside {what}, which belongs to the \
                 daemon's own state/ and is not workspace content."
            )
        };
        if let Some(what) = is_store_owned_path(file_path, StoreAccess::Read) {
            return Err(refuse(what));
        }
        let resolved = resolve_workspace_path(file_path, &self.workspace_root, FolderRules::Plain)?;
        if let Some(what) =
            is_store_owned_resolved(&resolved, &self.workspace_root, StoreAccess::Read)
        {
            return Err(refuse(what));
        }
        let metadata = std::fs::metadata(&resolved)
            .map_err(|e| format!("Cannot access file '{file_path}': {e}"))?;
        if !metadata.is_file() {
            return Err(format!("'{file_path}' is not a file."));
        }
        resolved.into_os_string().into_string().map_err(|_| {
            format!(
                "'{file_path}' resolves to a path that is not UTF-8 text, which no channel can send."
            )
        })
    }

    /// R23: a by-product of the turn's owner, by its id: its head file as the
    /// store recorded it, refused when the bytes are gone. Read only. The
    /// hand-edit check a Library read makes (`resolve_content`) can record a
    /// version, and the card (S1.5) shares this lookup and must write nothing.
    fn artifact(&self, id: &str, ctx: &ToolContext) -> Result<SendFile, String> {
        let db = self.db.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| {
            format!("send cannot look up artifact '{id}' here: there is no database.")
        })?;
        let owner = turn_owner(db, ctx)?;
        let record = ArtifactStore::new(db)
            .get(id, &owner)
            .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to look up artifact '{id}': {e}"))?
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("send: no artifact '{id}' of yours."))?;
        if !std::path::Path::new(&record.storage_path).is_file() {
            return Err(format!(
                "send: the bytes of '{id}' are gone ({}).",
                record.storage_path
            ));
        }
        Ok(SendFile {
            path: record.storage_path,
            mime_type: Some(record.mime_type),
        })
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl BuiltInTool for SendTool {
    async fn execute(&self, arguments: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<String, String> {
        self.execute_with_context(arguments, &ToolContext::default())
            .await
    }

    async fn execute_with_context(
        &self,
        arguments: &serde_json::Value,
        ctx: &ToolContext,
    ) -> Result<String, String> {
        let action = arguments
            .get("action")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
            .ok_or_else(|| "Missing required parameter: action".to_string())?;

        let channel = arguments
            .get("channel")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
            .ok_or_else(|| "Missing required parameter: channel".to_string())?;

        let recipient = arguments
            .get("recipient")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
            .ok_or_else(|| "Missing required parameter: recipient".to_string())?;

        // Validate action-specific parameters before acquiring the provider.
        match action {
            "message" => {
                let content = arguments
                    .get("content")
                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                    .ok_or_else(|| {
                        "Missing required parameter: content (required for action=\"message\")"
                            .to_string()
                    })?;

                let provider = self.acquire_provider()?;
                provider.send_message(channel, recipient, content).await
            }
            "file" => {
                let filename = arguments
                    .get("filename")
                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                    .ok_or_else(|| {
                        "Missing required parameter: filename (required for action=\"file\")"
                            .to_string()
                    })?;
                let caption = arguments
                    .get("caption")
                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                    .map(String::from);
                // R23: located before anything is handed on, so a path that
                // leaves the folder, or another owner's artifact, is refused
                // before the provider is asked.
                let file = self.locate(arguments, ctx)?;
                let mime_type = arguments
                    .get("mime_type")
                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                    .or(file.mime_type.as_deref())
                    .unwrap_or("application/octet-stream");

                let provider = self.acquire_provider()?;
                if !provider
                    .file_capable_channels()
                    .contains(&channel.to_string())
                {
                    return Err(format!(
                        "Channel '{}' does not support file sending. File-capable channels: {:?}",
                        channel,
                        provider.file_capable_channels()
                    ));
                }
                provider
                    .send_file(
                        channel,
                        recipient,
                        &file.path,
                        filename,
                        mime_type,
                        caption.as_deref(),
                    )
                    .await
            }
            other => Err(format!(
                "Invalid action '{}'. Must be \"message\" or \"file\".",
                other
            )),
        }
    }
}

pub(super) fn send_tool(
    provider: ConnectorSendLock,
    db: Option<Database>,
    workspace_root: PathBuf,
) -> RegisteredTool {
    RegisteredTool {
        definition: ToolDefinition {
            name: "send".to_string(),
            description: "Send a message or file to a contact via a connected external channel \
                (Telegram, iMessage, Discord). For messages: provide action='message' \
                with content text. For files: provide action='file' with file_path (a file \
                relative to OpenAlpaca's folder) or artifact_id (a by-product you saved, by its \
                id), filename, and optional mime_type/caption. Use recipient='default' for the \
                most recent conversation, or specify a channel-specific identifier (chat_id \
                for Telegram, phone/email for iMessage, channel_id for Discord). Returns \
                confirmation on success."
                .to_string(),
            parameters: serde_json::json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "action": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "enum": ["message", "file"],
                        "description": "Action type: 'message' to send text, 'file' to send a file"
                    },
                    "channel": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "Channel identifier: 'telegram', 'imessage', or 'discord'"
                    },
                    "recipient": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "'default' for most recent conversation, or specific: chat_id (Telegram), phone/email (iMessage), channel_id (Discord)"
                    },
                    "content": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "Message text (required for action='message')"
                    },
                    "file_path": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "A file to send, relative to OpenAlpaca's folder (e.g. 'reports/q3.pdf'); absolute paths and '..' are refused. Give this or artifact_id (action='file')"
                    },
                    "artifact_id": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "A by-product to send, by its id; give this or file_path"
                    },
                    "filename": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "Display filename for the recipient (required for action='file')"
                    },
                    "mime_type": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "MIME type of the file, e.g. 'application/pdf' (defaults to the artifact's own type, else 'application/octet-stream')"
                    },
                    "caption": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "Optional caption text to accompany the file"
                    }
                },
                "required": ["action", "channel", "recipient"]
            }),
            strict: Some(true),
            input_examples: Some(vec![
                serde_json::json!({
                    "action": "message",
                    "channel": "telegram",
                    "recipient": "default",
                    "content": "Task completed successfully!"
                }),
                serde_json::json!({
                    "action": "file",
                    "channel": "telegram",
                    "recipient": "default",
                    "file_path": "reports/q3.pdf",
                    "filename": "q3.pdf",
                    "mime_type": "application/pdf",
                    "caption": "Here is the analysis report"
                }),
            ]),
        },
        backend: ToolBackend::BuiltIn(Arc::new(SendTool {
            provider,
            db,
            workspace_root,
        })),
        provides_capabilities: vec!["messaging".into()],
        exempt_from_timeout: false,
        annotations: annotations_for_builtin("send"),
        version: env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION").to_string(),
        author: "builtin".to_string(),
        created_at: chrono::Utc::now(),
    }
}
```

```rust
use super::ConnectorSendLock;
use super::annotations_for_builtin;
use super::helpers::{
    FolderRules, StoreAccess, is_store_owned_path, is_store_owned_resolved, resolve_workspace_path,
};
use crate::tools::registry::{BuiltInTool, RegisteredTool, ToolBackend, ToolContext};
use crate::utils::text::{escape_hidden_line, hidden_notice};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use openalpaca_llm::ToolDefinition;
use openalpaca_storage::repository::TaskRepository;
use openalpaca_storage::{ArtifactStore, Database};
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;

/// The tail of a refusal for an argument only a file send needs.
const FILE_ONLY: &str = " (required for action=\"file\")";

struct SendTool {
    provider: ConnectorSendLock,
    /// The artifact store an `artifact_id` is looked up in (R23). Absent
    /// (tests, the CLI) refuses an artifact id at call time.
    db: Option<Database>,
    /// The folder a relative `file_path` is resolved under (R23, storage
    /// design §11): the file tools' root, the daemon's starting directory,
    /// until S3 moves both to the turn's working folder.
    workspace_root: PathBuf,
}

/// The file a `send` with action `file` delivers (R23).
struct SendFile {
    /// Its resolved absolute path: what the card names and the connector is
    /// handed.
    path: String,
    /// Its size, for the card.
    bytes: u64,
    /// A by-product's own MIME type, used when the call names none.
    mime_type: Option<String>,
}

/// A string argument the call cannot go without, refused in one wording for
/// the card and for the send.
fn required<'a>(
    arguments: &'a serde_json::Value,
    key: &str,
    note: &str,
) -> Result<&'a str, String> {
    arguments
        .get(key)
        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("Missing required parameter: {key}{note}"))
}

/// Whose by-products a call may send: the turn's owner, else, on a run's
/// context that threaded none, the run's `created_by`, as `artifact_write`
/// attributes what it saves (`put_tool_artifact`).
fn turn_owner(db: &Database, ctx: &ToolContext) -> Result<String, String> {
    if let Some(owner) = ctx.owner_id.as_deref() {
        return Ok(owner.to_string());
    }
    let task = match ctx.task_id.as_deref() {
        Some(task_id) => TaskRepository::new(db)
            .get(task_id)
            .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to load task: {e}"))?,
        None => None,
    };
    task.map(|task| task.created_by).ok_or_else(|| {
        "send cannot send an artifact on this turn: it has no owner context (it was not sent \
         on a person's behalf), and every artifact belongs to an owner."
            .to_string()
    })
}

/// R23's card (interfaces §4.3): the file as resolved, its size, where it
/// goes and under what name. Each value is shown escaped, because a model or
/// a file on disk chose it (Gotchas). The count of what was escaped goes on
/// its own line.
fn file_card(file: &SendFile, channel: &str, recipient: &str, filename: &str) -> String {
    let path = escape_hidden_line(&file.path);
    let channel = escape_hidden_line(channel);
    let recipient = escape_hidden_line(recipient);
    let filename = escape_hidden_line(filename);
    let mut card = format!(
        "Sends {} ({} bytes) to {} recipient {} as {}.",
        path.text, file.bytes, channel.text, recipient.text, filename.text
    );
    if let Some(notice) =
        hidden_notice(path.hidden + channel.hidden + recipient.hidden + filename.hidden)
    {
        card.push('\n');
        card.push_str(&notice);
    }
    card
}

impl SendTool {
    fn acquire_provider(
        &self,
    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn crate::orchestrator::ConnectorSendProvider>, String> {
        let guard = self
            .provider
            .read()
            .map_err(|_| "Failed to read connector send provider".to_string())?;
        guard.clone().ok_or_else(|| {
            "No connector send provider configured. External messaging is not available.".to_string()
        })
    }

    /// R23: the file a `send` with action `file` delivers, named by
    /// `file_path` or by `artifact_id` (exactly one). The card and the send
    /// locate it the same way, so the card names what is sent.
    fn locate(
        &self,
        arguments: &serde_json::Value,
        ctx: &ToolContext,
    ) -> Result<SendFile, String> {
        let file_path = arguments.get("file_path").and_then(|v| v.as_str());
        let artifact_id = arguments.get("artifact_id").and_then(|v| v.as_str());
        match (file_path, artifact_id) {
            (Some(_), Some(_)) => Err("Give file_path or artifact_id, not both.".to_string()),
            (None, None) => Err(format!(
                "Missing required parameter: file_path or artifact_id{FILE_ONLY}"
            )),
            (Some(file_path), None) => self.resolve(file_path),
            (None, Some(id)) => self.artifact(id, ctx),
        }
    }

    /// R23: the file `file_path` names, resolved as `file_read` resolves one
    /// — relative, no `..`, every component (the last included) canonicalized
    /// and under the root — and refused, before and after resolution, inside
    /// the store's `state/`, as `file_read` refuses it until S3 takes both
    /// tools' store rules away with the root (R33).
    fn resolve(&self, file_path: &str) -> Result<SendFile, String> {
        let refuse = |what: &str| {
            format!(
                "Sending '{file_path}' is refused: it is inside {what}, which belongs to the \
                 daemon's own state/ and is not workspace content."
            )
        };
        if let Some(what) = is_store_owned_path(file_path, StoreAccess::Read) {
            return Err(refuse(what));
        }
        let resolved = resolve_workspace_path(file_path, &self.workspace_root, FolderRules::Plain)?;
        if let Some(what) =
            is_store_owned_resolved(&resolved, &self.workspace_root, StoreAccess::Read)
        {
            return Err(refuse(what));
        }
        let metadata = std::fs::metadata(&resolved)
            .map_err(|e| format!("Cannot access file '{file_path}': {e}"))?;
        if !metadata.is_file() {
            return Err(format!("'{file_path}' is not a file."));
        }
        let path = resolved.into_os_string().into_string().map_err(|_| {
            format!(
                "'{file_path}' resolves to a path that is not UTF-8 text, which no channel can send."
            )
        })?;
        Ok(SendFile {
            path,
            bytes: metadata.len(),
            mime_type: None,
        })
    }

    /// R23: a by-product of the turn's owner, by its id: its head file as the
    /// store recorded it, refused when the bytes are gone. Read only. The
    /// hand-edit check a Library read makes (`resolve_content`) can record a
    /// version, and the card shares this lookup and must write nothing.
    fn artifact(&self, id: &str, ctx: &ToolContext) -> Result<SendFile, String> {
        let db = self.db.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| {
            format!("send cannot look up artifact '{id}' here: there is no database.")
        })?;
        let owner = turn_owner(db, ctx)?;
        let record = ArtifactStore::new(db)
            .get(id, &owner)
            .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to look up artifact '{id}': {e}"))?
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("send: no artifact '{id}' of yours."))?;
        let metadata = std::fs::metadata(&record.storage_path)
            .ok()
            .filter(std::fs::Metadata::is_file)
            .ok_or_else(|| {
                format!(
                    "send: the bytes of '{id}' are gone ({}).",
                    record.storage_path
                )
            })?;
        Ok(SendFile {
            path: record.storage_path,
            bytes: metadata.len(),
            mime_type: Some(record.mime_type),
        })
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl BuiltInTool for SendTool {
    async fn execute(&self, arguments: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<String, String> {
        self.execute_with_context(arguments, &ToolContext::default())
            .await
    }

    async fn execute_with_context(
        &self,
        arguments: &serde_json::Value,
        ctx: &ToolContext,
    ) -> Result<String, String> {
        let action = required(arguments, "action", "")?;
        let channel = required(arguments, "channel", "")?;
        let recipient = required(arguments, "recipient", "")?;

        // Validate action-specific parameters before acquiring the provider.
        match action {
            "message" => {
                let content =
                    required(arguments, "content", " (required for action=\"message\")")?;
                let provider = self.acquire_provider()?;
                provider.send_message(channel, recipient, content).await
            }
            "file" => {
                let filename = required(arguments, "filename", FILE_ONLY)?;
                let caption = arguments
                    .get("caption")
                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                    .map(String::from);
                // R23: located before anything is handed on, so a path that
                // leaves the folder, or another owner's artifact, is refused
                // before the provider is asked.
                let file = self.locate(arguments, ctx)?;
                let mime_type = arguments
                    .get("mime_type")
                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                    .or(file.mime_type.as_deref())
                    .unwrap_or("application/octet-stream");

                let provider = self.acquire_provider()?;
                if !provider
                    .file_capable_channels()
                    .contains(&channel.to_string())
                {
                    return Err(format!(
                        "Channel '{}' does not support file sending. File-capable channels: {:?}",
                        channel,
                        provider.file_capable_channels()
                    ));
                }
                provider
                    .send_file(
                        channel,
                        recipient,
                        &file.path,
                        filename,
                        mime_type,
                        caption.as_deref(),
                    )
                    .await
            }
            other => Err(format!(
                "Invalid action '{}'. Must be \"message\" or \"file\".",
                other
            )),
        }
    }

    /// R23 (interfaces §4.3): a file send's card names the resolved file, its
    /// size and where it goes. A send that would be refused raises no card. A
    /// message keeps the ordinary card, its text shown as written.
    async fn confirmation_preview(
        &self,
        arguments: &serde_json::Value,
        ctx: &ToolContext,
    ) -> Result<Option<String>, String> {
        if arguments.get("action").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) != Some("file") {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let channel = required(arguments, "channel", "")?;
        let recipient = required(arguments, "recipient", "")?;
        let filename = required(arguments, "filename", FILE_ONLY)?;
        let file = self.locate(arguments, ctx)?;
        Ok(Some(file_card(&file, channel, recipient, filename)))
    }
}

```

```rust
/// R29 (storage design §11): whether the `../` check applies to a tool's
/// arguments. The registry decides it from the tool's backend
/// (`ToolRegistry::traversal_rule`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum TraversalRule {
    /// A string argument holding `../` or `..\` is refused: a skill script,
    /// a command, HTTP, MCP or plugin tool, whose arguments reach a shell
    /// line or another program.
    Refuse,
    /// The check is skipped: a first-party builtin, whose path arguments
    /// carry their own `..` refusal and whose other arguments are content (a
    /// source file's relative import, a workflow goal).
    Allow,
}
```

```rust
    pub fn sanitize_tool_args(

    ///
    /// Checks:
    /// - Tool name is in the allowed list (if non-empty)
    /// - All string values are checked for null bytes, and for path traversal
    ///   unless `traversal` is [`TraversalRule::Allow`] (R29)
    /// - Shell-related tool arguments are additionally checked for hidden
    ///   command injection patterns (backticks, `$(`, newlines). Normal shell
    ///   operators (pipes, redirections, chaining) are allowed because the
    ///   LLM agent constructs the full command intentionally. Non-shell tools
    ///   are NOT subject to these checks so that tools like `file_write` and
    ///   `workspace_write` can accept multi-line content.
    ///
    /// `extra_shell_tools` lists additional tool names (e.g., command-backend
    /// tools loaded from TOML config) that should receive shell injection checks
    /// alongside the hardcoded `SHELL_TOOLS` list.
    pub fn sanitize_tool_args_with(
        tool_name: &str,
        arguments: &serde_json::Value,
        allowed_tools: &[String],
        extra_shell_tools: &[String],
        traversal: TraversalRule,
    ) -> Result<(), SecurityViolation> {
        // Check tool is in allowed list
        if !allowed_tools.is_empty() && !allowed_tools.iter().any(|t| t == tool_name) {
            return Err(SecurityViolation::InputBlocked {
                reason: format!("Tool '{}' is not in the allowed tools list", tool_name),
            });
        }

        let is_shell_tool = Self::SHELL_TOOLS.contains(&tool_name)
            || extra_shell_tools.iter().any(|t| t == tool_name);

        // Recursively check string values in arguments
        Self::check_value_safety(arguments, is_shell_tool, traversal)?;

        Ok(())
    }
```

```rust

    /// R29 (storage design §11): whether the sanitizer's `../` rule applies
    /// to `tool_name`'s arguments. `Allow` only for a first-party builtin, a
    /// `BuiltIn` whose handler says its arguments reach no program. `Refuse`
    /// for a skill script, a `Command`, `Http`, `Plugin` or `Mcp` tool, and a
    /// name that is not registered (fail closed). Identity is never read
    /// from `author`, which a TOML tool sets for itself.
    pub fn traversal_rule(&self, tool_name: &str) -> TraversalRule {
        self.tools
            .get(tool_name)
            .map_or(TraversalRule::Refuse, |entry| match &entry.backend {
                ToolBackend::BuiltIn(handler) if !handler.arguments_reach_a_program() => {
                    TraversalRule::Allow
                }
                _ => TraversalRule::Refuse,
            })
    }
```

```rust
/// R45 tests (storage design §11): a process a test's own command started,
/// sent SIGKILL when this guard drops, so an assertion that fails before the
/// code under test killed it leaves no orphan behind.
#[cfg(unix)]
pub(crate) struct KillOnFail(pub(crate) i32);

#[cfg(unix)]
impl Drop for KillOnFail {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // SAFETY: `kill` only sends a signal, to the pid this test read from
        // the file its own command wrote; one already gone answers ESRCH.
        unsafe {
            libc::kill(self.0, libc::SIGKILL);
        }
    }
}

/// How long an R45 test waits for a killed process to be gone. The kill is
/// immediate, but the system reaps an orphan asynchronously, and a loaded CI
/// machine is slow.
#[cfg(unix)]
pub(crate) const GONE_WITHIN: std::time::Duration = std::time::Duration::from_secs(5);

/// The pid a test's command wrote to `path`, waiting up to `within` for it.
#[cfg(unix)]
pub(crate) async fn pid_from_file(path: &std::path::Path, within: std::time::Duration) -> i32 {
    let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + within;
    loop {
        if let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(path)
            && let Ok(pid) = text.trim().parse::<i32>()
        {
            return pid;
        }
        assert!(
            tokio::time::Instant::now() < deadline,
            "no pid in {} after {within:?}",
            path.display()
        );
        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
    }
}

/// Whether `pid` has ended: `kill(pid, 0)` answers ESRCH or, on Linux, the
/// process is a zombie nobody has reaped yet (`kill` still finds one).
#[cfg(unix)]
pub(crate) fn process_is_gone(pid: i32) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: signal 0 sends nothing; it only asks whether `pid` exists.
    if unsafe { libc::kill(pid, 0) } != 0 {
        return std::io::Error::last_os_error().raw_os_error() == Some(libc::ESRCH);
    }
    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
    {
        if let Ok(stat) = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{pid}/stat")) {
            // `pid (comm) S …`: the state follows the last `)`.
            return stat
                .rsplit_once(')')
                .is_some_and(|(_, rest)| rest.trim_start().starts_with('Z'));
        }
    }
    false
}

/// Polls [`process_is_gone`] for up to `within`.
#[cfg(unix)]
pub(crate) async fn wait_until_gone(pid: i32, within: std::time::Duration) -> bool {
    let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + within;
    while tokio::time::Instant::now() < deadline {
        if process_is_gone(pid) {
            return true;
        }
        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
    }
    process_is_gone(pid)
}
```

```rust
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_shell_command_creates_command() {

        let _cmd = shell_command("echo hello");
```

```rust
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_program_that_cannot_start_is_a_spawn_failure() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let mut cmd = Command::new(dir.path().join("no-such-program"));
        cmd.current_dir(dir.path());
        let outcome = run_bounded(cmd, Duration::from_secs(5)).await;
        assert!(matches!(outcome, Err(RunFailure::Spawn(_))), "{outcome:?}");
    }

    /// `sleep 30` started in the background, its pid written to `pidfile`,
    /// and waited on: a command that started a process of its own (R45).
    #[cfg(unix)]
    fn starts_a_sleep(dir: &std::path::Path, pidfile: &std::path::Path) -> Command {
        let mut cmd = shell_command(&format!(
            "sleep 30 & echo $! > '{}'; wait",
            pidfile.display()
        ));
        cmd.current_dir(dir);
        cmd
    }

    #[cfg(unix)]

    async fn a_command_that_ends_returns_its_status_and_both_streams() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let mut cmd = shell_command("printf out; printf err >&2; exit 3");
        cmd.current_dir(dir.path());
        let output = run_bounded(cmd, Duration::from_secs(5)).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(output.status.code(), Some(3));
        assert_eq!(output.stdout, b"out");
        assert_eq!(output.stderr, b"err");
    }

    #[cfg(unix)]
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_command_past_its_time_is_killed_with_the_processes_it_started() {
        use crate::test_util::{GONE_WITHIN, KillOnFail, pid_from_file, wait_until_gone};
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let pidfile = dir.path().join("pid");
        let outcome = run_bounded(starts_a_sleep(dir.path(), &pidfile), Duration::from_secs(1)).await;
        let pid = pid_from_file(&pidfile, Duration::from_secs(1)).await;
        let _kill = KillOnFail(pid);
        assert!(matches!(outcome, Err(RunFailure::TimedOut)), "{outcome:?}");
        assert!(
            wait_until_gone(pid, GONE_WITHIN).await,
            "the background sleep {pid} outlived the timeout"
        );
    }

    /// The sandbox's per-tool timeout and a cancelled run both drop the
    /// tool's future, and dropping it is a kill too.
    #[cfg(unix)]
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_dropped_run_kills_the_processes_the_command_started() {
        use crate::test_util::{GONE_WITHIN, KillOnFail, pid_from_file, wait_until_gone};
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let pidfile = dir.path().join("pid");
        let run = tokio::spawn(run_bounded(
            starts_a_sleep(dir.path(), &pidfile),
            Duration::from_secs(60),
        ));
        let pid = pid_from_file(&pidfile, Duration::from_secs(5)).await;
        let _kill = KillOnFail(pid);
        run.abort();
        // Awaiting the handle is what makes the runtime drop the future.
        let _ = run.await;
        assert!(
            wait_until_gone(pid, GONE_WITHIN).await,
            "the background sleep {pid} outlived the dropped run"
        );
    }

    /// A normal end signals nothing: once a group is empty the system may
    /// give its id to another, so an ended run's id is never used. A process
    /// the command detached on purpose keeps running.
    #[cfg(unix)]
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_normal_end_leaves_a_process_the_command_detached() {
        use crate::test_util::{KillOnFail, pid_from_file, process_is_gone};
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let pidfile = dir.path().join("pid");
        let mut cmd = shell_command(&format!(
            "sleep 30 > /dev/null 2>&1 & echo $! > '{}'",
            pidfile.display()
        ));
        cmd.current_dir(dir.path());
        let output = run_bounded(cmd, Duration::from_secs(5))
            .await
            .expect("the shell ends at once");
        assert!(output.status.success());
        let pid = pid_from_file(&pidfile, Duration::from_secs(1)).await;
        // This test's own cleanup: the guard kills the sleep it left.
        let _kill = KillOnFail(pid);
        assert!(!process_is_gone(pid), "a normal end signalled the group");
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Platform-specific helpers for tool execution.

use std::process::{Output, Stdio};
use std::time::Duration;

use tokio::io::{AsyncRead, AsyncReadExt};
use tokio::process::{Child, Command};

/// Build a `tokio::process::Command` that runs the given shell command
/// using the platform's default shell.
///
/// - macOS / Linux: `sh -c "<cmd>"`
/// - Windows: `cmd /c "<cmd>"`
pub fn shell_command(cmd: &str) -> tokio::process::Command {
    if cfg!(target_os = "windows") {
        let mut c = tokio::process::Command::new("cmd");
        c.arg("/c").arg(cmd);
        c
    } else {
        let mut c = tokio::process::Command::new("sh");
        c.arg("-c").arg(cmd);
        c
    }
}

/// Why [`run_bounded`] produced no output.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum RunFailure {
    /// The program could not be started.
    Spawn(std::io::Error),
    /// `timeout` passed; the process (and its group, on unix) was killed.
    TimedOut,
    /// Reading its output or waiting for it failed; it was killed the same
    /// way.
    Io(std::io::Error),
}

/// Run `cmd` to its end with stdin null and stdout/stderr captured. Kill it
/// when `timeout` passes **or the returned future is dropped**. The sandbox's
/// per-tool timeout and a run cancelled mid-call both drop the tool's
/// future (R45, storage design §11).
///
/// unix: the child is started in a new process group (`process_group(0)`).
/// A guard owning the `Child` sends `killpg(pgid, SIGKILL)` on every exit
/// that is not a normal end, before it lets the `Child` drop, so the
/// processes the command started go too. A normal end disarms the guard. A
/// process that leaves the group on its own (`setsid`) is out of reach.
/// Windows: `kill_on_drop(true)` kills the direct child only, and processes
/// it started survive ("where the platform allows", R45).
pub async fn run_bounded(mut cmd: Command, timeout: Duration) -> Result<Output, RunFailure> {
    cmd.stdin(Stdio::null())
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(Stdio::piped())
        .kill_on_drop(true);
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        cmd.process_group(0);
    }
    let mut run = KillGuard::new(cmd.spawn().map_err(RunFailure::Spawn)?);
    let out_pipe = run.child.stdout.take();
    let err_pipe = run.child.stderr.take();
    let ended = tokio::time::timeout(timeout, async {
        let (status, stdout, stderr) =
            tokio::try_join!(run.child.wait(), read_all(out_pipe), read_all(err_pipe))?;
        Ok::<Output, std::io::Error>(Output {
            status,
            stdout,
            stderr,
        })
    })
    .await;
    match ended {
        Ok(Ok(output)) => {
            run.disarm();
            Ok(output)
        }
        Ok(Err(e)) => Err(RunFailure::Io(e)),
        Err(_elapsed) => Err(RunFailure::TimedOut),
    }
}

/// Everything a pipe yields until it closes; nothing for a pipe not taken.
async fn read_all(pipe: Option<impl AsyncRead + Unpin>) -> std::io::Result<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
    if let Some(mut pipe) = pipe {
        pipe.read_to_end(&mut bytes).await?;
    }
    Ok(bytes)
}

/// The running child of [`run_bounded`], killed with its process group on
/// every exit that is not a normal end (R45).
struct KillGuard {
    child: Child,
    /// The group to kill: the child's pid, which `process_group(0)` made the
    /// group's id. `None` once a normal end disarmed the guard. Never
    /// `Some(0)`: `killpg(0, …)` would signal the daemon's own group.
    #[cfg(unix)]
    group: Option<i32>,
}

impl KillGuard {
    fn new(child: Child) -> Self {
        Self {
            #[cfg(unix)]
            group: child
                .id()
                .and_then(|pid| i32::try_from(pid).ok())
                .filter(|pid| *pid > 0),
            child,
        }
    }

    /// A normal end: the group is not signalled.
    fn disarm(&mut self) {
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            self.group = None;
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(unix)]
impl Drop for KillGuard {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(group) = self.group.take() {
            // SAFETY: `killpg` only sends a signal. `group` is the positive id
            // of the group this run's child leads, signalled only while the
            // run has not ended normally, so the child or a process it started
            // still holds it.
            unsafe {
                libc::killpg(group, libc::SIGKILL);
            }
        }
        // `child` drops after this body, and `kill_on_drop(true)` kills it:
        // on Windows the only process that is killed.
    }
}
```

```rust
// --- R45: a skill script is killed with what it started (storage design §11) ---

#[cfg(unix)]
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_skill_script_that_times_out_takes_the_processes_it_started_with_it() {
    use crate::test_util::{GONE_WITHIN, KillOnFail, pid_from_file, wait_until_gone};
    use std::time::Duration;

    let skill = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    std::fs::create_dir_all(skill.path().join("scripts")).unwrap();
    std::fs::write(
        skill.path().join("scripts/hang.sh"),
        "for a in \"$@\"; do case \"$a\" in --pidfile=*) P=\"${a#--pidfile=}\" ;; esac; done\n\
         sleep 30 &\n\
         echo $! > \"$P\"\n\
         wait\n",
    )
    .unwrap();
    let tool = ScriptToolBuiltIn::new(
        skill.path(),
        &crate::middleware::skill::ScriptConfig {
            file: "hang.sh".to_string(),
            name: "hang".to_string(),

            parameters: serde_json::json!({"type": "object"}),
            interpreter: Some("sh".to_string()),
            timeout_secs: 1,
        },
    )
    .unwrap();
    let pidfile = skill.path().join("pid");

    let err = tool
        .execute(&serde_json::json!({"pidfile": pidfile.to_str().unwrap()}))
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    let pid = pid_from_file(&pidfile, Duration::from_secs(1)).await;
    let _kill = KillOnFail(pid);
    assert_eq!(err, "Script timed out after 1s");
    assert!(
        wait_until_gone(pid, GONE_WITHIN).await,
        "the script's background sleep {pid} outlived its timeout"
    );
}
```

  The string continuations (`\n\` followed by a newline) drop the next line's leading spaces, so the script's lines

### Spec conflicts

1. **The interfaces sheet leaves `send` able to send `state/` from S1 until S3.** §0.1 and §4.3 resolve `send`'s
   `file_path` under the startup root in S1. §2's R33 list ("all five rules from both file tools") gives `send` none
   of `file_read`'s store refusals. The startup root is `std::env::current_dir()` (`apps/openalpacad/src/services/tools.rs`,
   `let workspace_root = std::env::current_dir().ok();`), and both launchers start the daemon in the home store. So
   `send` with `file_path: "state/discovery.json"` would hand the daemon's token, its database or `.master_key` to a
   connector, which is the exact hole the task text gives as the reason R33 waits for S3. **Smallest correction (taken
   in S1.3):** `send` runs `file_read`'s two checks (`is_store_owned_path(.., Read)` before resolution,
   `is_store_owned_resolved(.., Read)` after). **S3's R33 removal list gains `SendTool::resolve`'s two checks** beside
   `file_read`'s.
2. **"the lock does not change" (interfaces §3.2) is wrong by one line.** `Cargo.lock` records each workspace
   package's direct dependencies, and `openalpaca_core`'s list gains ` "libc",`. The locked version is `0.2.189`, not
   `0.2.180`, which is the workspace requirement. tokio is locked at `1.53.1`, not `1.49.0`, and
   `Command::process_group` is there (`tokio-1.53.1/src/process/mod.rs:790`, `#[cfg(unix)]`). That settles the sheet's
   first §11 UNVERIFIED. S1.9 stages `Cargo.lock`.
3. **`send_tool(provider, db, workspace_root)` (interfaces §0.1) lands in two commits.** S1.3 adds `workspace_root`
   and S1.4 adds `db`. If `db` landed in S1.3, a struct field nobody reads until S1.4 would be a dead-code warning in
   one commit. S1's end state matches the sheet.
4. **The send card's `{file}` is escaped (interfaces §4.3).** The sheet's sentence ("`{file}` the resolved absolute
   path, `{channel}`, `{recipient}`, `{filename}` each `escape_hidden_line`") can be read as leaving `{file}` raw.
   §1.3's "folders print as they are" is about the owner's own folder. The file's name comes from the model's argument
   or from a file on disk, and the Gotcha escapes anything a person decides on that a model or a file chose. **S1.5
   escapes `{file}` too and counts it in the notice.** Its test plants the U+202E in the file's name.
5. **"Names kept (minimal churn: 26 test call sites)" (interfaces §2).** At `d484a56a` there are 8 test call sites
   (all `resolve_workspace_path_for_write`, in `helpers/tests.rs`) and 2 production calls (`file_ops.rs`, one per
   resolver). Nothing depends on the number; S1.1's `perl` step asserts the 8.
6. **Kill-test poll ceiling (interfaces §3.3: 2 s).** S1 polls up to 5 s (`GONE_WITHIN`), and on Linux also counts an
   unreaped zombie as gone (`/proc/<pid>/stat` state `Z`). A killed grandchild is reaped by init/launchd
   asynchronously. Inside a container whose PID 1 reaps nothing, it stays a zombie and `kill(pid, 0)` keeps answering
   0. The loop exits as soon as the process is gone, so the ceiling costs nothing on success.
7. **R29's list (design §11) names script, command, MCP and plugin tools; HTTP tools are not named.** S1 refuses
   `../` for `Http` too (interfaces §3.1 already does). Its arguments are substituted into a URL that reaches another
   program, and this is today's behaviour, so it is "no change" for them, not a new rule.
8. **`file_no_provider_returns_clear_error` keeps its name and purpose (interfaces §8.2 says it "flips").** It sent
   an absolute `/tmp/test.pdf`, which S1.3 refuses before the provider. It is rewritten to send a relative file in a
   tempdir root, which still reaches the provider check. The absolute-path refusal the flip would have pinned is
   pinned by the new `a_path_that_leaves_the_folder_is_refused_before_the_provider`, so both behaviours are tested.

### Open points

- **`FolderRules::Project` is constructed by no non-test code in S1.** It carries
  `#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]`, so the build stays warning-free. S3 must remove that attribute when
  `file_read` first passes `Project`. The attribute's comment says so.
- **`startup_root`** (new in S1.3, shared by `builtin_tools` and `builtin_tools_with_persona_context`) belongs on
  S4a's removal list, with `builtin_tools`' `workspace_root` parameter (interfaces §0.1). In S3, `send` stops taking
  the root (`send_tool(provider, db)`), and `startup_root` keeps only `file_write`'s use.
- **`send` by `artifact_id` reads `ArtifactStore::get` plus a stat of `storage_path`, not `resolve_content`.** The card
  and the send share one pure `locate`, so the card names exactly what is sent. `resolve_content` can record a
  hand-edit version (a write), which a preview must not do. The cost is that `send` does not stamp `missing_since` on a
  missing head, which the next Library read does. S5's `artifact_read` uses `resolve_content` as the sheet says; the
  two tools differ on purpose.
- **`send` by `artifact_id` is owner-scoped in S1; the project scope comes in S4a.17** (the lead's ruling R-T3). S1
  refuses another owner's artifact (interfaces §4.3's refusal); S4a.17, which rewrites `SendTool::artifact`, also
  refuses another project's by-product with `artifact_read`'s sentence (S5.2), so one rule governs which by-products
  a conversation may name.
- **The nested `invoke_skill:<id>` adapters (`SkillInvocationBuiltInAdapter`) answer `false` (Allow).** Their only
  argument, `query`, goes to a nested model loop whose own tool calls go through the sandbox again. Only
  `ScriptToolBuiltIn` overrides. A future builtin whose arguments reach a program must override
  `arguments_reach_a_program`; S1.7's `every_first_party_builtin_says_its_arguments_reach_no_program` is where that
  shows.
- **R45 residue, recorded and not built.** A process that leaves the group on its own (`setsid`, a daemon that
  double-forks) is out of the kill's reach. On Windows only the direct child is killed. A daemon killed by its
  force-exit path (`process::exit` after `FORCE_EXIT_GRACE`) runs no drop, so a running command survives it; that was
  already true with `kill_on_drop(false)`. Because commands now run in their own process group, a daemon run in a
  terminal's foreground no longer passes the terminal's Ctrl-C to them. The daemon's shutdown drops their futures,
  which kills them. A command that opens `/dev/tty` from a background group would stop on SIGTTIN until its timeout
  kills it. The daemon runs detached in every shipped launcher. These are recorded, not built: S6.6 writes them into
  design §18 (the lead's ruling R-T16).
- **The S1→S3 window for `send`.** Its folder is the startup root: the home store from the app, or the repository
  from a `cargo run` in a checkout. The description says "relative to OpenAlpaca's folder" (the sheet's S1 wording).
  It is unreleased and closed by S3.
- UNVERIFIED (cargo-only, a Windows target): that the `#[cfg(not(unix))]` side of `run_bounded` (no
  `process_group`, no `Drop` on `KillGuard`) compiles. Neither CI nor this machine builds Rust for Windows; the code
  there is the struct with one field and an empty `disarm`. Read, it is well-formed: the `#[cfg(unix)]` field, its
  initialiser, the `process_group` block, the `Drop` impl and every spawning test are all gated alike.
- The test totals in each Step 4 (21/26 helpers, 13/19/24 send, 43 sanitizer, 49 sandbox, 6 platform, 2
  shell_execute) were counted from the files at `d484a56a` by the drafter and again by the verifier: `helpers/tests.rs`
  15 tests, `send.rs` 9, `sanitizer/tests.rs` 39, `sandbox/tests.rs` 46, `platform.rs` 1, `shell_execute.rs` 0, every
  `#[cfg(unix)]` test counted (macOS and Linux), and no other test path contains any of the filters. No cargo was run;
  the engineer confirms them on the first run.
- **For S6's wording pass, not S1's:** `docs/tools/DESIGN.md` (the sanitizer row, "`../` and `..\` are rejected in any
  string value") and `docs/tools/TECHNICAL.md` (the sanitizer's "every string value: path traversal") describe the
  blanket rule R29 narrows. Both date from 2026-07-19 and are not on interfaces §8.4's list; S6 decides whether they
  are touched.
- UNVERIFIED (run-time only, not settled by reading): macOS `kill(pid, 0)` answers 0 for a zombie until launchd reaps
  it. `wait_until_gone`'s 5 s poll covers that either way.
- **The kill tests leave at most one bounded orphan on an early panic.** If `pid_from_file` panics before
  `KillOnFail` is made (the command never wrote its pid), that test's `sleep 30` ends by itself within 30 s. No test
  uses `sleep 3600`.

## Stage 2 — slice S2: approvals (ST-15, R34, ST-16 for the read tools that exist)

Drafted at `d484a56a` against `interfaces.md` (the shared sheet) and `spec-stage2.md` (design rev 0.9 §12, §16 step
(2)). Every `file:line` is from `d484a56a` and lands after S1, which edits some of the same files (`file_ops.rs`,
`shell_execute.rs`, `registry/mod.rs`, `builtins/mod.rs`): **locate every edit by the content quoted, never by line.**

### What this slice does

S2 makes the approval card say where a call acts, and stops the by-product writers from asking. It adds
`ToolContext.conversation_id` (nothing outside tests sets it until S3, R44) and `tools::working_folder`, the one pure
function that answers "which folder does this call act in": the registered project's root, else the conversation's
scratch folder under `~/.openalpaca/scratch/`, else one of five refusals whose sentences S3 hands the model. It
creates nothing. Through the preview hook that already exists (`BuiltInTool::confirmation_preview`,
`tools/registry/mod.rs`), `shell_execute`'s card names the folder the command starts in and says the folder does not
confine the command (ST-14, R34). `file_write`'s card names where the file lands under Round G's routing: a by-product
in which artifact store, or the plain write in the folder the daemon was started in. A hidden character in the path
the model wrote is shown escaped, with the notice under it (CLAUDE.md, Gotchas). S4a moves the write into the project
and adds that landing. ST-15: `artifact_write` and `workspace_write` stop prompting, while `file_write` and
`shell_execute` keep asking on every call. The rule is by tool name, through `annotations_for_builtin`, so it is
decided before the tool runs. With no project, `file_write` still asks although it saves a by-product. ST-16 is pinned
for `file_read` and `read_result`. The chat connectors (Telegram, iMessage, Discord) print the card's text too
(interfaces §10 C6).

**No GUI change.** `apps/openalpaca-gui/src/components/chat/ToolConfirmationBanner.tsx:95-103` draws `preview`
verbatim, under "From OpenAlpaca", `whitespace-pre-wrap`, above the arguments. All three rails that draw a card thread
it: the WS event (`hooks/useChat.ts:266`), the pending snapshot (`views/chat/useChatSession.ts:790`) and the SSE
request (`useChatSession.ts:978`). The CLI prints it as given too: the inline prompt (`apps/openalpaca/src/chat_stream/mod.rs:581`)
and `tasks confirmations list|watch` (`commands/confirmations.rs`: `list` through `preview_blocks`, `:304`; `watch`'s
own block, `:472`). Settings → Tools'
"requires confirmation" reads the annotation (`apps/openalpacad/src/routes/tools.rs:112`, `requires_confirmation` =
`destructive_hint`), so it follows ST-15 with no code change. No bun gate runs in S2.

**What S2 does not do.** No tool acts in its working folder yet: S3 does that. Until S3, a project turn's shell card
names the project folder while the command still runs in the daemon's folder. That window is recorded (interfaces §1.4,
§10 C8), and nothing in S2 fixes it. Every refusal of `working_folder` leaves today's ordinary card (`Ok(None)`). No
route, refusal code, migration, storage re-export or GUI export changes, so `docs/api/` does not move: core and
connectors list top-level modules only (`docs/api/crates/openalpaca_core.md`, `…_connectors.md`), and
`gen_api_docs.py` masks comments.

  ```rust
  /// A guarded temp home store and one temp project folder registered under
  /// it (storage design, Stage 2): every test that writes, edits, lists or
  /// runs a command does it here — never in the repository, never in the
  /// process's current directory, never in `~/.openalpaca`. `_guard` is
  /// declared first so it drops first: the variable is restored before the
  /// folders go.
  pub(crate) struct GuardedProject {
      _guard: HomeStoreGuard,
      pub(crate) home: tempfile::TempDir,
      pub(crate) project: tempfile::TempDir,
      /// The project's canonical root, as `projects::register` recorded it.
      pub(crate) root: std::path::PathBuf,
  }

  impl GuardedProject {
      /// Two tempdirs: the home store pointed at the first, the second
      /// registered as a project under it.
      pub(crate) fn new() -> Self {
          let home = tempfile::tempdir().expect("a temp home store");
          let project = tempfile::tempdir().expect("a temp project folder");
          let guard =
              HomeStoreGuard::set(&home.path().canonicalize().expect("the temp home resolves"));
          let root = openalpaca_storage::store::projects::register(
              &project.path().canonicalize().expect("the temp project resolves"),
          )
          .expect("the temp project registers under the temp home")
          .root;
          Self {
              _guard: guard,
              home,
              project,
              root,
          }
      }

      /// A project turn: its owner, the project as the request's root (and as
      /// memory's), and a conversation.
      pub(crate) fn ctx(&self) -> crate::tools::registry::ToolContext {
          let root = self.root.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
          crate::tools::registry::ToolContext {
              owner_id: Some("owner-test".to_string()),
              workspace_id: Some(root.clone()),
              request_workspace_root: Some(root),
              conversation_id: Some("conv-test".to_string()),
              ..Default::default()
          }
      }

      /// A turn with no project: its conversation, and nothing else. A test
      /// that needs an owner sets `owner_id` over it.
      pub(crate) fn scratch_ctx(&self) -> crate::tools::registry::ToolContext {
          crate::tools::registry::ToolContext {
              conversation_id: Some("conv-test".to_string()),
              ..Default::default()
          }
      }

      /// The home store's root, canonical: what `store::home_root()` answers
      /// while the guard holds.
      pub(crate) fn home_root(&self) -> std::path::PathBuf {
          self.home.path().canonicalize().expect("the temp home resolves")
      }
  }
  ```

  In `crates/openalpaca_core/src/tools/working_folder.rs`, insert above `#[cfg(test)]`:

  ```rust
  //! The working folder of a tool call (storage design §10): the project's own
  //! folder when the turn carries a registered project, else the conversation's
  //! scratch folder under the home store. One function decides it for every
  //! tool that acts on files or runs a command, and for the approval card that
  //! names it (R34).
  //!
  //! [`working_folder`] is pure. It reads at most two small files (a project's
  //! `project.json`, through `projects::lookup`) and creates nothing, so asking
  //! where a call would act, as the card does, never makes a folder.

  use std::fmt;
  use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

  use openalpaca_storage::store::{self, ContentKind, projects};

  use crate::session_log::session_dir_name;
  use crate::tools::registry::ToolContext;

  /// Where a tool call's files and commands live (design §10).
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub enum WorkingFolder {
      /// The turn's registered project: its canonical root (`Project::root`).
      Project { root: PathBuf },
      /// No project: `<home>/scratch/<session_dir_name(conversation_id)>`.
      Scratch {
          dir: PathBuf,
          conversation_id: String,
      },
  }

  impl WorkingFolder {
      /// The folder itself.
      pub fn path(&self) -> &Path {
          match self {
              Self::Project { root } => root,
              Self::Scratch { dir, .. } => dir,
          }
      }

      /// Whether the folder is a project's — where R32's rules bind.
      pub fn is_project(&self) -> bool {
          matches!(self, Self::Project { .. })
      }
  }

  /// Why a call has no working folder. `Display` is the one sentence the model,
  /// the card and the report read.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub enum WorkingFolderRefusal {
      /// A tool reached through `execute` (no context) — R26.
      NoContext,
      /// R27: the project is registered and its folder is gone (ST-7).
      ProjectMissing { root: String },
      /// The turn's root names no folder under `projects/` any more — re-pointed
      /// or deleted while the conversation ran.
      NotAProject { root: String },
      /// R44: neither a project nor a conversation id.
      NoConversation,
      /// `projects/` or the home root could not be read, or the scratch folder
      /// could not be made.
      Unavailable { reason: String },
  }

  impl fmt::Display for WorkingFolderRefusal {
      fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
          match self {
              Self::NoContext => f.write_str(
                  "This tool acts in the conversation's working folder, and this call carries no \
                   conversation to name one.",
              ),
              Self::ProjectMissing { root } => write!(
                  f,
                  "The project folder {root} is missing — its folder is gone: re-point the project \
                   to where its folder is now (Settings → Connection → Projects → Re-point…, or \
                   openalpaca store rebase {root} <new path>), or delete its data (Delete data…, or \
                   openalpaca store purge {root}). No file tool or command runs until then."
              ),
              Self::NotAProject { root } => write!(
                  f,
                  "{}",
                  projects::ProjectError::NotRegistered { root: root.clone() }
              ),
              Self::NoConversation => f.write_str(
                  "This call has neither a project nor a conversation, so it has no working \
                   folder: file tools and commands run only inside a conversation or a project.",
              ),
              Self::Unavailable { reason } => {
                  write!(f, "The working folder could not be read: {reason}")
              }
          }
      }
  }

  impl std::error::Error for WorkingFolderRefusal {}

  /// The working folder of the call `ctx` describes (design §10). Pure: reads
  /// two small files at most and creates nothing.
  ///
  /// 1. A non-blank `request_workspace_root`: an absolute one is looked up
  ///    under `projects/` — a present project is its root, a missing one
  ///    [`WorkingFolderRefusal::ProjectMissing`], an unrecorded one
  ///    [`WorkingFolderRefusal::NotAProject`]; a relative one is not a
  ///    project either.
  /// 2. Else a non-blank `conversation_id`: that conversation's scratch folder.
  /// 3. Else [`WorkingFolderRefusal::NoConversation`].
  pub fn working_folder(ctx: &ToolContext) -> Result<WorkingFolder, WorkingFolderRefusal> {
      if let Some(root) = ctx
          .request_workspace_root
          .as_deref()
          .filter(|root| !root.trim().is_empty())
      {
          return project_folder(root);
      }
      let Some(id) = ctx
          .conversation_id
          .as_deref()
          .filter(|id| !id.trim().is_empty())
      else {
          return Err(WorkingFolderRefusal::NoConversation);
      };
      let home = store::home_root().map_err(|e| WorkingFolderRefusal::Unavailable {
          reason: format!("{e:#}"),
      })?;
      Ok(WorkingFolder::Scratch {
          dir: home
              .join(ContentKind::Scratch.dir_name())
              .join(session_dir_name(id)),
          conversation_id: id.to_string(),
      })
  }

  /// Step 1 of [`working_folder`]: the request's root, as `projects/` records it.
  fn project_folder(root: &str) -> Result<WorkingFolder, WorkingFolderRefusal> {
      let path = Path::new(root);
      if !path.is_absolute() {
          return Err(WorkingFolderRefusal::NotAProject {
              root: root.to_string(),
          });
      }
      match projects::lookup(path) {
          Ok(Some(project)) if !project.missing => Ok(WorkingFolder::Project { root: project.root }),
          Ok(Some(project)) => Err(WorkingFolderRefusal::ProjectMissing {
              root: project.root_string(),
          }),
          Ok(None) => Err(WorkingFolderRefusal::NotAProject {
              root: root.to_string(),
          }),
          Err(e) => Err(WorkingFolderRefusal::Unavailable {
              reason: format!("{e:#}"),
          }),
      }
  }
  ```

  `lookup` is used, not `by_recorded_root`. The reason is that `request_workspace_root` is the canonical root the
  gateway resolved (interfaces §1.2). The project's root and the scratch path print unescaped: the first is the
  owner's own path and the second is OpenAlpaca's (interfaces §1.3, Stage 1's recorded choice). Every item is `pub` in a
  `pub mod` of the library, so the variants and functions S2 does not call yet (`NoContext`; `is_project`'s callers
  are S3's) raise no `dead_code` warning.

  ```rust
          let policy = SandboxPolicy {
              agent_id: "general_agent".to_string(),
              allowed_capabilities: Allowlist::Unrestricted,
              denied_capabilities: vec![],
              require_confirmation_for: vec![],
              max_tool_calls: None,
              max_tool_runtime_secs: 60,
              stream_id: None,
              lane_key: None,
              confirmation_timeout_secs: Some(5),
              auto_approve: false,
              unattended: false,
          };
          let marker = gp.root.join("ran.txt");
          let call = ToolCall {
              id: "tc_1".to_string(),
              name: "shell_execute".to_string(),
              arguments: serde_json::json!({"command": format!("touch {}", marker.display())}),
          };
          let responder = tokio::spawn({
              let broker = broker.clone();
              async move {
                  loop {
                      match events.recv().await {
                          Ok(SystemEvent::ToolConfirmationRequested {
                              request_id,
                              preview,
                              ..
                          }) => {
                              broker
                                  .respond(
                                      &request_id,
                                      ConfirmationResponse {
                                          approved: false,
                                          approval_scope: None,
                                      },
                                  )
                                  .unwrap();
                              return preview;
                          }
                          Ok(_) => continue,
                          Err(e) => panic!("the bus closed before a card was raised: {e}"),
                      }
                  }
              }
          });

          let result = sandbox.execute_tool(&call, &policy, &gp.ctx()).await;

          // The denial first: a call refused before any card (capability,
          // sanitizer) publishes no event, and awaiting the responder then would
          // wait for ever — this panics cleanly instead, aborting the task.
          let refusal = result.unwrap_err();
          assert!(refusal.contains("denied by user"), "the person said no: {refusal}");
          assert_eq!(responder.await.unwrap(), Some(project_card(&gp.root)));
          assert!(!marker.exists(), "a denied command never runs");
      }
  }
  ```

  ```rust
  /// Where a write lands, for its card (R34).
  pub(super) enum WriteLanding<'a> {
      /// A by-product in `store`, the artifact store directory
      /// (`store_root(scope)?.join("artifacts")` — creates nothing).
      ByProduct { store: &'a Path },
      /// The plain write at a startup root that is not the home store: a daemon
      /// started by hand in a folder (Round G's exception, until the write
      /// moves into the project).
      StartupFolder { dir: &'a Path },
  }

  /// The card of a file write: the file, where it lands, and — when the path
  /// the model wrote holds a hidden character — the notice on its own line.
  pub(super) fn write_card(path: &str, landing: WriteLanding<'_>) -> String {
      let shown = escape_hidden_line(path);
      let line = match landing {
          WriteLanding::ByProduct { store } => format!(
              "Saves {} as a by-product in {}, OpenAlpaca's artifact store — not in a folder of \
               yours.",
              shown.text,
              store.display()
          ),
          WriteLanding::StartupFolder { dir } => format!(
              "Writes {} in {}, the folder the daemon was started in.",
              shown.text,
              dir.display()
          ),
      };
      match hidden_notice(shown.hidden) {
          Some(notice) => format!("{line}\n{notice}"),
          None => line,
      }
  }
  ```

    doc comment, add:

    ```rust
        /// Round G's routing (FW-1), one predicate for the write and its card:
        /// the plain write is taken only on a turn that carries a project and
        /// from a workspace root that is not the home store; every other write
        /// is saved as an artifact.
        fn saves_as_artifact(&self, scope: &StoreScope) -> bool {
            !matches!(scope, StoreScope::Project(_)) || is_the_home_root(&self.workspace_root)
        }

        /// R34: where this write would land, for its card — [`Self::write`]'s own
        /// routing. `None` (today's ordinary card) for a call the write refuses
        /// on its face — no path, an absolute one, a `..`, one that names no
        /// file — and when the store cannot be named.
        fn landing_card(&self, arguments: &serde_json::Value, ctx: &ToolContext) -> Option<String> {
            let path = arguments.get("path").and_then(|v| v.as_str())?;
            if validate_workspace_path(path).is_err() || !names_a_file(path) {
                return None;
            }
            let scope = scope_from_context(ctx);
            if !self.saves_as_artifact(&scope) {
                return Some(write_card(
                    path,
                    WriteLanding::StartupFolder {
                        dir: &self.workspace_root,
                    },
                ));
            }
            let store = openalpaca_storage::store::store_root(&scope)
                .ok()?
                .join(ContentKind::Artifacts.dir_name());
            Some(write_card(path, WriteLanding::ByProduct { store: &store }))
        }
    ```

    ```rust
    /// Whether `path` ends in a file name. '', '.', 'reports/' or a blank last
    /// component name a directory, which `file_write` refuses (G2).
    fn names_a_file(path: &str) -> bool {
        let last = path.rsplit(['/', '\\']).next().unwrap_or_default().trim();
        !(last.is_empty() || last == ".")
    }
    ```

  ```bash
  adds the project landing.

  Verified: cargo test -p openalpaca_core a_write_card — 6 passed;
  cargo test -p openalpaca_core approval_preview — 5 passed;
  cargo test -p openalpaca_core tools::builtins::file_ops — 0 failed.
  ```
