### Task S2.5: Reading never asks — the pin for `file_read` and `read_result` (ST-16)

**Files:**
- Modify `crates/openalpaca_core/src/tools/builtins/tests.rs`: a new test after
  `annotations_for_builtin_by_product_writers_never_prompt`.
- Test: the same file.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `GuardedProject` (S2.1); `builtin_tools(None, None, None, Some(root))` (the startup root is the temp
  project, so `file_read` reads the same `notes.txt` before S3 and after it, when it reads the working folder);
  `SandboxManager::with_defaults`, `set_confirmation_broker`; `ConfirmationBroker::pending_count(&self) -> usize`;
  `SandboxPolicy` (all fields `pub`); `crate::security::capabilities::Allowlist::Unrestricted`; `EventBus::subscribe()
  -> tokio::sync::broadcast::Receiver<SystemEvent>`.
- Produces: the test `reading_tools_raise_no_card_under_a_broker`. S5 extends ST-16 to `file_list` and `artifact_read`
  in its own slice (interfaces §4.4).

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the test.**

  ```rust
  // --- ST-16: reading never asks (storage design §12) ---

  /// ST-16: `file_read` and `read_result` are read-only and raise no card, with
  /// a broker attached and no confirmation list, so the set is the one derived
  /// from the annotations `builtin_tools` registers them with. `file_write`
  /// under the same policy does raise one, which is what makes the two "no
  /// card" findings mean something. The one-second timeout lets that card lapse
  /// unanswered, so nothing is written. A read that started asking would fail
  /// here in a second instead of hanging the suite.
  #[tokio::test]
  async fn reading_tools_raise_no_card_under_a_broker() {
      use crate::bus::EventBus;
      use crate::events::SystemEvent;
      use crate::security::capabilities::Allowlist;
      use crate::security::confirmation::ConfirmationBroker;
      use crate::security::sandbox::{SandboxManager, SandboxPolicy};
      use crate::test_util::GuardedProject;
      use crate::tools::ToolRegistry;
      use openalpaca_llm::ToolCall;

      let gp = GuardedProject::new();
      std::fs::write(gp.root.join("notes.txt"), "read me\n").unwrap();
      let registry = ToolRegistry::default();
      for tool in builtin_tools(None, None, None, Some(gp.root.clone())) {
          registry.register(tool).unwrap();
      }
      let bus = EventBus::default();
      let mut events = bus.subscribe();
      let mut sandbox = SandboxManager::with_defaults(Arc::new(registry), bus);
      let broker = Arc::new(ConfirmationBroker::new());
      sandbox.set_confirmation_broker(broker.clone());
      let policy = SandboxPolicy {
          agent_id: "research_agent".to_string(),
          allowed_capabilities: Allowlist::Unrestricted,
          denied_capabilities: vec![],
          require_confirmation_for: vec![],
          max_tool_calls: None,
          max_tool_runtime_secs: 60,
          stream_id: None,
          lane_key: None,
          confirmation_timeout_secs: Some(1),
          auto_approve: false,
          unattended: false,
      };
      let call = |name: &str, arguments: serde_json::Value| ToolCall {
          id: format!("tc-{name}"),
          name: name.to_string(),
          arguments,
      };
      let carded = |events: &mut tokio::sync::broadcast::Receiver<SystemEvent>| {
          let mut tools = Vec::new();
          while let Ok(event) = events.try_recv() {
              if let SystemEvent::ToolConfirmationRequested { tool_name, .. } = event {
                  tools.push(tool_name);
              }
          }
          tools
      };

      let read = sandbox
          .execute_tool(
              &call("file_read", serde_json::json!({"path": "notes.txt"})),
              &policy,
              &gp.ctx(),
          )
          .await;
      assert_eq!(read, Ok("read me\n".to_string()));
      // The tool's own refusal: the sandbox let the call through with no card,
      // and the call has no session to page from.
      let paged = sandbox
          .execute_tool(
              &call(
                  "read_result",
                  serde_json::json!({"result_ref": "file:results/000001-a1b2c3d4-shell_execute.txt"}),
              ),
              &policy,
              &gp.ctx(),
          )
          .await;
      assert_eq!(
          paged,
          Err("read_result is scoped to a session, and this call has none".to_string())
      );
      assert_eq!(carded(&mut events), Vec::<String>::new(), "a read raised a card");
      assert_eq!(broker.pending_count(), 0);

      let write = sandbox
          .execute_tool(
              &call("file_write", serde_json::json!({"path": "out.md", "content": "x"})),
              &policy,
              &gp.ctx(),
          )
          .await;
      assert!(write.is_err(), "the unanswered card lapses: {write:?}");
      assert_eq!(carded(&mut events), vec!["file_write".to_string()]);
      assert!(!gp.root.join("out.md").exists(), "an unanswered write never runs");
  }
  ```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run it.** `pgrep -x cargo`, then `cargo test -p openalpaca_core reading_tools_raise_no_card_under_a_broker`.
  Expected: **PASS (1 passed)**, about one second. ST-16 is already how the annotations read
  (`annotations_for_builtin`'s read-only arm), and this task pins it. A red run is shown by a mutation instead: move

  `assert_eq!(read, Ok(...))`. The read's card lapses and the call returns `Err` (a timed-out confirmation), and
  `carded` lists `file_read`. Revert the mutation (`git diff crates/openalpaca_core/src/tools/builtins/mod.rs` must
  then be empty).

- [ ] **Step 3: Minimal implementation.** None: the behaviour holds at HEAD plus S2.4. The test is the deliverable.

- [ ] **Step 4: Run.** `pgrep -x cargo`, then `cargo test -p openalpaca_core reading_tools_raise_no_card_under_a_broker`.
  Expected: **1 passed**. Neighbour: `cargo test -p openalpaca_core tools::builtins::tests` — expected 0 failed.

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit.**

  ```bash

  git commit -F - <<'EOF'

  Owner decision ST-16, storage design §12, Stage 2 slice S2: under a broker
  ```

   `Project` is never constructed"). The slice may not add one: the clippy baseline is 78 with `--all-targets`, and the

   `Project { root: &'a Path, replaces: bool }` with §4.2's two texts unchanged, in the commit that first constructs it,

   that enum is `pub` in a `pub mod` of the library. **Cross-slice consequence:** S4a's draft at `d484a56a` still
   expects the variant to pre-exist — its S2 consumes-row lists `Project { root, replaces }`, its file_write card
   constructs `WriteLanding::Project { root: &root, replaces }`, and its step 3b only *removes* `StartupFolder` — so
   S4a's 3b must also **add** `Project { root: &'a Path, replaces: bool }` with §4.2's two texts (`Writes {path} in the
   project folder {root}.` / `Replaces {path} in the project folder {root}; its current content is kept in this
   conversation's log.`) and a test of each, in that commit. (S4a.11 does both: its *Files* and Step 3b.)
2. **The sheet's §8.2 S2 flip list is incomplete.** Three more items break, all handled in S2:

3. **§1.2 reads `request_workspace_root` "non-empty" and `conversation_id` `Some(id)` as written.** S2 treats a blank
   value (`""` or whitespace only) of either as absent. A blank id is no conversation, so the call is refused
   `NoConversation`; otherwise every blank-id call would share `scratch/_unnamed` (`session_dir_name("")`). A blank
   root is no project — the sheet would make `"  "` a relative root and refuse it `NotAProject` — which is the rule
   `scope_from_context` (`tools/builtins/artifact_write.rs:58`, `Some(root) if !root.trim().is_empty()`) already
   applies to the same field, so a turn's working folder and the store its by-products go to never disagree about
   whether it has a project. This is the smallest departure; no slice is known to set a blank value.

  the GUI banner, the CLI prompt and the connector prompt, and the arguments carry the same path. Each escaped block
  carries its own count, which is the Gotcha's rule: the card's line counts the card's text, the surface's line the
  arguments, and the two can differ (`escape_hidden_line` shows a `\n` or `\t` in a path, which the JSON arguments
  show as `\n`/`\t` escapes and the surface does not count). S2 implements the sheet's text as specified, and S4a's

## Stage 2 — slice S3: the working folder

Draft for the Stage 2 plan, slice **S3** of `interfaces.md` §0: design rev 0.9 §10 and §16 Stage 2 step (3) — R26, R27,
R28, R44, the scratch folder, and R33 (§11). Read at `d484a56a` (`feat/markdown-memory`). Every `file:line` is from
that commit; **locate code by the quoted content**, because S1 and S2 land first and move lines.

**S3 is written against S1's and S2's surfaces, none of which exist at `d484a56a`.** It uses the names and signatures
`interfaces.md` fixes, and every region S1 or S2 writes is quoted from their drafts in this folder (`S1.md`, `S2.md`):
from S1 `helpers::FolderRules` (`Project` / `Plain`, `Project` carrying `#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]`
until its first caller), the three-argument resolvers `resolve_workspace_path(rel, root, rules)` /
`resolve_workspace_path_for_write(rel, root, rules)`, `tools::platform::{run_bounded, RunFailure, shell_command}`
(imported by `shell_execute.rs` and `registry/mod.rs`), `send.rs` as S1.5 leaves it (`SendTool { provider, db,
workspace_root }`, `send_tool(provider, db, workspace_root)`, one `locate(arguments, ctx)` → `resolve(file_path)` that
the body and `confirmation_preview` share, and `resolve` running `is_store_owned_path` / `is_store_owned_resolved`),
and S1's R45 kill tests (S1.10, S1.11); from S2 `ToolContext.conversation_id: Option<String>`, the module
`crates/openalpaca_core/src/tools/working_folder.rs` (`WorkingFolder { Project { root }, Scratch { dir,
conversation_id } }` with `path()` / `is_project()`, `WorkingFolderRefusal` and its `Display` sentences of §1.3,
`working_folder(ctx)`, its `mod tests` importing `GuardedProject` and `HomeStoreGuard`),
`tools::builtins::approval_preview::command_card(&WorkingFolder) -> String`, `shell_execute.rs`'s `mod preview_tests`
(S2.2), and `crate::test_util::GuardedProject` (`new()`, `ctx()`, `scratch_ctx()`, `home_root()`, fields `home`,
`project`, `root`; `ctx()` = owner `owner-test`, `request_workspace_root` and `workspace_id` = `root`,
`conversation_id` `conv-test`; `scratch_ctx()` = `conversation_id` `conv-test` only — S2's verifier dropped its owner; no S3 test needs one on a scratch context). If what S1 or
S2 landed differs from its draft, the implementer reconciles against what landed and records it in the slice's review.

### What this slice does

After S3 every tool that acts on files or runs a program acts in the **call's working folder**, read from its
context (R26): the registered project the turn carries, or — with no project — the conversation's own scratch
folder `~/.openalpaca/scratch/<session-id>/`, made private on first use and removed with the conversation, so one
conversation never sees another's files. `file_read` loses its boot-root field, `shell_execute` and command tools are
spawned with that folder as their working directory, and `send` resolves `file_path` there; a call with no context
(`execute`), a call with neither a project nor a conversation (R44), a project whose folder is gone (R27) and a
root no folder under `projects/` records are each refused with their one sentence before anything is read, made
or run — and the shell's card is not raised for them. Every path that runs a sandboxed tool now puts the turn's
conversation on the context (`ToolContext.conversation_id`, R44: main loop, file-skill tier, plugin skill, lead,
subagents; nested skills and plugin agents inherit it), and the model is told its working folder in one
`<working_folder>` line on the main loop, the file-skill tier, the lead and every subagent (R28). R32's read rule is
switched on (`.openalpaca` refused in a project, for `file_read` and `send`), the five home-store rules go from both
file tools and the two `state/` checks S1 gave `send` go too (R33), and
Round G's `read_back_path` goes with the root it pointed into (interfaces C7). **What S3 leaves alone** (interfaces
C1): `file_write` keeps its startup root and Round G's routing (`!Project || is_the_home_root(root)`) until S4a, so
in production — where both launchers start the daemon in the home store — a `file_write` on a project turn stays a
by-product, as §16 requires; its five-part result keeps four parts and part 4 becomes the fixed "nothing to check"
sentence. A run parked by `POST /v1/tasks` on a lane with no session is given the lane's session at dispatch (S3.13,
the lead's ruling R-T2), so it too works in a scratch folder; `NoConversation`'s sentence stays for a call that has
neither. No migration, no route, no request struct, no refusal code, no config key, no event variant, no GUI file.

### Order and why

The library first (S3.1), then each tool body, the read tool first because Round G's read-back path dies with its
root (S3.2), then R33's write half (S3.3), the shell (S3.4), command tools (S3.5) and `send` (S3.6) — which also
drops the two `state/` checks S1 gave it, so `is_store_owned_resolved` goes there, with its last caller. Removal with the
conversation is independent (S3.7 daemon, S3.8 CLI). The setters and the R28 note come last (S3.9–S3.11): a note that
names a folder the tools did not yet act in would tell the model something false, while tools that refuse
`NoConversation` until the setters land are only unreleased commits. S3.13 (the lead's ruling R-T2) comes after
S3.11: the dispatcher opens the lane's session for a run that has none, and its test proves the run's lead is told
that conversation's scratch folder, which needs S3.11's line. The slice gate, S3.12, runs after S3.13, the last task
(numbers kept). Every commit compiles and keeps its crate green.

| S3.2 `file_read` in the working folder | core | S1, S2, S3.1 |

### Rules every task carries

- Every command runs from the repository root, `/Users/tangyunpei/dev/OpenAlpaca`; every path in this draft is
  relative to it.
- **One cargo process at a time** — `pgrep -x cargo` prints nothing before each run. Per task
  `cargo test -p <crate> <filter>`, never `--workspace`. The offline memory eval is never a gate;
  `cargo check -p openalpaca_core --features live-eval --tests` is compile only.
- **Never `~/.openalpaca`.** Every test that touches a store holds its crate's guard: `crate::test_util::HomeStoreGuard`
  (core, daemon), `crate::test_util::EnvSandbox` (CLI). From this slice on the file tools and the shell act on real
  files: every test that reads, writes, lists or runs a command does it in a `GuardedProject` (core) or under a
  guarded tempdir home (daemon) — never in the repository, never in the process's current directory. A test that
  reaches `WorkingFolder::ensure` or `remove_scratch` holds a guard, because both act under the home store.
- **Processes:** every command a test this slice adds runs (`pwd -P`, `echo`) ends by itself in milliseconds and
  starts no child that could outlive it. S1's three R45 kill tests (`shell_execute.rs`'s two, `registry/tests.rs`'s
  one) are moved onto a `GuardedProject` context in S3.4 and S3.5 — they would otherwise be refused before they spawn
  — and keep S1's `KillOnFail` guard and `wait_until_gone` exactly (interfaces §3.3); after each run that includes
  them, `pgrep -fl '^sleep 30$'` prints nothing. No new `sleep` in any test command.
- No test reaches `localhost:11434`. No `&s[..n]` on a `str`. `std::env::set_var` only inside the guards.
  Snake_case sentence test names. Anchored edits only (the `Edit` tool, or `perl -pi -e` / Python with an
  exactly-once assertion) — never BSD `sed -i`.
- **Clippy baseline 78**; no task adds one. **docs/api:** nothing in S3 is read by `scripts/gen_api_docs.py` — no
  route request struct, no refusal code, no migration, no storage `lib.rs` re-export, no GUI `lib/api` export;
  `tools::working_folder` is a submodule of `tools`, and core's generated doc lists top-level modules only — so no
  task regenerates `docs/api`, and the slice gate runs `--check` to prove it.
- Commits: conventional prefix, a `Verified:` line naming the command and its result, last line
  `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Stage explicit paths only (`tasks/deps-upgrade/` is
  another session's and stays untracked).

```rust
                if reason.contains("is not a folder of its own")),
```

  (c) Add to the `impl WorkingFolder` block (beside S2's `path` and `is_project`):

```rust
    /// The folder, ready to act in (storage design §10, R26). A scratch
    /// folder is made on first use — `<home>/scratch` and the conversation's
    /// folder, one level at a time, each private (0700 on unix) and each
    /// checked to be a folder of its own before the next is made, so a link
    /// planted at either name is refused and nothing is made through it. A
    /// project's root must still be a directory. Every tool that acts in the
    /// folder calls this first; the approval previews and the R28 note never
    /// do, so a conversation that never acts gets no folder.
    pub fn ensure(&self) -> Result<&Path, WorkingFolderRefusal> {
        match self {
            WorkingFolder::Project { root } => {
                if root.is_dir() {
                    Ok(root.as_path())
                } else {
                    Err(WorkingFolderRefusal::Unavailable {
                        reason: format!("the project folder {} is not a directory", root.display()),
                    })
                }
            }
            WorkingFolder::Scratch { dir, .. } => {
                let unavailable = |reason: String| WorkingFolderRefusal::Unavailable { reason };
                let scratch = dir
                    .parent()
                    .ok_or_else(|| unavailable(format!("{} has no parent folder", dir.display())))?;
                // The home store itself is made the way every store writer
                // makes it; only the two levels below it are private.
                if let Some(home) = scratch.parent() {
                    std::fs::create_dir_all(home)
                        .map_err(|e| unavailable(format!("{}: {e}", home.display())))?;
                }
                make_private_dir(scratch).map_err(unavailable)?;
                make_private_dir(dir).map_err(unavailable)?;
                Ok(dir.as_path())
            }
        }
    }
```

```rust
/// `<home>/scratch/<session_dir_name(conversation_id)>` — the working folder
/// of a conversation with no project (storage design §10), as a path:
/// nothing is created. `session_dir_name` makes the id one safe path segment,
/// the mapping `sessions/<id>/` uses.
pub fn scratch_dir(conversation_id: &str) -> anyhow::Result<PathBuf> {
    Ok(store::home_root()?
        .join(ContentKind::Scratch.dir_name())
        .join(session_dir_name(conversation_id)))
}

/// Removes a conversation's scratch folder: it goes with the conversation
/// (storage design §10). `Ok(false)` when nothing stood at its name. Never
/// follows a link — a link (or a file) at the folder's name is removed
/// itself, a directory with everything in it.
pub fn remove_scratch(conversation_id: &str) -> std::io::Result<bool> {
    let dir = scratch_dir(conversation_id)
        .map_err(|e| std::io::Error::other(format!("{e:#}")))?;
    let meta = match std::fs::symlink_metadata(&dir) {
        Ok(meta) => meta,
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(false),
        Err(e) => return Err(e),
    };
    if meta.is_dir() {
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir)?;
    } else if meta.file_type().is_symlink() {
        // A link to a directory is unlinked as a file on unix and taken by
        // `remove_dir` on Windows; neither follows it.
        std::fs::remove_file(&dir).or_else(|_| std::fs::remove_dir(&dir))?;
    } else {
        std::fs::remove_file(&dir)?;
    }
    Ok(true)
}

/// R28 (storage design §10): the one line a turn's context carries about
/// where its file tools and commands act — the project's folder, the
/// conversation's scratch folder, or, for a project whose folder is gone or
/// that no folder under `projects/` records, the refusal's own sentence, so
/// the model knows before it tries. `None` when there is nothing to name
/// (no context, neither a project nor a conversation, an unreadable store).
/// Pure, like [`working_folder`]: it creates nothing.
pub fn working_folder_note(ctx: &ToolContext) -> Option<String> {
    let line = match working_folder(ctx) {
        Ok(WorkingFolder::Project { root }) => format!(
            "Your working folder is the project folder {}. Paths in file_read, file_list, \
             file_write, file_edit and send are relative to it, and a shell command starts in it.",
            root.display()
        ),
        Ok(WorkingFolder::Scratch { dir, .. }) => format!(
            "This conversation has no project. Your working folder is its scratch folder {}: \
             paths in file_read, file_list and send are relative to it, and a shell command \
             starts in it. file_write saves a by-product in OpenAlpaca's artifact store instead.",
            dir.display()
        ),
        Err(
            refusal @ (WorkingFolderRefusal::ProjectMissing { .. }
            | WorkingFolderRefusal::NotAProject { .. }),
        ) => refusal.to_string(),
        Err(_) => return None,
    };
    Some(format!("<working_folder>{line}</working_folder>"))
}

/// One level of a scratch folder: made private when absent (never
/// recursively), then required to be a directory of its own — a link or a
/// file standing at its name is refused, not followed.
fn make_private_dir(path: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut builder = std::fs::DirBuilder::new();
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        use std::os::unix::fs::DirBuilderExt;
        builder.mode(0o700);
    }
    match builder.create(path) {
        Ok(()) => {}
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists => {}
        Err(e) => return Err(format!("{} could not be made: {e}", path.display())),
    }
    let meta = std::fs::symlink_metadata(path).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    if meta.is_dir() {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(format!(
            "{} is not a folder of its own: a link or a file stands at its name",
            path.display()
        ))
    }
}
```

  (`FolderRules::of` below constructs `Project` in the library, so the allowance is no longer needed and its comment

```rust
impl FolderRules {
    /// R32's rules for a working folder: [`FolderRules::Project`] in a
    /// project, [`FolderRules::Plain`] in a conversation's scratch folder.
    pub(super) fn of(folder: &WorkingFolder) -> Self {
        if folder.is_project() {
            FolderRules::Project
        } else {
            FolderRules::Plain
        }
    }
}

/// R26 (storage design §10): the call's working folder, ready to act in — a
/// scratch folder is made on first use (`WorkingFolder::ensure`) — and R32's
/// rules for it. `Err` is the refusal's own sentence (R26's no context, R27's
/// missing project, R44's neither project nor conversation): nothing was
/// read, made or run.
pub(super) fn acting_folder(ctx: &ToolContext) -> Result<(PathBuf, FolderRules), String> {
    let folder = working_folder(ctx).map_err(|refusal| refusal.to_string())?;
    let root = folder
        .ensure()
        .map_err(|refusal| refusal.to_string())?
        .to_path_buf();
    Ok((root, FolderRules::of(&folder)))
}
```

  (b) `file_ops.rs` — replace everything from `// --- file_read ---` through the closing `}` of
  `pub(super) fn file_read_tool(…) -> RegisteredTool { … }` (S1 changed only the resolver call inside it) with:

```rust
// --- file_read ---

/// Reads one file of the call's working folder (storage design §10, R26):
/// the project's root, or the conversation's scratch folder. It holds no
/// root of its own — the folder is the call's, read from its context.
struct FileReadTool;

#[async_trait]
impl BuiltInTool for FileReadTool {
    /// R26: a call reached with no context names no folder, and is refused
    /// rather than read from the daemon's own directory.
    async fn execute(&self, _arguments: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<String, String> {
        Err(WorkingFolderRefusal::NoContext.to_string())
    }

    async fn execute_with_context(
        &self,
        arguments: &serde_json::Value,
        ctx: &ToolContext,
    ) -> Result<String, String> {
        let path = arguments
            .get("path")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
            .ok_or_else(|| "Missing required parameter: path".to_string())?;

        // R26, R27, R44: the project's folder, or the conversation's scratch
        // folder; a missing project, or a call with neither, is refused with
        // its sentence before anything is read.
        let (root, rules) = acting_folder(ctx)?;
        // R31: relative, no `..`, resolved whole and under the root. R32 in a
        // project: nothing under a `.openalpaca` folder. `.git` and `.env`
        // are read like any file — reading never asks (ST-16).
        let full_path = resolve_workspace_path(path, &root, rules)?;

        // Guard against OOM: reject files larger than 10 MB
        let metadata = tokio::fs::metadata(&full_path)
            .await
            .map_err(|e| format!("Cannot access file '{}': {}", path, e))?;
        if metadata.len() > MAX_FILE_READ_SIZE {
            return Err(format!(
                "File '{}' is {} bytes, exceeding the {} byte limit",
                path,
                metadata.len(),
                MAX_FILE_READ_SIZE
            ));
        }

        tokio::fs::read_to_string(&full_path)
            .await
            .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to read file '{}': {}", path, e))
    }
}

pub(super) fn file_read_tool() -> RegisteredTool {
    RegisteredTool {
        definition: ToolDefinition {
            name: "file_read".to_string(),
            description: "Read a file from the working folder — the project, or this \
                conversation's scratch folder. Returns its full content as UTF-8; files over \
                10MB are refused. Paths are relative to the working folder; '..' is refused, \
                and in a project so is any .openalpaca folder. Reading never asks. For binary \
                files, use shell_execute."
                .to_string(),
            parameters: serde_json::json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "The file, relative to the working folder (e.g. 'src/main.rs', 'config/settings.toml'). Absolute paths and '..' are refused."
                    }
                },
                "required": ["path"]
            }),
            strict: Some(true),
            input_examples: Some(vec![
                serde_json::json!({"path": "src/main.rs"}),
            ]),
        },
        backend: ToolBackend::BuiltIn(Arc::new(FileReadTool)),
        provides_capabilities: vec!["file_read".into()],
        exempt_from_timeout: false,
        annotations: annotations_for_builtin("file_read"),
        version: env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION").to_string(),
        author: "builtin".to_string(),
        created_at: chrono::Utc::now(),
    }
}
```

```rust
use crate::tools::platform::{RunFailure, run_bounded, shell_command};
use crate::tools::registry::{BuiltInTool, RegisteredTool, ToolBackend, ToolContext};
use crate::tools::working_folder::{WorkingFolderRefusal, working_folder};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use openalpaca_llm::ToolDefinition;
use std::path::Path;
use std::sync::Arc;

use super::annotations_for_builtin;
use super::approval_preview::command_card;
use super::helpers::acting_folder;

/// The defence-in-depth bound on one command. The primary timeout is the
/// SandboxManager's (default 60s, `daemon_config.execution.agent_defaults.
/// max_tool_runtime_secs`); this one holds when the sandbox layer is bypassed
/// (e.g. ToolRegistry used directly). Either way the command and what it
/// started are killed (R45, `run_bounded`).
const SHELL_TIMEOUT_SECS: u64 = 300;

struct ShellExecuteTool;

impl ShellExecuteTool {
    /// Run `command` with `folder` as its working directory (storage design
    /// §10, R26) and shape its output for the model.
    async fn run_in(&self, command: &str, folder: &Path) -> Result<String, String> {
        // Note: InputSanitizer blocks backticks, $( command substitution, and
        // newlines/carriage returns in arguments. Shell chaining (;, &&, ||) and
        // pipes are intentionally allowed — the agent constructs the full command
        // string (see security::sanitizer::check_string_safety). The folder is a
        // working directory, not a confinement (ST-14): an absolute path, `~`
        // or `cd ..` reaches anywhere the user can.
        let mut cmd = shell_command(command);
        cmd.current_dir(folder);
        let output = run_bounded(cmd, std::time::Duration::from_secs(SHELL_TIMEOUT_SECS))
            .await
            .map_err(|failure| match failure {
                RunFailure::TimedOut => format!("Command timed out after {SHELL_TIMEOUT_SECS}s"),
                RunFailure::Spawn(e) | RunFailure::Io(e) => {
                    format!("Failed to execute command: {e}")
                }
            })?;

        // Cap output size to prevent memory pressure from commands producing
        // unbounded stdout/stderr (e.g. `find /` or `yes`).
        const MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES: usize = 512 * 1024; // 512 KB
        let stdout_raw = &output.stdout;
        let stderr_raw = &output.stderr;
        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&stdout_raw[..stdout_raw.len().min(MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES)]);
        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&stderr_raw[..stderr_raw.len().min(MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES)]);

        if output.status.success() {
            let mut result = String::new();
            if !stdout.is_empty() {
                result.push_str(&stdout);
            }
            if !stderr.is_empty() {
                if !result.is_empty() {
                    result.push_str("\n\n");
                }
                result.push_str("STDERR:\n");
                result.push_str(&stderr);
            }
            Ok(result)
        } else {
            Err(format!(
                "Command failed (exit {}):\n{}{}",
                output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1),
                stdout,
                if stderr.is_empty() {
                    String::new()
                } else {
                    format!("\nSTDERR:\n{}", stderr)
                }
            ))
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl BuiltInTool for ShellExecuteTool {
    /// R26: a command runs in its conversation's working folder, and a call
    /// reached with no context names none — refused, never run in the
    /// daemon's own directory.
    async fn execute(&self, _arguments: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<String, String> {
        Err(WorkingFolderRefusal::NoContext.to_string())
    }

    async fn execute_with_context(
        &self,
        arguments: &serde_json::Value,
        ctx: &ToolContext,
    ) -> Result<String, String> {
        let command = arguments
            .get("command")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
            .ok_or_else(|| "Missing required parameter: command".to_string())?;
        // R26, R27, R44: the project's folder, or the conversation's scratch
        // folder made on first use; a missing project, or a call with
        // neither, is refused here with its sentence and nothing runs.
        let (folder, _) = acting_folder(ctx)?;
        self.run_in(command, &folder).await
    }

    /// R34 (ST-14): the card names the folder the command starts in. A call
    /// the body would refuse — no conversation, a missing project — raises
    /// no card: its sentence is the answer (R27).
    async fn confirmation_preview(
        &self,
        _arguments: &serde_json::Value,
        ctx: &ToolContext,
    ) -> Result<Option<String>, String> {
        match working_folder(ctx) {
            Ok(folder) => Ok(Some(command_card(&folder))),
            Err(refusal) => Err(refusal.to_string()),
        }
    }
}

pub(super) fn shell_execute_tool() -> RegisteredTool {
    RegisteredTool {
        definition: ToolDefinition {
            name: "shell_execute".to_string(),
            description: "Execute a single shell command and return its output. The command \
                starts in the working folder — the project, or this conversation's scratch \
                folder — and every command asks first; an approved command runs as you and can \
                reach files outside that folder. Subshells ($(), backticks) and embedded \
                newlines are blocked for security; shell chaining (;, &&, ||) and pipes are \
                allowed. Timeout: 300 seconds. Output is truncated to 512KB. Use for system \
                operations, package management, git commands, build tools, and any operations \
                not covered by other tools."
                .to_string(),
            parameters: serde_json::json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "command": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "The shell command to execute (single command only, no chaining)"
                    }
                },
                "required": ["command"]
            }),
            strict: Some(true),
            input_examples: Some(vec![
                serde_json::json!({"command": "ls -la /tmp"}),
                serde_json::json!({"command": "grep -rn 'TODO' src/"}),
            ]),
        },
        backend: ToolBackend::BuiltIn(Arc::new(ShellExecuteTool)),
        provides_capabilities: vec!["shell_execute".into()],
        exempt_from_timeout: false,
        annotations: annotations_for_builtin("shell_execute"),
        version: env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION").to_string(),
        author: "builtin".to_string(),
        created_at: chrono::Utc::now(),
    }
```

  (d) Replace the whole of `async fn execute_command` (S1.11's, whose `run_bounded` match keeps interfaces §3.2's
  texts `Command timed out after {timeout_secs}s` and `Failed to execute command: {e}`; the replacement keeps them)
  with:

```rust
/// Execute a command backend tool call in the call's working folder
/// (storage design §10, R26): the template's placeholders are substituted
/// and checked first — a missing argument is named as such whatever the
/// context — then the folder is resolved, and a call with none is refused.
async fn execute_command(
    command: &str,
    args_template: Option<&str>,
    timeout_secs: u64,
    arguments: &serde_json::Value,
    ctx: Option<&ToolContext>,
) -> Result<String, String> {
    let mut full_args = args_template.unwrap_or("").to_string();
    if let Some(obj) = arguments.as_object() {
        for (key, value) in obj {
            let replacement = match value {
                serde_json::Value::String(s) => s.clone(),
                other => other.to_string(),
            };
            let escaped = shell_escape::escape(replacement.into());
            full_args = full_args.replace(&format!("{{{}}}", key), &escaped);
        }
    }

    // Check for unsubstituted {param_name} placeholders.
    // These indicate missing required arguments and would produce malformed commands.
    if let Some(start) = full_args.find('{')
        && let Some(end) = full_args[start..].find('}')
    {
        let placeholder = &full_args[start..start + end + 1];
        return Err(format!(
            "Command template has unsubstituted placeholder '{}' — \
             the required parameter was not provided in tool arguments",
            placeholder
        ));
    }

    let folder = command_folder(ctx)?;
    let timeout = std::time::Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs);
    let full_command = format!("{} {}", command, full_args);
    let mut cmd = shell_command(&full_command);
    cmd.current_dir(&folder);
    // R45 (storage design §11): killed with the processes it started when
    // its time runs out or its call is dropped.
    let output = match run_bounded(cmd, timeout).await {
        Ok(output) => output,
        Err(RunFailure::TimedOut) => {
            return Err(format!("Command timed out after {}s", timeout_secs));
        }
        Err(RunFailure::Spawn(e) | RunFailure::Io(e)) => {
            return Err(format!("Failed to execute command: {}", e));
        }
    };

    // Cap output size to prevent memory pressure from commands producing
    // unbounded stdout/stderr.
    const MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES: usize = 512 * 1024; // 512 KB
    let stdout_raw = &output.stdout;
    let stderr_raw = &output.stderr;
    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&stdout_raw[..stdout_raw.len().min(MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES)]);
    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&stderr_raw[..stderr_raw.len().min(MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES)]);

    if output.status.success() {
        Ok(stdout.to_string())
    } else {
        Err(format!(
            "Command failed (exit {}): {}{}",
            output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1),
            stdout,
            stderr
        ))
    }
}

/// The folder a command tool runs in: the call's working folder, made ready
/// (R26); a call with no context, or one the folder refuses, gets the
/// refusal's sentence and runs nothing.
fn command_folder(ctx: Option<&ToolContext>) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    let ctx = ctx.ok_or_else(|| WorkingFolderRefusal::NoContext.to_string())?;
    let folder = working_folder(ctx).map_err(|refusal| refusal.to_string())?;
    folder
        .ensure()
        .map(Path::to_path_buf)
        .map_err(|refusal| refusal.to_string())
}
```

  (`full_args[start..start + end + 1]` is unchanged from HEAD and cuts at the ASCII braces `find` located — both
  ends are character boundaries.)

```rust
/// [`acting_folder`] for an approval card (R34): the folder named, never
/// made — a conversation that never acts gets no scratch folder, and a file
/// in a scratch folder not made yet does not exist either.
pub(super) fn named_folder(ctx: &ToolContext) -> Result<(PathBuf, FolderRules), String> {
    let folder = working_folder(ctx).map_err(|refusal| refusal.to_string())?;
    Ok((folder.path().to_path_buf(), FolderRules::of(&folder)))
}
```

    through the closing `}` of `fn resolve` — with:

```rust
    /// R23: the file a `send` with action `file` delivers, named by
    /// `file_path` or by `artifact_id` (exactly one). The card and the send
    /// locate it the same way, so the card names what is sent; only the send
    /// makes a scratch folder (`make_folder`), the card names it (R34).
    fn locate(
        &self,
        arguments: &serde_json::Value,
        ctx: &ToolContext,
        make_folder: bool,
    ) -> Result<SendFile, String> {
        let file_path = arguments.get("file_path").and_then(|v| v.as_str());
        let artifact_id = arguments.get("artifact_id").and_then(|v| v.as_str());
        match (file_path, artifact_id) {
            (Some(_), Some(_)) => Err("Give file_path or artifact_id, not both.".to_string()),
            (None, None) => Err(format!(
                "Missing required parameter: file_path or artifact_id{FILE_ONLY}"
            )),
            (Some(file_path), None) => self.resolve(file_path, ctx, make_folder),
            (None, Some(id)) => self.artifact(id, ctx),
        }
    }

    /// R23 and R26 (storage design §10–§11): the file `file_path` names in the
    /// call's working folder — the project, or the conversation's scratch
    /// folder — resolved as `file_read` resolves one: relative, no `..`, every
    /// component (the last included) canonicalized and under the folder, and
    /// in a project nothing under a `.openalpaca` folder (R32). No home-store
    /// rule binds it (R33): the store lies under no working folder. A call the
    /// folder refuses (no context, no conversation, a missing project) gets
    /// that refusal's sentence, and nothing is sent.
    fn resolve(
        &self,
        file_path: &str,
        ctx: &ToolContext,
        make_folder: bool,
    ) -> Result<SendFile, String> {
        let (root, rules) = if make_folder {
            acting_folder(ctx)?
        } else {
            named_folder(ctx)?
        };
        let resolved = resolve_workspace_path(file_path, &root, rules)?;
        let metadata = std::fs::metadata(&resolved)
            .map_err(|e| format!("Cannot access file '{file_path}': {e}"))?;
        if !metadata.is_file() {
            return Err(format!("'{file_path}' is not a file."));
        }
        let path = resolved.into_os_string().into_string().map_err(|_| {
            format!(
                "'{file_path}' resolves to a path that is not UTF-8 text, which no channel can send."
            )
        })?;
        Ok(SendFile {
            path,
            bytes: metadata.len(),
            mime_type: None,
        })
    }
```

```rust
/// Remove a deleted conversation's scratch folder — `~/.openalpaca/scratch/<id>/`,
/// its working folder when it had no project (storage design §10) — so no
/// later conversation can see its files. Shared with the project delete
/// (`POST /v1/workspaces/purge`). Best effort, like the log: the rows are
/// gone and the caller's answer stands, so a failure is one WARN naming the
/// folder; a conversation that never ran a file tool or a command has none.
/// Clearing a conversation (`routes/chat.rs`) and archiving one keep it.
pub(crate) fn remove_scratch_folder(id: &str) {
    use openalpaca_core::tools::working_folder::{remove_scratch, scratch_dir};
    if let Err(e) = remove_scratch(id) {
        let folder = scratch_dir(id)
            .map_or_else(|_| format!("scratch/{id}"), |dir| dir.display().to_string());
        tracing::warn!(
```

```rust
fn orchestrator_for(registry: Arc<crate::tools::ToolRegistry>) -> Orchestrator {
    orchestrator_with(registry, None)
}

/// [`orchestrator_for`], with a database — what reads the turn's
/// conversation (storage design §10, R44).
fn orchestrator_with(
    registry: Arc<crate::tools::ToolRegistry>,
    db: Option<openalpaca_storage::Database>,
) -> Orchestrator {
    let bus = EventBus::default();
    let sandbox = Arc::new(SandboxManager::with_defaults(registry.clone(), bus.clone()));
    Orchestrator::new(
        Arc::new(SharedContext::new()),
        Arc::new(LaneManager::new()),
        bus,
        crate::middleware::prompt::SystemPersona::default(),
        None,
        LoopConfig::default(),
        Arc::new(SecurityGate::new(sandbox)),
        registry,
        db,

        Arc::new(skill_router::SkillRouter::new(0.65, 0.45)),
        Arc::new(ArcSwap::from_pointee(DaemonConfig::default())),
    )
}
```

```rust
// ── R44 (storage design §10): the conversation reaches a plugin skill's tools ──

/// Keeps the context the one call it served was handed.
struct RecordsCtx(Arc<Mutex<Option<crate::tools::registry::ToolContext>>>);

#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl BuiltInTool for RecordsCtx {
    async fn execute(&self, _arguments: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<String, String> {
        Err("needs context".to_string())
    }
    async fn execute_with_context(
        &self,
        _arguments: &serde_json::Value,
        ctx: &crate::tools::registry::ToolContext,
    ) -> Result<String, String> {
        *self.0.lock().unwrap() = Some(ctx.clone());
        Ok("recorded".to_string())
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_plugin_skills_tool_calls_carry_the_turns_conversation() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let db = openalpaca_storage::Database::open(&dir.path().join("test.db")).unwrap();
    let session = openalpaca_storage::ConversationRepository::new(&db)
        .get_or_create_active_session("test:cli", "cli", None)
        .unwrap();
    let seen = Arc::new(Mutex::new(None));
    let registry = registry(true);
    registry
        .register(RegisteredTool {
            definition: openalpaca_llm::ToolDefinition {
                name: "record_ctx".to_string(),
                description: "record_ctx".to_string(),
                parameters: serde_json::json!({"type": "object"}),
                strict: None,
                input_examples: None,
            },
            backend: ToolBackend::BuiltIn(Arc::new(RecordsCtx(seen.clone()))),
            provides_capabilities: vec![],
            exempt_from_timeout: false,
            annotations: None,
            version: "test-0.0.0".into(),
            author: "test".into(),
            created_at: Utc::now(),
        })
        .unwrap();
    let orch = orchestrator_with(Arc::new(registry), Some(db));
    let stub = Arc::new(StubPluginSkill {
        tool: "record_ctx".to_string(),
        invoked: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),
        outcome: Arc::new(Mutex::new(None)),
    });
    let mut fm = SkillFrontmatter {
        name: "acme-search".to_string(),
        ..Default::default()
    };
    fm.tools.allow = vec!["record_ctx".to_string()];

    run_plugin_skill(&orch, fm, stub.clone())
        .await
        .expect("the skill runs");

    assert_eq!(
        stub.outcome.lock().unwrap().clone(),
        Some(Ok("recorded".to_string()))
    );
    let ctx = seen.lock().unwrap().clone().expect("the tool ran");
    assert_eq!(ctx.conversation_id.as_deref(), Some(session.id.as_str()));
}
```

```rust
/// R44 + R28 (storage design §10), the lead: a run started from a
/// conversation with no project is told that conversation's scratch folder
/// after its objective — the line is read from the lead's own tool context,
/// so naming the conversation proves the context carries it — and a run
/// with neither a project nor a conversation is told nothing.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_lead_with_no_project_is_told_its_conversations_scratch_folder() {
    let home = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let home_root = home.path().canonicalize().unwrap();
    let _guard = crate::test_util::HomeStoreGuard::set(&home_root);
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let db = openalpaca_storage::Database::open(&dir.path().join("test.db")).unwrap();

    let messages = lead_first_request(&db, Some("conv-lead")).await;

    let folder = home_root.join("scratch").join("conv-lead");
    let objective = messages
        .iter()
        .position(|m| m.content == "Book the Alfama hotel")
        .expect("the objective");
    let at = messages
        .iter()
        .position(|m| {
            m.content.starts_with("<working_folder>This conversation has no project.")
                && m.content.contains(&folder.display().to_string())
        })
        .unwrap_or_else(|| {
            panic!(
                "no working-folder note: {:?}",
                messages.iter().map(|m| &m.content).collect::<Vec<_>>()
            )
        });
    assert_eq!(at, objective + 1, "with no chat state, the line follows the objective");
    assert!(!home_root.join("scratch").exists(), "a note makes no folder");

    let none = lead_first_request(&db, None).await;
    assert!(
        !none.iter().any(|m| m.content.starts_with("<working_folder>")),
        "a run with neither a project nor a conversation is told nothing"
    );
}

/// Tells the lead's rounds from a subagent's, as `LeadAndSubagentProvider`
/// does, and keeps the message list of every subagent request.
struct RecordsTheSubagent {
    lead: std::sync::Mutex<std::collections::VecDeque<openalpaca_llm::ChatResponse>>,
    subagent_requests: std::sync::Mutex<Vec<Vec<openalpaca_llm::ChatMessage>>>,
}

#[async_trait]
impl openalpaca_llm::LlmProvider for RecordsTheSubagent {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        "records-the-subagent"
    }
    fn supports_tools(&self) -> bool {
        true
    }
    async fn chat(
        &self,
        request: openalpaca_llm::ChatRequest,
    ) -> Result<openalpaca_llm::ChatResponse, openalpaca_llm::LlmError> {
        let is_subagent = request
            .messages
            .first()
            .is_some_and(|m| m.content.contains("You are a subagent"));
        if is_subagent {
            self.subagent_requests
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())
                .push(request.messages.as_ref().clone());
            return Ok(scripted_response("seventeen", vec![]));
        }
        let next = self
            .lead
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())
            .pop_front();
        Ok(next.unwrap_or_else(|| scripted_response("done", vec![])))
    }
}

    shared
        .agent_registry
        .register_template(crate::test_util::template_from_agent(&worker));
    let provider = Arc::new(RecordsTheSubagent {
        lead: std::sync::Mutex::new(
            vec![
                scripted_response(
                    "",
                    vec![openalpaca_llm::ToolCall {
                        id: "call-1".to_string(),
                        name: "spawn_subagent".to_string(),
                        arguments: serde_json::json!({
                            "agent_id": "worker",
                            "objective": "count the alpacas",
                        }),
                    }],
                ),
                scripted_response(
                    "",
                    vec![openalpaca_llm::ToolCall {
                        id: "call-2".to_string(),
                        name: "wait_for_subagents".to_string(),
                        arguments: serde_json::json!({}),
                    }],
                ),
                scripted_response("all done", vec![]),
            ]
            .into(),
        ),
        subagent_requests: std::sync::Mutex::new(Vec::new()),
    });
    let router = LlmRouter::single_provider(

        "task-1",

        Arc::new(crate::compose::ComposeEngine::new(16)),

        false,

    .await;
    assert!(result.success, "finish: {:?}", result.loop_result.finish_reason);

    let requests = provider.subagent_requests.lock().unwrap().clone();
    assert_eq!(requests.len(), 1, "the subagent answered in one round");
    let messages = &requests[0];
    let folder = home_root.join("scratch").join("conv-sub");
    let note = &messages[messages.len() - 2].content;
    assert!(
        note.starts_with("<working_folder>This conversation has no project.")

    assert!(

}
```

```rust
/// Storage design §10, R44 and the lead's ruling R-T2: a run dispatched with
/// no turn on a lane that has no session — one parked by `POST /v1/tasks`
/// and started later — is given the lane's session at dispatch, opened there,
/// so it has a conversation and a session log, and its lead is told that
/// conversation's scratch folder. Before R-T2 the row carried no session and
/// every file tool and command of the run was refused `NoConversation`.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_run_on_a_lane_with_no_session_gets_one_and_works_in_its_scratch_folder() {
    let home = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let home_root = home.path().canonicalize().unwrap();
    let _guard = crate::test_util::HomeStoreGuard::set(&home_root);
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let db = Database::open(&dir.path().join("test.db")).unwrap();
    let repo = openalpaca_storage::ConversationRepository::new(&db);
    assert!(repo.active_session_id("user1:cli").unwrap().is_none());

    let requests = Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
    let router = Arc::new(openalpaca_llm::LlmRouter::single_provider(
        Arc::new(RecordingLeadMock {
            requests: requests.clone(),
        }),
        openalpaca_llm::ProviderType::Anthropic,
        "mock-model".to_string(),
    ));
    let dispatcher = setup_with_specific_router_and_db(
        vec![make_agent("lead-01", vec!["orchestration"])],
        DaemonConfig::default(),
        db.clone(),
        router,
    );
    let outcome = dispatcher
        .dispatch_lead_agent(
            "Tidy the notes",
            "Parked run".to_string(),
            "user1",
            "user1:cli",
            "cli",
            MemoryScopeContext::global_only(),
            None,
            false,
        )
        .unwrap();

    let task = openalpaca_storage::repository::TaskRepository::new(&db)
        .get(&outcome.task_id)
        .unwrap()
        .expect("the row is persisted at dispatch");
    let session = task
        .session_id
        .clone()
        .expect("the dispatch opened a session for the lane");
    assert_eq!(
        repo.active_session_id("user1:cli").unwrap().as_deref(),
        Some(session.as_str()),
        "the run's session is the lane's active one"
    );

    let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(5);
    let first = loop {
        if let Some(first) = requests.lock().unwrap().first().cloned() {
            break first;
        }
        assert!(
            tokio::time::Instant::now() < deadline,
            "timed out waiting for the lead's request"
        );
        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
    };
    let scratch = home_root.join("scratch").join(&session);
    assert!(
        first.iter().any(|m| {
            m.content.starts_with("<working_folder>This conversation has no project.")
                && m.content.contains(&scratch.display().to_string())
        }),
        "the lead is told its conversation's scratch folder: {:?}",
        first.iter().map(|m| &m.content).collect::<Vec<_>>()
    );
    assert!(!scratch.exists(), "a note makes no folder");
}
```

## Stage 2 — slice S4a: result files (pointer rows, migration 004, `file_write` writes the real file)

Draft for the lead, read at `d484a56a` (`feat/markdown-memory`). Every task assumes S1, S2 and S3 have landed exactly
as `interfaces.md` sheets them; where a step edits code those slices write, the step says what it expects to find and
gives the whole function as it must read afterwards. Line numbers below are HEAD's and will have moved: **locate every
edit by the content quoted**.

### What this slice does

A file an agent writes into its project becomes the user's real file, and OpenAlpaca keeps only a **pointer row** to
it (ST-12): `file_assets` gains `in_project` (migration `004_project_files.sql`, whose rebuilt address index lets a
result file share a path with a by-product's or an upload's address), and `ArtifactStore::record_project_file` (R35)
inserts or updates that row — origin `produced`, status `ready`, no `artifact_versions` row, nothing under
`.versions/`, never through `put`. Every store reader leaves such a row alone or reads it through the resolver under
its project root: `put`'s identity scan and name reservation, the sweep and the run counts skip it; the read-time
check refreshes its hash and size and records no version, and clears `missing_since` when the file is found again
(R37); the project delete takes its row and never its file (ST-19, C13), and the re-point's second prefix (built in
Stage 1) moves its address. The pre-edit copy moves to its own module and is judged against the call's project instead
of the daemon's startup folder (ST-17), and refuses to replace a file where no copy can be kept (R46). `file_write`
then loses its startup root: in a project it writes the real file (R32's `.git`/`.openalpaca` rule on, ST-17's copy
first, then the row; a row that fails is reported, R36), with no project it saves a by-product as Round G built, and
its approval card says which (R34) from the same plan the write follows. The run's count, chips and connector delivery
read by-products only, and the completion report names the result files in one runtime line (R38). On the wire,
`artifact_written`, `GET /v1/artifacts` and `GET /v1/artifacts/{id}` carry `in_project` and `openable`, the list takes
`?in_project=`, and `POST /v1/files/{id}/open` refuses a result file of a kind the store does not keep
(`409 OPEN_NOT_OFFERED`, ST-18). Open, the file content route and `send` by `artifact_id` read a result file through
the resolver under its project (R37). R39's seven tests are written against R35's method and assert the user's bytes and
modification time. `send` by `artifact_id` also refuses another project's by-product with `artifact_read`'s
sentence (S4a.17, the lead's ruling R-T3), a result file named as a chat attachment is refused with that tool's
sentence (S4a.18, R-T8), and `GET /v1/status`'s `produced_bytes` counts by-products only (S4a.6, R-T9). S4a.11 lands
last (R-T1): every reader that guards a result file is in place before `file_write` writes one. The app's surfaces are S6a's; nothing under `apps/openalpaca-gui/` changes here.

### Preconditions — what S1, S2 and S3 leave (checked against slices S1, S2 and S3 of this plan)

The tasks below compile only against this state. If a sibling slice landed a different name, use the sibling's name
and record it in the slice's review; do not re-create anything listed here.

| From | What S4a relies on |
|---|---|
| S1 | `helpers::FolderRules::{Project, Plain}` (`Project` with `#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]` until S3's first caller removes it); `resolve_workspace_path_for_write(relative_path: &str, workspace_root: &Path, rules: FolderRules) -> Result<PathBuf, String>` resolving the leaf when an entry stands there and refusing `.git` (write) and `.openalpaca` under `FolderRules::Project` with interfaces §2's sentences (`.openalpaca` is checked first); `file_ops.rs` test `a_write_through_a_link_out_of_the_root_is_refused` (renamed from `a_symlink_out_of_the_workspace_is_not_imaged`, on `Bench`, `bench.work.path()`); in `tools/builtins/mod.rs` the private `fn startup_root(workspace_root: Option<PathBuf>) -> PathBuf` (S1.3; its doc says S4a removes it with the parameter), which `builtin_tools` calls as `let ws_root = startup_root(workspace_root);`. |
| S2 | `ToolContext.conversation_id: Option<String>`; `crate::tools::working_folder::{WorkingFolder, WorkingFolderRefusal, working_folder}` (pure; `ProjectMissing { root }` carries `project.root_string()`, the recorded canonical root); `tools/builtins/approval_preview.rs` with `pub(super) enum WriteLanding<'a> { ByProduct { store: &'a Path }, StartupFolder { dir: &'a Path } }` — **no `Project` variant: S2's spec conflict 1 leaves `Project { root, replaces }` to S4a, which adds it in S4a.11, the commit that first constructs it** — and `pub(super) fn write_card(path: &str, landing: WriteLanding<'_>) -> String` producing interfaces §4.2's by-product and startup-folder texts, with the approval_preview test `a_startup_folder_write_card_names_the_folder_the_daemon_was_started_in`; in `file_ops.rs`, `FileWriteTool::confirmation_preview` (never `Err`), `FileWriteTool::saves_as_artifact` and `FileWriteTool::landing_card` (routed by `is_the_home_root`), the free `fn names_a_file` directly above `artifact_name`'s doc, and in its tests the helpers `card()` (`.expect("the write card refuses nothing yet")`) and `by_product()` with six `a_write_card_*` tests; `crate::test_util::GuardedProject` (core) with `new()`, `ctx()` (`owner_id` `owner-test`, `request_workspace_root` and `workspace_id` = `root`, `conversation_id` `conv-test`, no `session_log`), `scratch_ctx()`, `home_root()`, field `root`. |

### Choices made where the spec is open

- **`file_write` with no project and no conversation saves a by-product** (`WorkingFolderRefusal::NoConversation` maps
  to the by-product, like `Scratch`): a by-product's place is its owner's artifact store, not a working folder, and
  ST-10 says that with no project `file_write` is an artifact; only `ProjectMissing`, `NotAProject` and `Unavailable`
  refuse (Spec conflicts, 8). Ruled so by the lead (R-T5).
- **One `plan` function answers the card and the write** (`FileWriteTool::plan`, sync, creates nothing): every refusal
  the write gives before it touches a byte is the card's refusal too, so no card is raised for a write that would then
  be refused (interfaces §4.3).
- **`storage_path` is `Path::new(project_root).join(rel_path)`** where `rel_path` is `store::relative_to(root,
  resolved)`: the write resolver's answer, so a write through a link inside the root records where it landed.
- **`record_project_file` refuses a relative `project_root` and a `rel_path` that is not plain names**: the row's
  address must be an exact suffix of `storage_path` (spec §13's table), which only plain names guarantee.
- **R46 is checked before ST-17's cap**: with no conversation log, "raise snapshot_max_bytes" would be advice that
  cannot help.
- **A pre-edit target outside the project, or inside the home store, is refused, not written uncopied** (fail closed):
  the write resolver already refuses both, so this is a backstop that never runs; when it does, losing bytes is worse
  than refusing.
- **The project delete removes pointer rows with their own uncounted statement** (`… AND in_project = 1`) before the
  counted by-product delete: `PurgeCounts` gains no field, the wire does not change, and the plan's counts and the
  outcome's stay equal.
- **The read-time refresh is compare-and-set on `sha256` and `in_project = 1`** and touches `updated_at`: a write that
  landed while the hash ran wins, and the row says when it last followed the file.
- **The content routes name every download for its last path component**, by-product or not: a by-product's name has
  no `/`, so only a result file's changes.
- **`openalpaca tail` prints `[in the project]`** where a by-product prints `[markdown v2]`: a result file has no
  versions to number.
- **`EditVerb::Edit` carries `#[allow(dead_code)]` until S4b constructs it**: the clippy baseline (78) admits no new
  warning, and S4b removes the attribute with its first use.
- **Only S4a.1's schema tests insert a pointer-shaped row by hand** (`insert_result`, the migration test): they test
  the index before R35's method exists. Every other row with `in_project = 1` in this slice — R39's seven included — is
  written by `record_project_file`.
- **The completion report's two runtime lines come from one function, `outcome::runtime_notes`**, used by the report
  message and by the summary's cut, refusals first: the summary keeps both whole through `truncate_summary`.

### Order (the lead's ruling R-T1)

The tasks land in this order: **S4a.1–S4a.10, S4a.12–S4a.17, S4a.18, then S4a.11 last** — task numbers kept, since
later slices cite "S4a.11". No commit offers Open on an agent-written script, or follows a link out of the project,
before the readers that guard it exist (§16's "guards before the root moves", inside the slice): the run's counts
(S4a.6), the report line (S4a.12), the list and its filter (S4a.13), Open's refusal (S4a.14), the content route
(S4a.15), the sweep (S4a.16), `send` (S4a.17) and the attachment refusal (S4a.18) all land before `file_write` writes
its first result file. None of S4a.12–S4a.18 consumes a name S4a.11 produces (`record_tool_project_file`,
`WriteLanding::Project`, `FileWriteTool::plan`, the startup root's removal): their tests write pointer rows with
S4a.3's `record_project_file`, never through `file_write`. The slice gate runs after the last task, S4a.11.

```rust
/// Migration 4 (ST-12, R35): every row a version-3 store holds reads
/// `in_project = 0` — a by-product or an upload, never a result file — and
/// the address index is rebuilt with the column, so a result file may share
/// its path with a by-product's or an upload's address.
#[test]
fn a_version_3_database_migrates_to_4_with_every_row_outside_the_project() {
    let dir = tempdir().unwrap();
    let db_path = dir.path().join("v3.db");
    {
        let conn = Connection::open(&db_path).unwrap();
        for migration in &migrations::MIGRATIONS[..3] {
            conn.execute_batch(migration.sql).unwrap();
        }
        conn.execute_batch(
            "INSERT INTO file_assets (id, owner_id, sha256, filename, mime_type, size_bytes,
                                      storage_path, origin, project_root, rel_path) VALUES
                 ('upload', 'u', 'a', 'a.txt', 'text/plain', 1,
                  '/h/.openalpaca/projects/-w-app/uploads/2026-09-01/01-a.txt', 'upload',
                  '/w/app', '2026-09-01/01-a.txt'),
                 ('by-product', 'u', 'b', '01-notes.md', 'text/markdown', 1,
                  '/h/.openalpaca/projects/-w-app/artifacts/loose/2026-09-01/01-notes.md',
                  'produced', '/w/app', 'loose/2026-09-01/01-notes.md');",
        )
        .unwrap();
        let version: i32 = conn
            .query_row("SELECT MAX(version) FROM schema_version", [], |row| {
                row.get(0)
            })
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(version, 3, "the fixture is a version-3 store");
    }

    let db = Database::open(&db_path).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(db.schema_version().unwrap(), newest_version());
    db.with_connection(|conn| {
        let versions = conn
            .prepare("SELECT version FROM schema_version ORDER BY version")?
            .query_map([], |row| row.get::<_, i32>(0))?
            .collect::<rusqlite::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
        assert!(versions.contains(&4), "migration 4 ran in place: {versions:?}");
        let rows = conn
            .prepare("SELECT id, in_project FROM file_assets ORDER BY id")?
            .query_map([], |row| Ok((row.get::<_, String>(0)?, row.get::<_, i64>(1)?)))?
            .collect::<rusqlite::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
        assert_eq!(
            rows,
            [("by-product".to_string(), 0), ("upload".to_string(), 0)]
        );
        let index: String = conn.query_row(
            "SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'index' AND name = 'idx_file_assets_addr'",
            [],
            |row| row.get(0),
        )?;
        assert!(index.contains("in_project"), "{index}");
        // A result file at the upload's address is a row of its own.
        insert_result(conn, "result", "/w/app", "2026-09-01/01-a.txt")?;
        Ok(())
    })
    .unwrap();
}
```

Create `crates/openalpaca_storage/src/migrations/004_project_files.sql` (interfaces §5.1, verbatim; its first line is
the generated docs' summary):

```sql
-- Project files, version 4: a result file an agent writes into its project gets a pointer row (owner decision ST-12, design §13 R35) — the real file's address, no copy, no versions.
-- `in_project = 1` marks such a row: `project_root` is the project, `rel_path`
-- the file's path relative to it (an exact suffix of `storage_path`), `origin`
-- 'produced', `status` 'ready'. Every other row is 0. The unique address
-- index gains the column, so a pointer path equal to a by-product's or an
-- upload's address is a different row.

ALTER TABLE file_assets ADD COLUMN in_project INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_file_assets_addr;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_file_assets_addr ON file_assets(COALESCE(project_root, ''), in_project, rel_path) WHERE rel_path IS NOT NULL;

INSERT INTO schema_version(version) VALUES (4);
```

```rust
/// ST-18: whether Open hands a file named `name` to the system's default app —
/// only when a kind keeps its extension (R21's sets, [`kind_for_file_name`]).
/// `false` for `.sh`, `.command`, `.svg`, `.exe` and every name with no
/// extension (`Makefile`, `Dockerfile`, a dotfile such as `.env`): those get
/// Reveal only, since a default app could run them.
pub fn opens_in_default_app(name: &str) -> bool {
    kind_for_file_name(name).is_some()
}
```

```rust
/// R39: the user's file is exactly as they had it — its bytes, and its
/// modification time, which any write (even of the same bytes) would move.
fn assert_untouched(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8], mtime: std::time::SystemTime) {
    assert_eq!(fs::read(path).unwrap(), bytes, "the user's bytes");
    assert_eq!(
        fs::metadata(path).unwrap().modified().unwrap(),
        mtime,
        "the user's modification time"
    );
}
```

```rust
// ============================================================================
// R35 — the pointer row (ST-12)

/// The row R35 writes: produced, ready, in the project, the real file's
/// address, no version row, nothing under `.versions/` or the project's
/// `artifacts/`, and the file untouched.
#[test]
fn recording_a_result_file_writes_its_pointer_row_and_no_version() {
    let f = Fixture::new();
    f.task("3f2a1b7c-0000-4000-8000-000000000000", "Build the parser");
    let path = f.project_root().join("src").join("main.rs");
    fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
    fs::write(&path, b"fn main() {}\n").unwrap();
    let mtime = fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().modified().unwrap();
    let root = f.project_root().to_string_lossy().into_owned();

    let (row, inserted) = f
        .store()
        .record_project_file(NewProjectFile {
            owner_id: OWNER,
            project_root: &root,
            rel_path: "src/main.rs",
            content: b"fn main() {}\n",
            task_id: Some("3f2a1b7c-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"),
            agent_id: Some("code_agent::a1"),
        })
        .unwrap();

    assert!(inserted);
    assert!(row.in_project);
    assert_eq!(row.origin, ArtifactOrigin::Produced);
    assert_eq!(row.project_root.as_deref(), Some(root.as_str()));
    assert_eq!(row.rel_path.as_deref(), Some("src/main.rs"));
    assert_eq!(row.name, "src/main.rs");
    assert_eq!(row.storage_path, path.to_string_lossy());
    assert_eq!(row.kind, Some(ArtifactKind::Code));
    assert_eq!(row.mime_type, "text/plain");
    assert_eq!(row.sha256, sha256_hex(b"fn main() {}\n"));
    assert_eq!(row.size_bytes, 13);
    assert_eq!(
        row.task_id.as_deref(),
        Some("3f2a1b7c-0000-4000-8000-000000000000")
    );
    assert_eq!(row.agent_id.as_deref(), Some("code_agent::a1"));
    assert_eq!((row.version, row.version_count, row.pinned), (1, 0, false));
    assert!(row.summary.is_none());
    assert!(row.metadata().is_none(), "only the store's own head stamp");
    let asset = FileAssetRepository::new(&f.db)
        .get_by_id(&row.id)
        .unwrap()
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(asset.status.as_str(), "ready", "the extractor never reads it");
    assert!(f.store().versions(&row.id).unwrap().is_empty(), "no artifact_versions row");
    assert!(
        !f.artifacts_root().exists(),
        "nothing is written under the project's artifacts/"
    );
    assert!(!f.project_root().join("src").join(".versions").exists());
    assert_untouched(&path, b"fn main() {}\n", mtime);
}

/// R39: a second `file_write` of a path updates its own pointer row — never a
/// by-product that shares its address (fails when the lookup ignores
/// `in_project`).
#[test]
fn a_second_file_write_of_a_path_updates_only_its_own_row() {
    let f = Fixture::new();
    let scope = f.scope();
    let mut new = NewArtifact::new(OWNER, &scope, ArtifactKind::Markdown, "notes", b"a draft\n");
    new.created = at(1);
    let (by_product, _) = f.store().put(new).unwrap();
    let rel = by_product.rel_path.clone().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(rel, "loose/2026-09-01/01-notes.md");

    let (first, path, _) = f.result_file(&rel, b"first\n");
    fs::write(&path, b"second, longer\n").unwrap();
    let mtime = fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().modified().unwrap();
    let root = f.project_root().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
    let (second, inserted) = f
        .store()
        .record_project_file(NewProjectFile {
            owner_id: OWNER,
            project_root: &root,
            rel_path: &rel,
            content: b"second, longer\n",
            task_id: None,
            agent_id: None,
        })
        .unwrap();

    assert!(!inserted, "the second write updates");
    assert_eq!(second.id, first.id);
    assert_eq!(second.sha256, sha256_hex(b"second, longer\n"));
    assert_eq!(second.size_bytes, 15);
    assert_eq!(
        (second.version, second.version_count),
        (1, 0),
        "no version: a result file's history is git's (ST-12)"
    );
    let untouched = f.store().get(&by_product.id, OWNER).unwrap().unwrap();
    assert!(!untouched.in_project);
    assert_eq!(untouched.storage_path, by_product.storage_path);
    assert_eq!(untouched.sha256, by_product.sha256);
    assert_eq!(fs::read(&by_product.storage_path).unwrap(), b"a draft\n");
    assert_eq!(file_asset_count(&f), 2);
    assert_untouched(&path, b"second, longer\n", mtime);
}

/// R39: a result file whose path equals an upload's address is a row of its
/// own, and the upload's row is left alone (fails when the index or the
/// lookup ignores `in_project`).
#[test]
fn a_pointer_path_equal_to_an_uploads_address_leaves_the_upload_row_alone() {
    let f = Fixture::new();
    let scope = f.scope();
    let upload = crate::UploadStore::new(&f.db)
        .put(crate::NewUpload {
            owner_id: OWNER,
            filename: "report.txt",
            mime_type: "text/plain",
            data: b"uploaded\n",
            scope: &scope,
            created: at(1),
        })
        .unwrap()
        .asset;
    let upload_row = f.store().get(&upload.id, OWNER).unwrap().unwrap();
    let rel = upload_row.rel_path.clone().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(rel, "2026-09-01/01-report.txt");

    let (result, path, mtime) = f.result_file(&rel, b"the user's report\n");

    assert_ne!(result.id, upload.id);
    assert!(result.in_project);
    let after = f.store().get(&upload.id, OWNER).unwrap().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(after.origin, ArtifactOrigin::Upload);
    assert!(!after.in_project);
    assert_eq!(after.storage_path, upload_row.storage_path);
    assert_eq!(after.sha256, upload_row.sha256);
    assert_eq!(fs::read(&upload_row.storage_path).unwrap(), b"uploaded\n");
    assert_untouched(&path, b"the user's report\n", mtime);
}

/// A pointer row another owner recorded is never updated by this one.
#[test]
fn a_result_file_another_owner_recorded_is_never_taken_over() {
    let f = Fixture::new();
    let (theirs, path, mtime) = f.result_file("docs/plan.md", b"theirs\n");
    let root = f.project_root().to_string_lossy().into_owned();

    let err = f
        .store()
        .record_project_file(NewProjectFile {
            owner_id: "owner-2",
            project_root: &root,
            rel_path: "docs/plan.md",
            content: b"mine\n",
            task_id: None,
            agent_id: None,
        })
        .unwrap_err();

    assert!(format!("{err:#}").contains("belongs to another owner"), "{err:#}");
    let row = f.store().get(&theirs.id, OWNER).unwrap().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(row.sha256, theirs.sha256);
    assert_untouched(&path, b"theirs\n", mtime);
}

/// ST-12, ST-18: a result file's record says it is in the project, Open is
/// offered only when a kind keeps its extension, and `list` filters on the
/// column — against rows R35's method wrote.
#[test]
fn a_result_files_record_says_so_and_the_list_filters_on_it() {
    let f = Fixture::new();
    let scope = f.scope();
    let mut new = NewArtifact::new(OWNER, &scope, ArtifactKind::Markdown, "notes", b"a draft\n");
    new.created = at(1);
    let (by_product, _) = f.store().put(new).unwrap();
    let (code, code_path, code_mtime) = f.result_file("src/main.rs", b"fn main() {}\n");
    let (script, script_path, script_mtime) = f.result_file("scripts/build.sh", b"echo hi\n");

    assert!(code.in_project && script.in_project);
    assert!(code.openable(), "a kind keeps .rs");
    assert!(!script.openable(), "a shell script is Reveal only (ST-18)");
    let ids = |in_project: Option<bool>| -> Vec<String> {
        let mut q = ArtifactQuery::new(OWNER);
        q.in_project = in_project;
        let mut ids: Vec<String> = f.store().list(&q).unwrap().0.into_iter().map(|r| r.id).collect();
        ids.sort();
        ids
    };
    assert_eq!(ids(Some(false)), vec![by_product.id.clone()]);
    let mut results = vec![code.id.clone(), script.id.clone()];
    results.sort();
    assert_eq!(ids(Some(true)), results);
    assert_eq!(ids(None).len(), 3, "absent: both");
    assert_untouched(&code_path, b"fn main() {}\n", code_mtime);
    assert_untouched(&script_path, b"echo hi\n", script_mtime);
}
```
