```rust
//! `file_edit` (ST-22; storage design §13, R47–R49): the match, the body,
//! the pre-edit copy and the pointer row. Every test that touches a file does
//! it in a guarded temp project (`GuardedProject`, interfaces §1.7) — never in
//! the repository, never in the process's current directory.

use super::*;
use crate::session_log::{RecordType, SNAPSHOTS_DIR, SessionLogLimits, SessionLogService};
use crate::test_util::GuardedProject;
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
use std::fs;

const SESSION: &str = "sess-edit";
const OWNER: &str = "owner-test";

// ── R47's match, pure ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

#[test]
fn one_occurrence_is_replaced_and_every_other_byte_kept() {
    let text = "keep\tthis  \nold line\r\nlast line, no newline at the end";
    let edited = apply_edit("a.txt", text, "old line", "new line", false).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        edited,
        Edited {
            text: "keep\tthis  \nnew line\r\nlast line, no newline at the end".to_string(),
            replacements: 1,
            first_line: 2,
        }
    );
}

#[test]
fn two_occurrences_without_replace_all_are_refused_naming_the_count() {
    let refused = apply_edit("src/a.rs", "x = 1;\ny = 2;\nx = 1;\n", "x = 1;", "x = 3;", false)
        .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        refused,
        "old_string occurs 2 times in 'src/a.rs'. Give more of the surrounding text so it \
         occurs once, or set replace_all to true to change every one."
    );
}

#[test]
fn replace_all_changes_every_occurrence_and_names_the_first_line() {
    let edited = apply_edit("a.txt", "x\na\nb\na\n", "a", "c", true).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        edited,
        Edited {
            text: "x\nc\nb\nc\n".to_string(),
            replacements: 2,
            first_line: 2,
        }
    );
}

#[test]
fn an_absent_old_string_is_refused_naming_file_read() {
    let refused = apply_edit("a.txt", "alpha\n", "beta", "gamma", false).unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        refused,
        "old_string was not found in 'a.txt'. Read the file with file_read and copy the exact \
         text, whitespace and line breaks included."
    );
}

#[test]
fn an_empty_old_string_is_refused_naming_file_write() {
    let refused = apply_edit("a.txt", "alpha\n", "", "beta", false).unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        refused,
        "old_string is empty. Give the exact text to replace; to create a file, use file_write."
    );
}

#[test]
fn identical_strings_are_refused() {
    let refused = apply_edit("a.txt", "alpha\n", "alpha", "alpha", false).unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        refused,
        "old_string and new_string are the same, so there is nothing to change."
    );
}

/// R47: a model writes LF; a CRLF file keeps its endings.
#[test]
fn an_lf_old_string_matches_a_crlf_file_and_the_file_keeps_its_endings() {
    let text = "fn a() {\r\n    1\r\n}\r\n";
    let edited = apply_edit("a.rs", text, "    1\n}", "    2\n    // two\n}", false).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        edited,
        Edited {
            text: "fn a() {\r\n    2\r\n    // two\r\n}\r\n".to_string(),
            replacements: 1,
            first_line: 2,
        }
    );
}

/// The CRLF retry may make the two strings one: that is still nothing to do.
#[test]
fn a_crlf_retry_that_makes_the_strings_equal_is_refused_as_identical() {
    let refused = apply_edit("a.txt", "a\r\nb\r\n", "a\nb", "a\r\nb", false).unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        refused,
        "old_string and new_string are the same, so there is nothing to change."
    );
}

#[test]
fn lf_to_crlf_leaves_an_existing_crlf_alone() {
    assert_eq!(lf_to_crlf("a\nb\r\nc\n"), "a\r\nb\r\nc\r\n");
    assert_eq!(lf_to_crlf("no break"), "no break");
}

/// The lead's ruling R-T11 (R47: "line endings included"): a file whose
/// every line break is `\r\n` stays all-CRLF when a one-line `old_string` is
/// replaced by a two-line `new_string`; a file that already mixes the two
/// keeps what the model wrote.
#[test]
fn a_two_line_new_string_in_an_all_crlf_file_keeps_it_all_crlf() {
    let text = "[a]\r\nkey = 1\r\n";
    let edited = apply_edit("a.toml", text, "key = 1", "key = 2\nother = 3", false).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        edited,
        Edited {
            text: "[a]\r\nkey = 2\r\nother = 3\r\n".to_string(),
            replacements: 1,
            first_line: 2,
        }
    );

    let mixed = "[a]\nkey = 1\r\n";
    let edited = apply_edit("a.toml", mixed, "key = 1", "key = 2\nother = 3", false).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(edited.text, "[a]\nkey = 2\nother = 3\r\n");
}

// ── The tool, in a guarded project ──────────────────────────────────────

/// A guarded project, this conversation's log and a database for its
/// pointer rows. Declared so the log and the database drop before the
/// project's guard and folders.
struct Bench {
    service: Arc<SessionLogService>,
    db: Database,
    _db_dir: tempfile::TempDir,
    gp: GuardedProject,
}

impl Bench {
    fn new() -> Self {
        let gp = GuardedProject::new();
        fs::create_dir_all(gp.home_root().join("sessions")).unwrap();
        let service = SessionLogService::new(
            gp.home_root().join("sessions"),
            None,
            SessionLogLimits::default(),
            "test".to_string(),
        )
        .into_arc();
        let db_dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let db = Database::open(&db_dir.path().join("test.db")).unwrap();
        Self {
            service,
            db,
            _db_dir: db_dir,
            gp,
        }
    }

    /// The tool with a database; `cap` sets `snapshot_max_bytes`.
    fn tool(&self, cap: Option<u64>) -> FileEditTool {
        let daemon_config = cap.map(|bytes| {
            let mut config = DaemonConfig::default();
            config.orchestrator.sessions.snapshot_max_bytes = bytes;
            Arc::new(ArcSwap::from_pointee(config))
        });
        FileEditTool {
            db: Some(self.db.clone()),
            daemon_config,
        }
    }

    /// A project turn whose loop writes this conversation's log — what the
    /// main loop and a subagent hand the tool.
    fn ctx(&self) -> ToolContext {
        ToolContext {
            session_id: Some(SESSION.to_string()),
            session_log: Some(self.service.handle_for(SESSION)),
            ..self.gp.ctx()
        }
    }

    fn put(&self, rel: &str, bytes: &[u8]) {
        let file = self.gp.root.join(rel);
        fs::create_dir_all(file.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
        fs::write(file, bytes).unwrap();
    }

    fn bytes(&self, rel: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
        fs::read(self.gp.root.join(rel)).unwrap()
    }

    /// Every copy this conversation kept, by name.
    fn images(&self) -> Vec<std::path::PathBuf> {
        let mut out: Vec<std::path::PathBuf> =
            fs::read_dir(self.service.session_dir(SESSION).join(SNAPSHOTS_DIR))
                .into_iter()
                .flatten()
                .flatten()
                .map(|entry| entry.path())
                .filter(|path| path.is_file())
                .collect();
        out.sort();
        out
    }

    /// The owner's pointer rows (interfaces §5.2).
    fn rows(&self) -> Vec<openalpaca_storage::ArtifactRecord> {
        let mut query = openalpaca_storage::ArtifactQuery::new(OWNER);
        query.in_project = Some(true);
        openalpaca_storage::ArtifactStore::new(&self.db)
            .list(&query)
            .unwrap()
            .0
    }
}

fn args(path: &str, old: &str, new: &str) -> serde_json::Value {
    serde_json::json!({"path": path, "old_string": old, "new_string": new})
}

const LIB: &str = "pub fn retries() -> u32 {\n    3\n}\n";

#[tokio::test]
async fn an_edit_changes_the_file_in_the_project_and_says_where() {
    let b = Bench::new();
    b.put("src/lib.rs", LIB.as_bytes());

    let out = b
        .tool(None)
        .execute_with_context(&args("src/lib.rs", "    3", "    5"), &b.ctx())
        .await
        .unwrap();

    let after = "pub fn retries() -> u32 {\n    5\n}\n";
    assert_eq!(b.bytes("src/lib.rs"), after.as_bytes());
    assert_eq!(
        out,
        format!(
            "Edited src/lib.rs in the project: 1 replacement, the first at line 2; {} bytes at {}. \
             Its previous content is kept in this conversation's log.",
            after.len(),
            b.gp.root.join("src/lib.rs").display()
        )
    );
}

/// R47 (§13's first test): refused, and nothing is touched — no copy, no row.
#[tokio::test]
async fn old_string_found_twice_without_replace_all_is_refused_and_the_file_unchanged() {
    let b = Bench::new();
    let before = "x = 1;\ny = 2;\nx = 1;\n";
    b.put("src/a.rs", before.as_bytes());
    let ctx = b.ctx();

    let refused = b
        .tool(None)
        .execute_with_context(&args("src/a.rs", "x = 1;", "x = 3;"), &ctx)
        .await
        .unwrap_err();

    assert!(refused.starts_with("old_string occurs 2 times in 'src/a.rs'."), "{refused}");
    assert_eq!(b.bytes("src/a.rs"), before.as_bytes());
    assert!(ctx.session_log.as_ref().unwrap().flush().await);
    assert!(b.images().is_empty(), "a refusal keeps no copy");
    assert!(b.rows().is_empty(), "a refusal records no row");
}

/// R47 (§13's second test): a missing file's refusal names file_write, and
/// nothing is created.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_missing_file_is_refused_naming_file_write() {
    let b = Bench::new();

    let refused = b
        .tool(None)
        .execute_with_context(&args("docs/new.md", "a", "b"), &b.ctx())
        .await
        .unwrap_err();

    assert_eq!(
        refused,
        "'docs/new.md' does not exist in the project. file_edit changes an existing file; \
         use file_write to create it."
    );
    assert!(!b.gp.root.join("docs").exists(), "nothing was created");
}

/// ST-17 (§13's third test): the bytes the edit destroys are in this
/// conversation's `snapshots/`, committed by a `file_snapshot` record.
#[tokio::test]
async fn the_pre_edit_copy_is_kept_before_the_change() {
    let b = Bench::new();
    b.put("src/lib.rs", LIB.as_bytes());
    let ctx = b.ctx();

    b.tool(None)
        .execute_with_context(&args("src/lib.rs", "    3", "    5"), &ctx)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert!(ctx.session_log.as_ref().unwrap().flush().await);

    let images = b.images();
    assert_eq!(images.len(), 1, "{images:?}");
    assert_eq!(fs::read(&images[0]).unwrap(), LIB.as_bytes(), "the copy holds the old bytes");
    let records = crate::session_log::read_records(&b.service.session_dir(SESSION)).unwrap();
    let snapshot = records
        .iter()
        .find(|r| r.kind == RecordType::FileSnapshot.as_str())
        .expect("the copy is committed by a record");
    assert_eq!(snapshot.data["path"], "src/lib.rs");
}

/// ST-17's second refusal, and the proof of the order: a copy that cannot be
/// taken stops the edit before the file is touched.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_copy_that_fails_refuses_the_edit_and_leaves_the_file() {
    let b = Bench::new();
    b.put("src/lib.rs", LIB.as_bytes());
    // `snapshots/` cannot be created: a file stands at its name.
    fs::create_dir_all(b.service.session_dir(SESSION)).unwrap();
    fs::write(b.service.session_dir(SESSION).join(SNAPSHOTS_DIR), "in the way").unwrap();

    let refused = b
        .tool(None)
        .execute_with_context(&args("src/lib.rs", "    3", "    5"), &b.ctx())
        .await
        .unwrap_err();

    assert!(
        refused.starts_with("Refusing to edit 'src/lib.rs': its pre-edit snapshot could not be taken ("),
        "{refused}"
    );
    assert!(refused.ends_with("). The file is unchanged."), "{refused}");
    assert_eq!(b.bytes("src/lib.rs"), LIB.as_bytes());
    assert!(b.rows().is_empty());
}

/// R35 (§13's fourth test): one row per project file, updated in place.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_second_edit_updates_the_same_pointer_row() {
    let b = Bench::new();
    b.put("src/lib.rs", LIB.as_bytes());
    let tool = b.tool(None);

    tool.execute_with_context(&args("src/lib.rs", "    3", "    5"), &b.ctx())
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let first = b.rows();
    assert_eq!(first.len(), 1, "{first:?}");
    tool.execute_with_context(&args("src/lib.rs", "    5", "    8"), &b.ctx())
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let second = b.rows();

    assert_eq!(second.len(), 1, "{second:?}");
    assert_eq!(second[0].id, first[0].id, "the same row");
    let after = b.bytes("src/lib.rs");
    assert_eq!(after, "pub fn retries() -> u32 {\n    8\n}\n".as_bytes());
    assert!(second[0].in_project);
    assert_eq!(second[0].rel_path.as_deref(), Some("src/lib.rs"));
    assert_eq!(second[0].size_bytes, after.len() as i64);
    assert_eq!(second[0].sha256, format!("{:x}", Sha256::digest(&after)));
    assert_ne!(second[0].sha256, first[0].sha256, "the row follows the file");
}

/// R47 (§13's last test), through the tool.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_crlf_file_keeps_its_line_endings() {
    let b = Bench::new();
    b.put("notes.txt", b"one\r\ntwo\r\nthree\r\n");

    b.tool(None)
        .execute_with_context(&args("notes.txt", "two\nthree", "2\n3"), &b.ctx())
        .await
        .unwrap();

    assert_eq!(b.bytes("notes.txt"), b"one\r\n2\r\n3\r\n");
}

#[cfg(unix)]
#[tokio::test]
async fn an_edit_keeps_the_files_mode() {
    use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;

    let b = Bench::new();
    b.put("run.sh", b"#!/bin/sh\necho 1\n");
    fs::set_permissions(b.gp.root.join("run.sh"), fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755)).unwrap();

    b.tool(None)
        .execute_with_context(&args("run.sh", "echo 1", "echo 2"), &b.ctx())
        .await
        .unwrap();

    let mode = fs::metadata(b.gp.root.join("run.sh")).unwrap().permissions().mode();
    assert_eq!(mode & 0o777, 0o755);
}

/// R46: a loop with no session log keeps no copy, so an existing file —
/// every file `file_edit` changes — is not changed.
#[tokio::test]
async fn without_a_session_log_an_existing_file_is_not_edited() {
    let b = Bench::new();
    b.put("notes.md", b"draft\n");

    let refused = b
        .tool(None)
        .execute_with_context(&args("notes.md", "draft", "final"), &b.gp.ctx())
        .await
        .unwrap_err();

    assert_eq!(
        refused,
        "Refusing to edit 'notes.md': it already exists, and no copy of its current content can \
         be kept here — a skill or a plugin agent keeps no conversation log. The file is \
         unchanged. Write the result to a new file, or ask for the change in the conversation \
         itself."
    );
    assert_eq!(b.bytes("notes.md"), b"draft\n");
}

/// ST-17's cap, asked before the file is read.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_file_above_the_snapshot_cap_is_refused() {
    let b = Bench::new();
    b.put("big.txt", b"far more than eight bytes");

    let refused = b
        .tool(Some(8))
        .execute_with_context(&args("big.txt", "far", "near"), &b.ctx())
        .await
        .unwrap_err();

    assert_eq!(
        refused,
        "Refusing to edit 'big.txt': it is 25 bytes, above the 8 byte [orchestrator.sessions] \
         snapshot_max_bytes limit, so no pre-edit snapshot can be kept for it. The file is \
         unchanged. Raise snapshot_max_bytes, or copy the file aside yourself first."
    );
    assert_eq!(b.bytes("big.txt"), b"far more than eight bytes");
}

/// R48: in a project only, and the refusal names file_write.
#[tokio::test]
async fn with_no_project_file_edit_is_refused_naming_file_write() {
    let b = Bench::new();
    let ctx = ToolContext {
        session_id: Some(SESSION.to_string()),
        session_log: Some(b.service.handle_for(SESSION)),
        ..b.gp.scratch_ctx()
    };

    let refused = b
        .tool(None)
        .execute_with_context(&args("notes.md", "a", "b"), &ctx)
        .await
        .unwrap_err();

    assert_eq!(
        refused,
        "file_edit changes a file in a project, and this conversation has no project. Use \
         file_write to save a file instead."
    );
}
```

  In `crates/openalpaca_core/src/tools/builtins/tests.rs`, add after `annotations_for_builtin_open_world_correct`:

```rust
/// ST-22 / R49: `file_edit` is a builtin, asks exactly as `file_write` does
/// (destructive, local), is not strict-marked (`replace_all` is optional —
/// interfaces §7.4), and the sanitizer's `../` rule does not read its strings
/// (R29: a first-party builtin's arguments are content); and `file_write`'s
/// description points at it for a change to part of a file (the lead's
/// ruling R-T13).
#[test]
fn file_edit_is_registered_asking_like_file_write() {
    use crate::security::sanitizer::TraversalRule;
    use crate::tools::ToolRegistry;

    let registry = ToolRegistry::default();
    for tool in builtin_tools(None, None, None) {
        registry.register(tool).unwrap();
    }
    let edit = registry.get("file_edit").expect("file_edit is a builtin");
    let write = registry.get("file_write").expect("file_write is a builtin");
    let (edit_ann, write_ann) = (edit.annotations.unwrap(), write.annotations.unwrap());
    assert_eq!(edit_ann.destructive_hint, Some(true));
    assert_eq!(edit_ann.destructive_hint, write_ann.destructive_hint);
    assert_eq!(edit_ann.read_only_hint, write_ann.read_only_hint);
    assert_eq!(edit_ann.idempotent_hint, write_ann.idempotent_hint);
    assert_eq!(edit_ann.open_world_hint, write_ann.open_world_hint);
    assert_eq!(edit.definition.strict, None);
    assert_eq!(
        edit.definition.parameters["required"],
        serde_json::json!(["path", "old_string", "new_string"])
    );
    assert_eq!(registry.traversal_rule("file_edit"), TraversalRule::Allow);
    assert!(
        write
            .definition
            .description
            .contains("To change part of an existing file in the project, use file_edit."),
        "{}",
        write.definition.description
    );
}
```

```rust
    "old_string is empty. Give the exact text to replace; to create a file, use file_write.";
const EDIT_IDENTICAL: &str =
    "old_string and new_string are the same, so there is nothing to change.";

/// R47: a missing file's refusal names the tool that creates one.
fn edit_missing(path: &str) -> String {
    format!(
        "'{path}' does not exist in the project. file_edit changes an existing file; use \
         file_write to create it."
    )
}

/// Change part of one file in the project (ST-22): the exact text to find and
/// the text to put in its place, every other byte kept. The same folder,
/// confinement, card, pre-edit copy and pointer row as `file_write`'s real
/// write (storage design §13, R47–R49).
struct FileEditTool {
    /// Where the pointer row is recorded (R35). Absent (tests, the CLI): the
    /// edit still lands, and the result says the app could not list it (R36).
    db: Option<Database>,
    /// `[orchestrator.sessions] snapshot_max_bytes`, the cap on the pre-edit
    /// copy (ST-17). Absent: the documented default.
    daemon_config: Option<Arc<ArcSwap<DaemonConfig>>>,
}

/// R47's arguments, read once for the card and the body alike.
struct EditArgs<'a> {
    path: &'a str,
    old_string: &'a str,
    new_string: &'a str,
    /// Default false; anything but `true` is false.
    replace_all: bool,
}

fn edit_args(arguments: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<EditArgs<'_>, String> {
    fn required<'a>(arguments: &'a serde_json::Value, key: &str) -> Result<&'a str, String> {
        arguments
            .get(key)
            .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("Missing required parameter: {key}"))
    }
    Ok(EditArgs {
        path: required(arguments, "path")?,
        old_string: required(arguments, "old_string")?,
        new_string: required(arguments, "new_string")?,
        replace_all: arguments
            .get("replace_all")
            .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_bool)
            .unwrap_or(false),
    })
}

/// What an edit will do, worked out without writing anything — the card's
/// whole and the body's first half (one plan answers both, interfaces §4.3).
struct EditPlan {
    /// The project's canonical root.
    root: std::path::PathBuf,
    /// The file, as the write resolver returned it.
    target: std::path::PathBuf,
    /// The whole file after the edit.
    text: String,
    replacements: usize,
    first_line: usize,
}

/// What R47's match made of a file's text.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Edited {
    text: String,
    replacements: usize,
    /// 1-based line of the first occurrence.
    first_line: usize,
}

/// R47's match: exact, non-overlapping occurrences of `old_string` — exactly
/// one unless `replace_all` — replaced by `new_string`, every other byte of
/// `text` kept. A file holding `\r\n`, asked with an `old_string` that holds
/// `\n` but no `\r\n` and is not found as given, is searched again with every
/// lone `\n` of both strings written `\r\n`: a model writes LF, and the file
/// keeps its endings. In a file whose every line break is `\r\n` (no lone
/// `\n`), `new_string`'s lone `\n` are written `\r\n` even when `old_string`
/// is found as given (the lead's ruling R-T11).
fn apply_edit(
    path: &str,
    text: &str,
    old_string: &str,
    new_string: &str,
    replace_all: bool,
) -> Result<Edited, String> {
    if old_string.is_empty() {
        return Err(EDIT_EMPTY_OLD.to_string());
    }
    let crlf = !text.contains(old_string)
        && text.contains("\r\n")
        && old_string.contains('\n')
        && !old_string.contains("\r\n");
    // The lead's ruling R-T11: a file whose every line break is `\r\n` stays
    // so — `new_string`'s lone `\n` are written `\r\n` there even when
    // `old_string` holds no line break. A file that mixes the two keeps what
    // the model wrote.
    let all_crlf = text.contains("\r\n") && !has_lone_lf(text);
    let old = if crlf {
        lf_to_crlf(old_string)
    } else {
        old_string.to_string()
    };
    let new = if crlf || all_crlf {
        lf_to_crlf(new_string)
    } else {
        new_string.to_string()
    };
    if old == new {
        return Err(EDIT_IDENTICAL.to_string());
    }
    let Some(first) = text.find(old.as_str()) else {
        return Err(format!(
            "old_string was not found in '{path}'. Read the file with file_read and copy the \
             exact text, whitespace and line breaks included."
        ));
    };
    let count = text.matches(old.as_str()).count();
    if count > 1 && !replace_all {
        return Err(format!(
            "old_string occurs {count} times in '{path}'. Give more of the surrounding text so \
             it occurs once, or set replace_all to true to change every one."
        ));
    }
    // A byte slice up to a match's start, never a `str` cut.
    let first_line = 1 + text.as_bytes()[..first]
        .iter()
        .filter(|byte| **byte == b'\n')
        .count();
    let (text, replacements) = if replace_all {
        (text.replace(old.as_str(), &new), count)
    } else {
        (text.replacen(old.as_str(), &new, 1), 1)
    };
    Ok(Edited {
        text,
        replacements,
        first_line,
    })
}

/// Every `\n` that does not already end a `\r\n`, written `\r\n`.
fn lf_to_crlf(text: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len() + text.len() / 8);
    let mut after_cr = false;
    for c in text.chars() {
        if c == '\n' && !after_cr {
            out.push('\r');
        }
        out.push(c);
        after_cr = c == '\r';
    }
    out
}

/// Whether `text` holds a `\n` that does not end a `\r\n` — a file with none
/// is all-CRLF (the lead's ruling R-T11).
fn has_lone_lf(text: &str) -> bool {
    let bytes = text.as_bytes();
    bytes
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .any(|(i, byte)| *byte == b'\n' && (i == 0 || bytes[i - 1] != b'\r'))
}

impl FileEditTool {
    fn snapshot_max_bytes(&self) -> u64 {
        match self.daemon_config {
            Some(ref config) => config.load().orchestrator.sessions.snapshot_max_bytes,
            None => crate::daemon_config::SessionsConfig::default().snapshot_max_bytes,
        }
    }

    /// Everything but the copy, the write and the row: the folder (R48), the
    /// path (R31, R32), the file (it exists, is a regular file, is UTF-8, and
    /// fits the 10 MB bound before and after), the copy's preconditions
    /// (ST-17's cap and R46, from the size alone, before a byte is read) and
    /// the match. Creates nothing, so the card can call it.
    async fn plan(&self, args: &EditArgs<'_>, ctx: &ToolContext) -> Result<EditPlan, String> {
        use crate::tools::working_folder::{WorkingFolder, working_folder};

        let root = match working_folder(ctx) {
            Ok(WorkingFolder::Project { root }) => root,
            Ok(WorkingFolder::Scratch { .. }) => return Err(EDIT_NEEDS_A_PROJECT.to_string()),
            Err(refusal) => return Err(refusal.to_string()),
        };
        let path = args.path;
        let target = super::helpers::resolve_workspace_path_for_write(
            path,
            &root,
            super::helpers::FolderRules::Project,
        )?;
        let metadata = match tokio::fs::metadata(&target).await {
            Ok(metadata) => metadata,
            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Err(edit_missing(path)),
            Err(e) => return Err(format!("Cannot access '{path}': {e}")),
        };
        if metadata.is_dir() {
            return Err(format!("'{path}' is a folder, not a file."));
        }
        if !metadata.is_file() {
            return Err(format!(
                "'{path}' is not a regular file, so file_edit cannot change it."
            ));
        }
        super::pre_edit::check_pre_edit(
            path,
            &target,
            ctx,
            self.snapshot_max_bytes(),
            super::pre_edit::EditVerb::Edit,
        )?;
        let limit = super::helpers::MAX_FILE_READ_SIZE;
        if metadata.len() > limit {
            return Err(format!(
                "File '{path}' is {} bytes, exceeding the {limit} byte limit",
                metadata.len()
            ));
        }
        let bytes = tokio::fs::read(&target)
            .await
            .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to read file '{path}': {e}"))?;
        let text = String::from_utf8(bytes)
            .map_err(|_| format!("'{path}' is not UTF-8 text, so file_edit cannot change it."))?;
        let edited = apply_edit(path, &text, args.old_string, args.new_string, args.replace_all)?;
        if edited.text.len() as u64 > limit {
            return Err(format!(
                "The edited '{path}' would be {} bytes, above the {limit} byte limit file_read \
                 and file_write keep to. The file is unchanged.",
                edited.text.len()
            ));
        }
        Ok(EditPlan {
            root,
            target,
            text: edited.text,
            replacements: edited.replacements,
            first_line: edited.first_line,
        })
    }

    /// R47's order: the plan, the pre-edit copy (ST-17, R46), the file, the
    /// pointer row (R35; R36 when it cannot be recorded).
    async fn edit(&self, arguments: &serde_json::Value, ctx: &ToolContext) -> Result<String, String> {
        use super::pre_edit::{EditVerb, PreEdit, keep_pre_edit_copy};

        let args = edit_args(arguments)?;
        let plan = self.plan(&args, ctx).await?;
        let path = args.path;
        // The current bytes go into this conversation's log first; `Err` —
        // R46, the cap, a copy that failed — leaves the file untouched.
        match keep_pre_edit_copy(
            path,
            &plan.target,
            &plan.root,
            ctx,
            self.snapshot_max_bytes(),
            EditVerb::Edit,
        )
        .await?
        {
            PreEdit::Kept => {}
            // The plan read the file a moment ago and it is gone now.
            PreEdit::NewFile => return Err(edit_missing(path)),
        }
        tokio::fs::write(&plan.target, &plan.text)
            .await
            .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to write file '{path}': {e}"))?;
        let listed = match self.db.as_ref() {
            Some(db) => super::artifact_write::record_tool_project_file(
                db,
                ctx,
                &plan.root,
                &plan.target,
                &plan.text,
            )
            .map(|_| ()),
            // S4a.11's `file_write` words this case the same way.
            None => Err("no database is wired to this tool".to_string()),
        };
        let mut result = format!(
            "Edited {path} in the project: {} replacement{}, the first at line {}; {} bytes at {}. \
             Its previous content is kept in this conversation's log.",
            plan.replacements,
            if plan.replacements == 1 { "" } else { "s" },
            plan.first_line,
            plan.text.len(),
            plan.target.display()
        );
        // R36: the file is the result; the row is a view of it.
        if let Err(e) = listed {
            tracing::warn!(path, "file_edit: the file is written but not listed: {e}");
            result.push_str(&format!(
                " The file is written, but the app could not list it ({e})."
            ));
        }
        Ok(result)
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl BuiltInTool for FileEditTool {
    /// R26: with no context there is no folder to edit in.
    async fn execute(&self, _arguments: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<String, String> {
        Err(crate::tools::working_folder::WorkingFolderRefusal::NoContext.to_string())
    }

    async fn execute_with_context(
        &self,
        arguments: &serde_json::Value,
        ctx: &ToolContext,
    ) -> Result<String, String> {
        self.edit(arguments, ctx).await
    }
}

pub(super) fn file_edit_tool(
    db: Option<Database>,
    daemon_config: Option<Arc<ArcSwap<DaemonConfig>>>,
) -> RegisteredTool {
    RegisteredTool {
        definition: ToolDefinition {
            name: "file_edit".to_string(),
            description: "Change part of one file in the project: give the exact text to find \
                (old_string) and the text to put in its place (new_string), instead of writing \
                the whole file back. old_string must occur exactly once unless replace_all is \
                true. The rest of the file is kept byte for byte, line endings included. Its \
                current content is kept in the conversation's log first. In a project only — to \
                create a file, or with no project, use file_write."
                .to_string(),
            parameters: serde_json::json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "The file, relative to the project folder (e.g. 'src/main.rs'). It must exist."
                    },
                    "old_string": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "The exact text to find, whitespace and line breaks included. It must occur exactly once, unless replace_all is true."
                    },
                    "new_string": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "The text to put in its place. It must differ from old_string."
                    },
                    "replace_all": {
                        "type": "boolean",
                        "description": "Replace every occurrence instead of exactly one. Default false."
                    }
                },
                "required": ["path", "old_string", "new_string"]
            }),
            // Not strict: `replace_all` is optional with a default, and strict
            // mode requires every key (interfaces §7.4; Gotchas, R8).
            strict: None,
            input_examples: Some(vec![serde_json::json!({
                "path": "src/main.rs",
                "old_string": "let retries = 3;",
                "new_string": "let retries = 5;"
            })]),
        },
        backend: ToolBackend::BuiltIn(Arc::new(FileEditTool { db, daemon_config })),
        provides_capabilities: vec!["file_edit".into()],
        exempt_from_timeout: false,
        annotations: annotations_for_builtin("file_edit"),
        version: env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION").to_string(),
        author: "builtin".to_string(),
        created_at: chrono::Utc::now(),
    }
}
```

```rust
        let card = edit_card("src/lib.rs", Path::new("/work/alpaca"), 2, 1, "    3\n}", "    5\n}");
        assert_eq!(
            card,
            "Edits src/lib.rs in the project folder /work/alpaca: 1 replacement, the first at \
             line 2. Its current content is kept in this conversation's log.\n\
             Replace:\n    3\n}\nWith:\n    5\n}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn several_replacements_read_in_the_plural() {
        let card = edit_card("a.txt", Path::new("/p"), 4, 3, "a", "b");
        assert!(
            card.starts_with(
                "Edits a.txt in the project folder /p: 3 replacements, the first at line 4."
            ),
            "{card}"
        );
    }

    /// R49 at the text layer: a U+202E in either string, and a U+200B in the
    /// path, are shown escaped, and one notice counts all three.
    #[test]
    fn hidden_characters_in_the_path_and_both_strings_are_escaped_under_one_notice() {
        let card = edit_card(
            "src/a\u{200B}.rs",
            Path::new("/p"),
            1,
            1,
            "let a = 1;\u{202E}",
            "let a = 2;\u{202E}",
        );
        assert!(!card.contains('\u{202E}') && !card.contains('\u{200B}'), "{card}");
        let lines: Vec<&str> = card.lines().collect();
        assert!(lines[0].starts_with("Edits src/a<U+200B>.rs in the project folder /p:"), "{card}");
        assert_eq!(
            lines[1..].to_vec(),
            vec![
                "Replace:",
                "let a = 1;<U+202E>",
                "With:",
                "let a = 2;<U+202E>",
                "Note: this request contains 3 hidden characters, shown as <U+…>.",
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_string_over_the_budget_is_cut_with_the_cut_notice() {
        let long = "a".repeat(EDIT_PREVIEW_BYTES + 500);
        let card = edit_card("a.txt", Path::new("/p"), 1, 1, &long, "b");
        let lines: Vec<&str> = card.lines().collect();
        assert_eq!(lines[1], "Replace:");
        assert_eq!(lines[2], "a".repeat(EDIT_PREVIEW_BYTES));
        assert_eq!(lines[3], "... (500 more characters not shown)");
        assert_eq!(lines[4..].to_vec(), vec!["With:", "b"]);
    }
}
```

```rust
/// Interfaces §4.3: a call the body would refuse raises no card — the preview
/// refuses with the body's own sentence — and a card's plan writes nothing:
/// no copy, no row, the file as it was.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_refused_edit_raises_no_card_and_a_card_writes_nothing() {
    let b = Bench::new();
    let before = "x = 1;\ny = 2;\nx = 1;\n";
    b.put("src/a.rs", before.as_bytes());
    let ctx = b.ctx();
    let tool = b.tool(None);

    let refused = tool
        .confirmation_preview(&args("src/a.rs", "x = 1;", "x = 3;"), &ctx)
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    assert!(refused.starts_with("old_string occurs 2 times in 'src/a.rs'."), "{refused}");

    let card = tool
        .confirmation_preview(&args("src/a.rs", "y = 2;", "y = 4;"), &ctx)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert!(card.is_some());
    assert_eq!(b.bytes("src/a.rs"), before.as_bytes());
    assert!(ctx.session_log.as_ref().unwrap().flush().await);
    assert!(b.images().is_empty(), "a card keeps no copy");
    assert!(b.rows().is_empty(), "a card records no row");
}

/// The card through the sandbox, as the main loop raises it: `file_edit` is
/// destructive, so a card goes out carrying the escaped strings, and a Deny
/// leaves the file as it was.
#[tokio::test]
async fn the_sandbox_raises_file_edits_card_and_a_deny_leaves_the_file() {
    use crate::agent::subagent::AgentConstraints;
    use crate::bus::EventBus;
    use crate::daemon_config::CircuitBreakerConfig;
    use crate::security::confirmation::{ConfirmationBroker, ConfirmationResponse};
    use crate::security::sandbox::{SandboxManager, SandboxPolicy};
    use crate::tools::ToolRegistry;

    let b = Bench::new();
    let before = "let a = 1;\u{202E}\n";
    b.put("src/a.rs", before.as_bytes());
    let registry = ToolRegistry::default();
    registry
        .register(file_edit_tool(Some(b.db.clone()), None))
        .unwrap();
    let mut sandbox = SandboxManager::new(
        Arc::new(registry),
        EventBus::new(16),
        &CircuitBreakerConfig::default(),
    );
    let broker = Arc::new(ConfirmationBroker::new());
    sandbox.set_confirmation_broker(broker.clone());
    let policy = SandboxPolicy::from_constraints(
        "orchestrator",
        &AgentConstraints {
            allowed_capabilities: vec!["file_edit".to_string()],
            ..Default::default()
        },
    );
    let answering = {
        let broker = broker.clone();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            for _ in 0..300 {
                if let Some(card) = broker.pending_requests().into_iter().next() {
                    broker
                        .respond(
                            &card.request_id,
                            ConfirmationResponse {
                                approved: false,
                                approval_scope: None,
                            },
                        )
                        .unwrap();
                    return Some(card);
                }
                tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
            }
            None
        })
    };
    let call = openalpaca_llm::ToolCall {
        id: "tc-1".to_string(),
        name: "file_edit".to_string(),
        arguments: args("src/a.rs", "let a = 1;\u{202E}", "let a = 2;\u{202E}"),
    };
    let ctx = ToolContext {
        agent_id: Some("orchestrator".to_string()),
        ..b.ctx()
    };

    let refused = sandbox.execute_tool(&call, &policy, &ctx).await.unwrap_err();

    let card = answering.await.unwrap().expect("a card was raised");
    let preview = card.preview.expect("the card carries file_edit's preview");
    assert!(preview.contains("let a = 1;<U+202E>"), "{preview}");
    assert!(preview.contains("let a = 2;<U+202E>"), "{preview}");
    assert!(!preview.contains('\u{202E}'), "{preview}");
    assert!(refused.contains("denied by user"), "{refused}");
    assert_eq!(b.bytes("src/a.rs"), before.as_bytes());
}
```

  (a) `crates/openalpaca_core/src/tools/builtins/approval_preview.rs`, after S2's `pub(super) fn write_card(..) { .. }`

```rust
/// R49's budget for each of `old_string` and `new_string` on `file_edit`'s
/// card, in bytes of escaped text: two strings and the frame stay a card a
/// person reads at a glance (~25 lines each), and the full arguments are
/// drawn below the preview anyway.
pub(super) const EDIT_PREVIEW_BYTES: usize = 1_000;

/// `file_edit`'s card (R49): the file, the project folder and the line of the
/// first occurrence, then both strings — each escaped (`escape_hidden_within`,
/// which keeps `\n` and `\t` as their layout) and cut to
/// [`EDIT_PREVIEW_BYTES`] with the cut notice — then one notice counting every
/// hidden character of the path and both strings. The folder prints as it is:
/// the owner's own path (interfaces §1.3).
pub(super) fn edit_card(
    path: &str,
    root: &std::path::Path,
    first_line: usize,
    replacements: usize,
    old_string: &str,
    new_string: &str,
) -> String {
    use crate::utils::text::{cut_notice, escape_hidden_line, escape_hidden_within, hidden_notice};

    let shown_path = escape_hidden_line(path);
    let old = escape_hidden_within(old_string, EDIT_PREVIEW_BYTES);
    let new = escape_hidden_within(new_string, EDIT_PREVIEW_BYTES);
    let mut lines = vec![format!(
        "Edits {} in the project folder {}: {replacements} replacement{}, the first at line \
         {first_line}. Its current content is kept in this conversation's log.",
        shown_path.text,
        root.display(),
        if replacements == 1 { "" } else { "s" }
    )];
    lines.push("Replace:".to_string());
    lines.push(old.text);
    lines.extend(cut_notice(old.left_out));
    lines.push("With:".to_string());
    lines.push(new.text);
    lines.extend(cut_notice(new.left_out));
    lines.extend(hidden_notice(shown_path.hidden + old.hidden + new.hidden));
    lines.join("\n")
}
```

```rust
/// R48 (storage design §13): `file_edit` comes with the `file_write`
/// capability. Every shipped template that grants `file_write` is handed
/// `file_edit` beside it and its sandbox admits the call; every one that
/// denies `file_write` — and the lead's, which grants neither — is handed
/// neither, and its sandbox refuses `file_edit` by name. Each template is
/// walked exactly as the subagent spawn walks it: `to_subagent`,
/// `resolve_agent_tools`, `SandboxPolicy::from_constraints`,
/// `admit_tool_surface`.
#[test]
fn file_edit_comes_with_the_file_write_capability_in_every_shipped_template() {
    use crate::security::capabilities::CapabilityManager;
    use crate::security::sandbox::SandboxPolicy;
    use crate::tools::ToolRegistry;
    use crate::tools::builtins::builtin_tools;

    let registry = std::sync::Arc::new(ToolRegistry::default());
    for tool in builtin_tools(None, None, None) {
        registry.register(tool).unwrap();
    }
    let agents = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../config/agents");
    for (id, writes) in [
        ("code_agent", true),
        ("general_agent", true),
        ("system_agent", true),
        ("writing_agent", true),
        ("explore_agent", false),
        ("planning_agent", false),
        ("research_agent", false),
        ("review_agent", false),
        ("lead_agent", false),
    ] {
        let path = agents.join(format!("{id}.md"));
        let body = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("reading {}: {e}", path.display()));
        let doc = parse_agent_markdown(&body)
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{} does not parse: {e}", path.display()));
        let agent = doc.to_subagent(&format!("{id}::r48"), "task-1");

        let surface = crate::tools::resolve_agent_tools(&agent, &registry, None);
        let names: Vec<&str> = surface.iter().map(|d| d.name.as_str()).collect();
        assert_eq!(names.contains(&"file_write"), writes, "{id}: file_write on {names:?}");
        assert_eq!(names.contains(&"file_edit"), writes, "{id}: file_edit on {names:?}");

        let mut policy = SandboxPolicy::from_constraints(&agent.id, &agent.constraints);
        policy.admit_tool_surface(&surface);
        assert_eq!(
            CapabilityManager::check_agent_capability(
                &agent.id,
                "file_edit",
                &policy.allowed_capabilities,
                &policy.denied_capabilities,
            )
            .is_ok(),
            writes,
            "{id}: the sandbox admits file_edit"
        );
    }
}
```

```rust
/// The lead's ruling R-T14: a project turn is one whose request carries a
/// non-blank, absolute root — `scope_from_context`'s project arm, the reading
/// every store path makes of it. One predicate for every offer.
#[test]
fn a_project_turn_is_a_non_blank_absolute_root() {
    let with = |root: Option<&str>| ToolContext {
        request_workspace_root: root.map(str::to_string),
        ..Default::default()
    };
    let absolute = std::env::temp_dir().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
    assert!(is_project_turn(&with(Some(&absolute))));
    assert!(!is_project_turn(&with(None)));
    assert!(!is_project_turn(&with(Some("   "))));
    assert!(!is_project_turn(&with(Some("relative/path"))));
}
```

```rust
/// Through the front door: the offers that depend on whether a turn is a
/// project turn (the lead's ruling R-T14: one predicate, computed once).
/// R48: a project turn whose words suggest `file_write` carries `file_edit`
/// beside it on the main loop's request; a turn with no project carries
/// `file_write` alone.
mod project_turn_offers {
    use super::*;
    use openalpaca_llm::{ChatResponse, FinishReason, LlmError, LlmProvider, Usage};

    /// Answers at once and keeps every request it was handed.
    struct Capturing(Arc<Mutex<Vec<ChatRequest>>>);

    #[async_trait]
    impl LlmProvider for Capturing {
        fn name(&self) -> &str {
            "capturing"
        }
        fn supports_tools(&self) -> bool {
            true
        }
        async fn chat(&self, request: ChatRequest) -> Result<ChatResponse, LlmError> {
            self.0.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner()).push(request);
            Ok(ChatResponse {
                content: "ok".to_string(),
                tool_calls: vec![],
                model: "mock-model".to_string(),
                usage: Usage {
                    input_tokens: 1,
                    output_tokens: 1,
                    ..Default::default()
                },
                finish_reason: FinishReason::Stop,
                thinking: None,
                parts: None,
            })
        }
    }

    /// The tool names on the main loop's request for one turn whose words
    /// are `content`, with `tools` registered by name.
    async fn offered(workspace_path: Option<String>, content: &str, tools: &[&str]) -> Vec<String> {
        let captured = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
        let router = openalpaca_llm::LlmRouter::single_provider(
            Arc::new(Capturing(captured.clone())),
            openalpaca_llm::ProviderType::Anthropic,
            "claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929".to_string(),
        );
        let orch = make_orchestrator_with_tools_and_llm(Arc::new(router), tools);
        orch.handle_message(HandleRequest {
            request_id: Uuid::new_v4(),
            source: "cli".to_string(),
            content: content.to_string(),
            principal: Principal::System,
            scope: Scope::Global,
            lane_key: "user1:cli".to_string(),
            workspace_path,
            stream_id: None,
            model_override: None,
            unattended: false,
            turn_sink: None,
        })
        .await
        .expect("the turn answers");
        let requests = captured.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        requests
            .last()
            .expect("the main loop asked the model")
            .tools
            .iter()
            .map(|t| t.name.clone())
            .collect()
    }

    const EDIT_ASK: &str = "edit src/main.rs so the retry count is 5";

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_project_turn_asking_for_a_write_is_offered_file_edit_beside_file_write() {
        let project = tempfile::TempDir::new().unwrap();
        std::fs::create_dir(project.path().join(".git")).unwrap();
        let home = tempfile::TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let _env = crate::test_util::HomeStoreGuard::set(&home.path().join(".openalpaca"));

        let names = offered(
            Some(project.path().to_string_lossy().to_string()),
            EDIT_ASK,
            &["file_write", "file_edit"],
        )
        .await;

        assert!(names.contains(&"file_write".to_string()), "{names:?}");
        assert!(names.contains(&"file_edit".to_string()), "{names:?}");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_turn_with_no_project_is_offered_file_write_without_file_edit() {
        let home = tempfile::TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let _env = crate::test_util::HomeStoreGuard::set(&home.path().join(".openalpaca"));

        let names = offered(None, EDIT_ASK, &["file_write", "file_edit"]).await;

        assert!(names.contains(&"file_write".to_string()), "{names:?}");
        assert!(!names.contains(&"file_edit".to_string()), "{names:?}");
    }
}
```

  (a) `crates/openalpaca_core/src/tools/builtins/mod.rs`, after the line

```rust
/// The lead's ruling R-T14: the one "project turn" predicate — the turn's
/// request carries a root the store paths read as a project
/// (`scope_from_context`'s project arm: non-blank and absolute). The main
/// loop computes it once per turn and hands it to every offer that depends
/// on it (`file_edit` beside `file_write`, S4b; the file readers, S5).
pub(crate) fn is_project_turn(ctx: &ToolContext) -> bool {
    matches!(
        artifact_write::scope_from_context(ctx),
        openalpaca_storage::store::StoreScope::Project(_)
    )
}

```

  (b) `crates/openalpaca_core/src/orchestrator/query_handler/mod.rs`, after the closing `}` of `fn apply_send_keepalive`:

```rust
/// R48 (storage design §13): on a project turn the main chat is offered
/// `file_edit` beside `file_write`, by the same keywords — a change inside a
/// file is asked for in the words a write is (`suggest_tools`: a write verb,
/// `edit` among them, and a file name). With no project `file_edit` refuses
/// every call, so it is not offered there.
fn offer_file_edit_beside_file_write(tool_names: &mut Vec<String>, project_turn: bool) {
    if project_turn
        && tool_names.iter().any(|name| name == "file_write")
        && !tool_names.iter().any(|name| name == "file_edit")
    {
        tool_names.push("file_edit".to_string());
    }
}
```

  (`crates/openalpaca_core/src/security/confirmation.rs:33-36`, `ConfirmationRequest::preview`;
  `crates/openalpaca_api/src/events/mod.rs:248-251`, `ToolConfirmationRequested.preview`). S2's `write_card` (the path)

- **C-S4b-4 — R47's order, refined.** §7.1 orders the work resolve → read + match → copy → write → row. `check_pre_edit`
  (ST-17's cap, R46) depends only on the file's size and the loop, so S4b asks it after `metadata` and before the read
  — the copy itself (`keep_pre_edit_copy`) still comes after the match, as R47 says. Without this, a file far above the

- **C-S4b-5 — §7.1's refusal table is short of four cases the body meets**, each given one sentence here (*Choices*):
  a path that is neither a folder nor a regular file (a FIFO would block the read); the 10 MB bound on the file read
  (`file_read`'s own sentence) and on the file left behind; an I/O error from `metadata`
  (`Cannot access '{path}': {e}`), the read (`Failed to read file '{path}': {e}`) and the write

- **C-S4b-6 — interfaces §1.6 lists S4b among the callers of `WorkingFolder::ensure()`.** `file_edit` acts only in a

### Open points

- **The card can go stale before the click.** The card is planned when it is raised; the body plans again after the
  approval (up to `confirmation_timeout_secs`, 300 s by default, later). If the file changed in between, the body edits
  what is there then — the same `old_string`/`new_string` the person approved, possibly at another line or a different
  number of times under `replace_all` — or refuses if `old_string` no longer occurs. Comparing the approved plan with
  the body's (line, count, the file's hash) and refusing on a difference is not built; it would need the card's plan
  carried to the body. Recorded, not built: S6.6 writes it into design §18 (the lead's ruling R-T16).
- **The bytes read and the bytes copied can differ.** Between the plan's read and `keep_pre_edit_copy` another writer
  can change the file; the copy then holds that newer content, which the edit (computed from the older read) replaces.
  Nothing is lost — the copy has it — but the edit is not a compare-and-swap. Same remedy as above, not built;
  S6.6 records it in design §18 (R-T16).
- **CRLF with a one-line `old_string` — settled (the lead's ruling R-T11):** a file whose every line break is
  `\r\n` (no lone `\n`) keeps that: `apply_edit` writes `new_string`'s lone `\n` as `\r\n` there even when
  `old_string` holds no line break, pinned by `a_two_line_new_string_in_an_all_crlf_file_keeps_it_all_crlf`. A file
  that already mixes the two keeps what the model wrote.
- **In the skill tier, nested skills, plugin skills and plugin agents `file_edit` is always refused (R46)**, because
  the file it edits always exists and those loops keep no session log. R46's sentence names the way out ("ask for the
  change in the conversation itself"). The manuals' R46 paragraph (S6) should say it covers `file_edit` whole.
- **A template naming the capability `file_edit` while denying `file_write`** is handed no `file_edit`
  (`resolve_capabilities` drops a tool that provides a denied capability), yet its sandbox admits a call named
  `file_edit`, because the allow list holds the template's capability strings and the check is a name match — the
  documented "a tool named like a listed string is admitted" rule (CLAUDE.md, *Execution Topology*). No shipped
  template does this; recorded, not changed.
- **A store seeded before F1 whose template still carries an explicit `require_confirmation_for` list** never prompts
  for `file_edit` (interfaces §10.1's residue, S6 records it).
- **The S3→S4b window.** S3's `<working_folder>` note for a project turn (interfaces §1.3) already names `file_edit`,
  which is not registered until S4b.1: between the two the model is told of a tool it cannot call (a call is refused
  as not on its surface). Unreleased commits only, closed by S4b.1, like interfaces §10 C8; S6 records it with C8.
- **`apps/openalpaca-gui/src/lib/chat-stream.ts:132` — taken by S6a.12 (consistency pass); was owned by nobody.** Its doc comment on the stream's `preview`
  says the preview is composed "from the notes, never from the call's arguments" — false since S2's `write_card` and
  plainly so with `edit_card`. Interfaces §4.6 names only `ToolConfirmationBanner.tsx`, and neither S6a's nor S6's
  draft touches `chat-stream.ts`. S4b changes no GUI file (no bun gate); S6a should take it with the banner's comment.
- Checked against the drafts, not yet compiled (cargo-only until S1–S4a land): every name S4b consumes from S1–S4a
  (the *Before you start* list) has the signature and visibility used here — `working_folder` and
  `WorkingFolderRefusal` (S2.1), `FolderRules` `pub(super)` and `resolve_workspace_path_for_write(path, root, rules)`
  (S1), `traversal_rule` in `tools/registry/mod.rs` (S1), `pre_edit`'s four items (S4a.10),
  `record_tool_project_file` (S4a.11), `GuardedProject` with `root`, `ctx()`, `scratch_ctx()`, `home_root()`
  (S2.1), `ArtifactRecord.in_project` / `ArtifactQuery.in_project` (S4a.2), `command_card` / `write_card` (S2.2,
  S2.3). The refusal texts S4b.1's tests pin whole — §2's `.git` sentence, §6.2's cap and R46 sentences with

- Settled against S4a's draft (S4a's own tests pin them): `keep_pre_edit_copy` passes `path` as given into the

### What this slice does

An agent can now look around the folder it works in and read back what it saved. `file_list` (R40) lists one folder
of the working folder — the project, or the conversation's scratch folder — read-only and never asking (ST-16).
`artifact_read` (R41) reads a by-product back by its id, paged like `read_result`, for the turn's owner and only from
the turn's project or from no project; it refuses a result file in the project, which is `file_read`'s. Every place
that hands the model a by-product's id now points at it: `file_write`'s by-product result says "call artifact_read
with …", `file_read`'s description names it, and `task_status` and a workspace entry already carry the id
(`task_status` pinned by S5.5; the workspace entry already by HEAD's `workspace_read_names_the_artifact_behind_a_preview`).
R42 decides who holds them: `file_list` comes with the `file_read` capability and `artifact_read` with `read_result`
(all nine shipped templates name it), so subagents get them with no template edit; the lead gets `file_read`,
`file_list` and `artifact_read` on its hand-built surface in code and still holds no tool that writes, edits or runs
anything in the project; the main chat gets `artifact_read` on every turn with a database and `file_read` and
`file_list` on every project turn — "a project turn" being S4b.4's one predicate, computed once per turn (the lead's
ruling R-T14) — and `file_list` wherever `file_read` is, by keyword too (R-T6). §15: `writing_agent` gains
`file_read`; the relay rules and `start_workflow`'s description stop saying only a workflow can write a file, and
the relay rules say a file asked for with no writing tool on the surface is `start_workflow`'s (R-T7); `artifact_write`'s description says it saves by-products
(ST-11). No route, refusal code, migration, event or GUI file changes.

```rust
// --- file_list ---

/// The most entries one `file_list` call shows (R40). Past it the listing
/// ends with one line saying how many more there are: a folder of thousands
/// of files is listed a subfolder at a time, not poured into the context.
const FILE_LIST_MAX_ENTRIES: usize = 500;

/// `file_list` (R40): one folder of the working folder — the project, or the
/// conversation's scratch folder — never recursive and never asking (ST-16).
/// Resolved like `file_read`'s path: relative, no `..`, under the canonical
/// root, and in a project `.openalpaca` refused (R32).
struct FileListTool;

#[async_trait]
impl BuiltInTool for FileListTool {
    async fn execute(&self, _arguments: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<String, String> {
        Err(WorkingFolderRefusal::NoContext.to_string())
    }

    async fn execute_with_context(
        &self,
        arguments: &serde_json::Value,
        ctx: &ToolContext,
    ) -> Result<String, String> {
        let path = arguments
            .get("path")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
            .ok_or_else(|| "Missing required parameter: path".to_string())?;
        // R26, R27, R44: the project's folder, or the conversation's scratch
        // folder (made on first use), and R32's rules for it — the resolution
        // `file_read` makes; a refusal is its own sentence, before anything
        // is listed.
        let (root, rules) = acting_folder(ctx)?;
        let dir = resolve_workspace_path(path, &root, rules)?;
        let metadata = tokio::fs::metadata(&dir)
            .await
            .map_err(|e| format!("Cannot access '{path}': {e}"))?;
        if !metadata.is_dir() {
            return Err(format!(
                "'{path}' is a file, not a folder; read it with file_read."
            ));
        }
        list_folder(path, &dir).await
    }
}

/// Read `dir`'s entries and lay them out. `DirEntry::metadata` does not
/// follow a link, so a link is shown as one (`@`) rather than as what it
/// points at; a directory gets a trailing `/`, a file its size, anything
/// else (a socket, a pipe) its bare name.
async fn list_folder(path: &str, dir: &Path) -> Result<String, String> {
    let cannot = |e: std::io::Error| format!("Cannot list '{path}': {e}");
    let mut reader = tokio::fs::read_dir(dir).await.map_err(cannot)?;
    let mut entries: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();
    while let Some(entry) = reader.next_entry().await.map_err(cannot)? {
        let name = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        let shown = match entry.metadata().await {
            Ok(meta) if meta.file_type().is_symlink() => format!("{name}@"),
            Ok(meta) if meta.is_dir() => format!("{name}/"),
            Ok(meta) if meta.is_file() => format!("{name}  {} bytes", meta.len()),
            _ => name.clone(),
        };
        entries.push((name, shown));
    }
    Ok(format_listing(path, dir, entries))
}

/// The listing's text: `{path} ({abs}): {n} entries`, then one line per
/// entry sorted by name in byte order, at most [`FILE_LIST_MAX_ENTRIES`] of
/// them, then — past that — how many were left out. Names are not escaped:
/// this is a tool result, not an approval surface.
fn format_listing(path: &str, dir: &Path, mut entries: Vec<(String, String)>) -> String {
    // By name in byte order: the tuple sorts on its first field, and names in
    // one folder are unique (and `sort()` keeps clippy's sort lints quiet).
    entries.sort();
    let total = entries.len();
    let mut out = format!("{path} ({}): {total} entries", dir.display());
    for (_, shown) in entries.iter().take(FILE_LIST_MAX_ENTRIES) {
        out.push('\n');
        out.push_str(shown);
    }
    if total > FILE_LIST_MAX_ENTRIES {
        out.push_str(&format!(
            "\n... and {} more entries not shown — list a subfolder",
            total - FILE_LIST_MAX_ENTRIES
        ));
    }
    out
}

pub(super) fn file_list_tool() -> RegisteredTool {
    RegisteredTool {
        definition: ToolDefinition {
            name: "file_list".to_string(),
            description: "List one folder under the working folder (the project, or this \
                conversation's scratch folder): its files with their sizes, its folders \
                marked with a trailing /, links with @. Not recursive — list a subfolder to \
                go deeper. Read a file with file_read."
                .to_string(),
            parameters: serde_json::json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "The folder to list, relative to the working folder; '.' is the working folder itself."
                    }
                },
                "required": ["path"],
                "additionalProperties": false
            }),
            // Closed and fully required: `strict_mode_compatible` accepts it,
            // so it is one of the two builtins that keep the flag on the wire.
            strict: Some(true),
            input_examples: Some(vec![
                serde_json::json!({"path": "."}),
                serde_json::json!({"path": "src"}),
            ]),
        },
        backend: ToolBackend::BuiltIn(Arc::new(FileListTool)),
        // R42: comes with `file_read`, so a template that reads files lists
        // them with no template edit — and one that denies `file_read` is
        // handed neither (`resolve_capabilities`' provided-capability filter).
        provides_capabilities: vec!["file_read".into(), "file_list".into()],
        exempt_from_timeout: false,
        annotations: annotations_for_builtin("file_list"),
        version: env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION").to_string(),
        author: "builtin".to_string(),
        created_at: chrono::Utc::now(),
    }
}
```

```bash
folder, one level at a time — files with their sizes, folders with a trailing
/, links with @, sorted by name, at most 500 entries. It resolves its path as
file_read does (relative, no '..', under the root, .openalpaca refused in a
project), never asks (ST-16), and comes with the file_read capability (R42).
Strict-mode compatible, so the builtins' strict walk now counts 22.
```

  Put this above the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `artifact_read.rs`:

```rust
//! `artifact_read` — read a by-product back by its id (storage design §14,
//! R41), modelled on `read_result`: the same pages, the same footer shape.
//!
//! A by-product is what `artifact_write` saves — and `file_write` with no
//! project — in OpenAlpaca's artifact store. A result file written into the
//! project is a pointer row (ST-12) that `file_read` reads where it is, so
//! this tool refuses one. The scope is the turn's owner, and a by-product of
//! the turn's project or of no project: another project's is refused, so a
//! conversation never reads into a project it is not in. An upload of the
//! owner's (`origin = upload`) reads like a by-product: it is the owner's own
//! file, and refusing it would guard nothing.

use std::sync::Arc;

use async_trait::async_trait;
use openalpaca_llm::ToolDefinition;
use openalpaca_storage::store::project_root_of;
use openalpaca_storage::{ArtifactError, ArtifactKind, ArtifactStore, Database};

use super::annotations_for_builtin;
use super::artifact_write::scope_from_context;
use super::read_result::{DEFAULT_LIMIT, MAX_LIMIT, page_bounds, read_page_bytes};
use crate::tools::registry::{BuiltInTool, RegisteredTool, ToolBackend, ToolContext};

struct ArtifactReadTool {
    /// Absent (tests, the CLI) refuses at call time, as `artifact_write` does.
    db: Option<Database>,
}

#[async_trait]
impl BuiltInTool for ArtifactReadTool {
    async fn execute(&self, _arguments: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<String, String> {
        Err("artifact_read requires execution context — use execute_with_context".to_string())
    }

    async fn execute_with_context(
        &self,
        arguments: &serde_json::Value,
        ctx: &ToolContext,
    ) -> Result<String, String> {
        let db = self
            .db
            .as_ref()
            .ok_or_else(|| "artifact_read requires database context".to_string())?;
        let id = arguments
            .get("artifact_id")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
            .map(str::trim)
            .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
            .ok_or_else(|| "Missing required parameter: artifact_id".to_string())?;
        let owner = ctx.owner_id.as_deref().ok_or_else(|| {
            "artifact_read cannot read this turn's artifacts: it has no owner.".to_string()
        })?;
        let unreadable = |e: String| format!("artifact_read: '{id}' could not be read: {e}");

        let record = ArtifactStore::new(db)
            .get(id, owner)
            .map_err(|e| unreadable(format!("{e:#}")))?
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("artifact_read: no artifact '{id}' of yours."))?;

        // The turn's project, as the address artifact_write records for it
        // (`project_root_of`), or none. A by-product of no project is the
        // owner's from any turn; one of a project only from that project.
        let turn_project = project_root_of(&scope_from_context(ctx))
            .map_err(|e| unreadable(format!("{e:#}")))?;
        if let Some(root) = record.project_root.as_deref()
            && turn_project.as_deref() != Some(root)
        {
            return Err(format!(
                "artifact_read: '{id}' belongs to another project ({root}); read it from a \
                 conversation in that project."
            ));
        }
        if record.in_project {
            let rel = record.rel_path.as_deref().unwrap_or(&record.name);
            return Err(format!(
                "artifact_read: '{id}' is a file in the project ({rel}); read it with file_read."
            ));
        }
        let kind = record
            .kind
            .unwrap_or_else(|| ArtifactKind::for_mime(&record.mime_type));
        if matches!(kind, ArtifactKind::Image | ArtifactKind::Binary) {
            let article = if kind == ArtifactKind::Image { "an" } else { "a" };
            return Err(format!(
                "artifact_read: '{id}' is {article} {} artifact; artifact_read returns text only.",
                kind.as_str()
            ));
        }

        // The store's read: it stats the head and, when the bytes were edited
        // by hand, records them as a version first — so the version reported
        // is the rotated record's, not the one read above. Hashing is
        // blocking work, so the whole call runs on the blocking pool.
        let store_db = db.clone();
        let owned_id = id.to_string();
        let resolved = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
            ArtifactStore::new(&store_db).resolve_content_with_edit(&owned_id, None)
        })
        .await
        .map_err(|e| unreadable(e.to_string()))?;
        let (path, rotated) = match resolved {
            Ok(found) => found,
            Err(e) => {
                return Err(match e.downcast_ref::<ArtifactError>() {
                    Some(ArtifactError::Gone { path, .. }) => {
                        format!("artifact_read: the bytes of '{id}' are gone ({path}).")
                    }
                    Some(ArtifactError::NotFound { .. }) => {
                        format!("artifact_read: no artifact '{id}' of yours.")
                    }
                    _ => unreadable(format!("{e:#}")),
                });
            }
        };
        let version = rotated.as_ref().map_or(record.version, |r| r.version);

        let offset = arguments
            .get("offset")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_u64())
            .unwrap_or(0);
        let limit = arguments
            .get("limit")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_u64())
            .map(|n| n as usize)
            .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_LIMIT)
            .clamp(1, MAX_LIMIT);
        let (buf, total) = read_page_bytes(&path, offset, limit).await.map_err(|_| {
            format!(
                "artifact_read: the bytes of '{id}' are gone ({}).",
                path.display()
            )
        })?;
        let from = (offset as usize).min(total);
        let (start, end) = page_bounds(&buf, limit, from + buf.len() >= total);
        let (page_start, page_end) = (from + start, from + end);

        let mut out = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf[start..end]).into_owned();
        out.push_str(&format!(
            "\n\n[artifact_read: bytes {page_start}–{page_end} of {total} from {}, version {version}",
            record.name
        ));
        if page_end < total {
            out.push_str(&format!("; next offset={page_end}"));
        }
        out.push(']');
        Ok(out)
    }
}

pub(super) fn artifact_read_tool(db: Option<Database>) -> RegisteredTool {
    RegisteredTool {
        definition: ToolDefinition {
            name: "artifact_read".to_string(),
            description: "Read a by-product back by its id: a draft, a hand-off or another file \
                saved with artifact_write (or with file_write when there is no project). Pages \
                like read_result. A file written into the project is not a by-product — read it \
                with file_read."
                .to_string(),
            parameters: serde_json::json!({
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "artifact_id": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "The id of a by-product, as artifact_write's result, a workspace entry's file_asset_id or task_status names it."
                    },
                    "offset": {
                        "type": "integer",
                        "description": "Byte offset to start from. Defaults to 0; a partial page tells you the next offset."
                    },
                    "limit": {
                        "type": "integer",
                        "description": "Maximum bytes to return. Defaults to 8192, capped at 65536."
                    }
                },
                "required": ["artifact_id"]
            }),
            // `offset` and `limit` are optional, which strict mode cannot
            // express, so the tool is not marked (CLAUDE.md Gotchas).
            strict: None,
            input_examples: Some(vec![serde_json::json!({
                "artifact_id": "0b6f3c2a-6d1e-4c5b-9a8f-2e7d4c1b0a93",
                "offset": 8192,
                "limit": 8192
            })]),
        },
        backend: ToolBackend::BuiltIn(Arc::new(ArtifactReadTool { db })),
        // R42: comes with `read_result`, which every shipped template names,
        // so a seeded install's agents read by-products with no template edit.
        provides_capabilities: vec!["read_result".into(), "artifact_read".into()],
        exempt_from_timeout: false,
        annotations: annotations_for_builtin("artifact_read"),
        version: env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION").to_string(),
        author: "builtin".to_string(),
        created_at: chrono::Utc::now(),
    }
```

### Task S5.3: the two new read tools never raise a card (ST-16)

**Files:**
- Test `crates/openalpaca_core/src/tools/builtins/tests.rs` (a new test after the S5.2 one). No production change.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `SandboxManager::with_defaults(Arc<ToolRegistry>, EventBus)`, `set_confirmation_broker`,
  `execute_tool(&ToolCall, &SandboxPolicy, &ToolContext)`; `ConfirmationBroker::{new, pending_count}`;
  `crate::security::sandbox::effective_confirmation_set(&SandboxPolicy, &ToolRegistry) -> Vec<String>`;
  `SystemEvent::ToolConfirmationRequested`; `builtin_tools(db, daemon_config, web_search_config)`; `GuardedProject`.
- Produces: nothing new; pins ST-16 for `file_list` and `artifact_read`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the test.**

```rust
// --- ST-16: the read tools Stage 2 adds never ask ---

/// ST-16 (storage design §12): `file_list` and `artifact_read` are read-only
/// and never raise an approval card. They are outside the confirmation set
/// the sandbox derives from the registered annotations, and run through the
/// sandbox with a broker and an `unattended` policy — under which a tool that
/// needed approval is refused at once — they run, and nothing waits on the
/// broker or reaches the bus as a confirmation request.
#[tokio::test]
async fn file_list_and_artifact_read_run_with_no_approval_card() {
    use crate::bus::EventBus;
    use crate::security::capabilities::Allowlist;
    use crate::security::confirmation::ConfirmationBroker;
    use crate::security::sandbox::{SandboxManager, SandboxPolicy, effective_confirmation_set};
    use crate::tools::ToolRegistry;

    let gp = crate::test_util::GuardedProject::new();
    let db_dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let db = openalpaca_storage::Database::open(&db_dir.path().join("test.db")).unwrap();
    let registry = ToolRegistry::default();
    for tool in builtin_tools(Some(db), None, None) {
        registry.register(tool).unwrap();
    }
    let registry = Arc::new(registry);
    let bus = EventBus::new(64);
    let mut rx = bus.subscribe();
    let mut sandbox = SandboxManager::with_defaults(registry.clone(), bus);
    let broker = Arc::new(ConfirmationBroker::new());
    sandbox.set_confirmation_broker(broker.clone());
    let policy = SandboxPolicy {
        agent_id: "explore_agent::a1".to_string(),
        allowed_capabilities: Allowlist::Unrestricted,
        denied_capabilities: vec![],
        require_confirmation_for: vec![],
        max_tool_calls: None,
        max_tool_runtime_secs: 30,
        stream_id: None,
        lane_key: None,
        confirmation_timeout_secs: Some(300),
        auto_approve: false,
        unattended: true,
    };

    let set = effective_confirmation_set(&policy, &registry);
    for name in ["file_list", "artifact_read"] {
        assert!(!set.contains(&name.to_string()), "{name} never asks: {set:?}");
    }

    std::fs::write(gp.root.join("README.md"), "hi").unwrap();
    let listed = sandbox
        .execute_tool(
            &openalpaca_llm::ToolCall {
                id: "tu-list".to_string(),
                name: "file_list".to_string(),
                arguments: serde_json::json!({"path": "."}),
            },
            &policy,
            &gp.ctx(),
        )
        .await
        .expect("file_list runs on an unattended turn");
    assert!(listed.contains("README.md  2 bytes"), "{listed}");

    let refused = sandbox
        .execute_tool(
            &openalpaca_llm::ToolCall {
                id: "tu-read".to_string(),
                name: "artifact_read".to_string(),
                arguments: serde_json::json!({"artifact_id": "no-such-id"}),
            },
            &policy,
            &gp.ctx(),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        refused.contains("no artifact 'no-such-id' of yours"),
        "the tool ran and answered, not the approval gate: {refused}"
    );
    assert!(!refused.contains("needs your approval"), "{refused}");

    assert_eq!(broker.pending_count(), 0, "nothing was raised");
    while let Ok(event) = rx.try_recv() {
        assert!(
            !matches!(
                event,
                crate::events::SystemEvent::ToolConfirmationRequested { .. }
            ),
            "no card was raised: {event:?}"
        );
    }
}
```

```rust
    /// A registered builtin, run with a context.
    async fn call_registered(
        tool: &RegisteredTool,
        args: &serde_json::Value,
        ctx: &ToolContext,
    ) -> Result<String, String> {
        match &tool.backend {
            ToolBackend::BuiltIn(handler) => handler.execute_with_context(args, ctx).await,
            _ => panic!("{} is a builtin", tool.definition.name),
        }
    }

    /// FW-1's five parts, pinned whole (CLAUDE.md Gotchas): the write is
    /// done, as which artifact, version and absolute path; where this
    /// conversation's files are kept; that the Library lists it and it is the
    /// deliverable; how to read it back — by the id `artifact_read` takes
    /// (R41); and how to change it. Read back by that id from the same turn
    /// it is what was written; written again, it is the next version (with no
    /// task both writes land in `loose/<UTC date>`, so a run straddling UTC
    /// midnight would see two version-1 artifacts).
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_by_product_result_is_pinned_whole_in_five_parts() {
        let gp = crate::test_util::GuardedProject::new();
        let db_dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let db = Database::open(&db_dir.path().join("test.db")).unwrap();
        let write = file_write_tool(Some(db.clone()), None);
        let read = super::super::artifact_read::artifact_read_tool(Some(db.clone()));
        let ctx = ToolContext {
            owner_id: Some("owner-test".to_string()),
            ..gp.scratch_ctx()
        };
        let path = "reports/pasta-night.md";

        for (i, content) in ["# Pasta night\n", "# Pasta night, again\n"]
            .into_iter()
            .enumerate()
        {
            let version = i + 1;
            let out = call_registered(
                &write,
                &serde_json::json!({"path": path, "content": content}),
                &ctx,
            )
            .await
            .unwrap();
            let row = openalpaca_storage::ArtifactStore::new(&db)
                .list(&openalpaca_storage::ArtifactQuery::new("owner-test"))
                .unwrap()
                .0
                .remove(0);
            assert_eq!(
                out,
                format!(
                    "Saved: {path} is the artifact \"{}\", version {version}, at {}. This \
                     conversation has no project folder, so its files are kept in \
                     OpenAlpaca's artifact store. It is listed in the Library. This file is \
                     the deliverable: tell the user it is saved at that absolute path, and do \
                     not write another copy with the shell or any other tool. To read it back, \
                     call artifact_read with \"{}\". To change it, call file_write with \
                     \"{path}\" again; that saves its next version.",
                    row.name, row.storage_path, row.id
                )
            );

            let back = call_registered(&read, &serde_json::json!({"artifact_id": row.id}), &ctx)
                .await
                .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("artifact_read({}): {e}", row.id));
            let n = content.len();
            assert_eq!(
                back,
                format!(
                    "{content}\n\n[artifact_read: bytes 0–{n} of {n} from {}, version {version}]",
                    row.name
                )
            );
        }
    }

    /// R41: `file_read` points at `artifact_read` for a by-product.
    #[test]
    fn file_read_names_artifact_read_for_a_by_product() {
        let description = file_read_tool().definition.description;
        assert!(
            description.contains("For a by-product, use artifact_read."),
            "{description}"
        );
    }
```
