```rust
/// R42 and the lead's rulings R-T6 and R-T14: on a project turn the main chat
/// is offered `file_read` — its working folder is the project and reading
/// never asks (ST-16), so it does not wait for a keyword — and `file_list`
/// comes wherever `file_read` is, by a keyword or by the project. Each name
/// is added once.
fn offer_file_readers(tool_names: &mut Vec<String>, project_turn: bool) {
    if project_turn && !tool_names.iter().any(|name| name == "file_read") {
        tool_names.push("file_read".to_string());
    }
    if tool_names.iter().any(|name| name == "file_read")
        && !tool_names.iter().any(|name| name == "file_list")
    {
        tool_names.push("file_list".to_string());
    }
}
```


```rust
        let path = entry.unwrap().path();
        if path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()) != Some("md") {
            continue;
        }
        let body = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap();
        let doc = parse_agent_markdown(&body)
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{} does not parse: {e}", path.display()));
        let agent = doc.to_subagent("a1", "task-1");
        let surface: Vec<String> = crate::tools::resolve_agent_tools(&agent, &registry, None)
            .into_iter()
            .map(|d| d.name)
            .collect();
        let has = |name: &str| surface.iter().any(|n| n == name);
        let names_file_read = doc.frontmatter.capabilities.iter().any(|c| c == "file_read");

        assert_eq!(has("file_read"), names_file_read, "{}: {surface:?}", path.display());
        assert_eq!(has("file_list"), names_file_read, "{}: {surface:?}", path.display());
        assert!(has("artifact_read"), "{}: {surface:?}", path.display());
        if doc.frontmatter.id == "writing_agent" {
            assert!(names_file_read, "writing_agent reads files (§15)");
        }
        seen += 1;
    }
    assert!(seen >= 9, "every shipped template was checked, not {seen}");
}
```

### Spec conflicts

- **C-S5-1 — `test_all_tools_have_strict_enabled` asserts every builtin is strict.** `builtins/tests.rs:57` walks
  every tool `builtin_tools_with_persona_context` returns and asserts `strict == Some(true)`. The sheet (§7.3, §7.4,
  §9) gives `artifact_read` — and S4b's `file_edit` — `strict: None`, and says of the strict tests only that S4b
  changes nothing in `every_builtin_goes_to_openai_with_strict_only_where_strict_mode_accepts_it`. With `None`, the
  first test fails at S4b and again at S5. Smallest correction: the test names its exemptions and asserts `None` for
  them, `Some(true)` for the rest. S4b.1 builds the list for `file_edit` (`const NOT_STRICT: &[&str] =
  &["file_edit"];`, its C-S4b-1); S5.2 extends it to `&["file_edit", "artifact_read"]`, the type unchanged. The alternative —
  marking them `Some(true)` as `read_result` is, and letting the serializer drop the flag — is what the Gotcha warns
  against ("quietly loses strict mode").
- **C-S5-2 — the lead's three readers "in code" need the lead's deny list.** Sheet §7.5 and §9 put `file_read`,
  `file_list`, `artifact_read` on the lead's surface unconditionally. `admit_tool_surface`
  (`security/sandbox/mod.rs:121`) admits every definition on the surface by name, and the sandbox's deny check is by
  tool name, so a lead template that denies `file_read` would be handed and admitted `file_list` (and, denying
  `read_result`, `artifact_read`). Smallest correction (S5.7): skip a tool whose name or a provided capability the
  lead's `constraints.denied_capabilities` names — the filter `resolve_capabilities` already applies to subagents —
  pinned by `a_lead_that_denies_file_read_is_handed_neither_file_reader`.
- **C-S5-3 — `artifact_read` reads through `resolve_content_with_edit`, not `resolve_content(id, None)`.** Sheet §7.3
  says `resolve_content`. That call runs `check_head`, which records a hand edit of a by-product as a new version
  before resolving the path, so the footer's `version {v}` read off the earlier `get` would be stale. Smallest
  correction: `resolve_content_with_edit(id, None)` and the rotated record's version when there is one; same bytes,
  same path.
- **C-S5-4 — the lead surface test the sheet names cannot see the builtins.** Sheet §8.2: "`runner/lead_agent/tests.rs`
  surface test (~:1887) gains `file_read`, `file_list`, `artifact_read`". That test's registry holds two extension
  tools and no builtin (`test_lead_loop_request_carries_extension_defs_and_invoke_skill`), so nothing could put
  `file_read` on its surface. Correction: a new test with the builtins registered (S5.7); the old one is untouched.
- **C-S5-5 — "a project turn" for the main loop is the store's reading, not `is_some()`.** Sheet §7.5 says
  `ctx.request_workspace_root.is_some()`. `scope_from_context` (`artifact_write.rs:56`) — what every store path reads
  the field as — treats an empty, blank or relative value as no project. Correction (S5.6):
  `matches!(scope_from_context(ctx), StoreScope::Project(_))`, so a value no tool would act on as a project does not
  offer the project readers. Ruled by the lead (R-T14): that reading is the one predicate,
  `builtins::is_project_turn`, which S4b.4 builds and the main loop computes once per turn; S5.6 consumes it.
- **C-S5-6 — `read_result`'s two limits are shared too.** Sheet §7.3 makes only `page_bounds` `pub(super)`.
  `artifact_read` also needs the 8192 default and the 65536 cap the description promises ("Defaults to 8192, capped
  at 65536"); S5.2 makes `DEFAULT_LIMIT` and `MAX_LIMIT` `pub(super)` rather than restating the numbers.
- **C-S5-7 — the not-text refusal's article.** Sheet §7.3 fixes `artifact_read: '{id}' is a {kind} artifact;
  artifact_read returns text only.` for kinds `image` and `binary`, which reads "is a image artifact". S5.2 writes
  `is an image artifact` / `is a binary artifact` (the article chosen by kind), pinned by
  `an_image_or_binary_by_product_is_refused_as_not_text`; every other sentence of §7.3 is used verbatim.

### Open points

- **A no-file-name "save this" request — settled (the lead's ruling R-T7).** Under `tool_selection = "core_union"`

## Stage 2 — slice S6a: the app's surfaces for result files

Read at `d484a56a` (`feat/markdown-memory`). Spec: `spec-stage2.md` §13 *Surfaces*, ST-12, ST-18, R37, R38 (its app
half), §16 step (6); the shared names are `interfaces.md` §5.2, §5.4, §5.7, §5.8, §4.6, §8.5. Every `file:line` below
was read at HEAD and will drift: locate by content.

### What this slice does

From S4a on, a file an agent writes into its project is the project's own file with a **pointer row** —
`in_project = true`, `name` = `rel_path` = its path in the project, `path` = the real file, version 1 with no
versions — and the daemon says on the row and on the `artifact_written` frame whether `Open` is offered
(`openable`, ST-18). S6a makes the app draw that honestly. The `File written` card says `in the project`, draws no
`vN`, draws `Open` only for an openable kind and draws each write of the same file as its own card. The Library lists
by-products by default and the project's results behind a `Results in the project` chip; a result row carries a
`project` tag and its project's name; its detail and the chat file panel offer Preview alone (no History, no Diff)
and `Open` only when `openable`; every opener (the card, the palette, a run's files, the panel's `Library ↗`) lands
on the side the row is on. `Export` saves a result file under its base name (`main.rs`, not `src/main.rs`). The
Work detail lists a run's by-products under **Output** and the files it wrote into its project under **Written in the project**, one row each,
and its event log says `· in the project`. On the Rust side, `store::revealable_path` also admits a regular file under
the root of a project `projects::list()` records, so `Reveal in Finder` works on a result file of any kind. The Tauri
`reveal_path` asks it on the blocking pool. The banner's and `lib/chat-stream.ts`'s doc comments, `lib/reveal.ts`'s doc and the GUI README's
`reveal_path` line describe the result; `DESIGN_SPEC.md` and `API_MAP.md` are S6's (interfaces §8.4, S6.3d).
**Depends on S4a** (the wire fields, `?in_project=`, `OPEN_NOT_OFFERED`, and S4a.15's resolver-backed
`GET /v1/files/{id}/content`, which `Export` reads). No migration, no route, no refusal code, no event variant and no
`lib/api/*.ts` export change here, so `docs/api` does not change (`gen_api_docs.py --check` stays clean).

```rust
//! Which paths the app may show in their folder (Round G, G4; storage design
//! §13, ST-18).
//!
//! The GUI's `Reveal in Finder` hands the Tauri shell an artifact's `path`,
//! which the webview read from the daemon. The shell trusts the file system,
//! not the webview: [`revealable_path`] resolves the path — symlinks included —
//! and admits only a regular file under the home store, where every store file
//! lives — a project's included, in its folder under `projects/` (ST-1) — or
//! under the root of a project `projects/` records, where a file an agent
//! wrote into the project lives (ST-12). The shell then passes the answer to
//! the platform's reveal as an argument, never through a shell. Nothing here
//! opens, reads or changes the file.

use std::fmt;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use super::{home_root, projects};

/// Why [`revealable_path`] refused a path. `Display` is one sentence, written
/// to be shown as it is in a toast.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RevealRefusal {
    /// Nothing is there, or the path cannot be resolved. Carries the path as
    /// it was asked for.
    Missing(PathBuf),
    /// A directory, or anything else that is not a regular file. Carries the
    /// resolved path.
    NotAFile(PathBuf),
    /// The resolved file is under neither the home root nor the root of a
    /// registered project, or there is neither to compare with. A symlink
    /// inside either whose target is outside both lands here, with the target,
    /// and so does a file in an old in-project `.openalpaca/` of a folder no
    /// project records (ST-9). Inside a registered project such a file is
    /// under its root and is shown: showing a file in its folder reads
    /// nothing, and the file tools refuse `.openalpaca` themselves (R32).
    OutsideStore(PathBuf),
}

impl fmt::Display for RevealRefusal {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            RevealRefusal::Missing(path) => write!(
                f,
                "{} is not there any more, so it cannot be shown in its folder.",
                path.display()
            ),
            RevealRefusal::NotAFile(path) => write!(
                f,
                "{} is not a file, so it cannot be shown in its folder.",
                path.display()
            ),
            RevealRefusal::OutsideStore(path) => write!(
                f,
                "{} is not in an OpenAlpaca store or one of your projects, so it is not shown in \
                 its folder.",
                path.display()
            ),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for RevealRefusal {}

/// The canonical form of `path` when it may be shown in its folder: a
/// regular file whose canonical path is under the canonical home root
/// ([`home_root`], `OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE` honoured) or under the canonical
/// root of a project [`projects::list`] returns (ST-18: Reveal is what a file
/// written into the project is offered whatever its kind). Refused: a path
/// that does not resolve, anything that is not a regular file, and a file
/// under neither. The canonical path decides, so a symlink is judged by where
/// it leads. Reads `projects/` — one `project.json` per project — so a caller
/// on an async runtime asks it on the blocking pool.
pub fn revealable_path(path: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, RevealRefusal> {
    revealable_path_among(path, home_root().ok().as_deref(), &project_roots())
}

/// The roots of the projects `projects/` records — a missing one's included
/// (nothing under it resolves), one mid re-point by the root it is going to.
/// A `projects/` that cannot be read records none, with one WARN: a file in
/// the home store is still shown, and a project's file is refused as outside.
fn project_roots() -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    match projects::list() {
        Ok(found) => found.into_iter().map(|project| project.root).collect(),
        Err(e) => {
            tracing::warn!("Reveal in Finder reads no project roots: {e:#}");
            Vec::new()
        }
    }
}

/// [`revealable_path`] with the home root and the project roots passed in, so
/// the rule is testable without reading the environment or `projects/`.
fn revealable_path_among(
    path: &Path,
    home: Option<&Path>,
    project_roots: &[PathBuf],
) -> Result<PathBuf, RevealRefusal> {
    let canonical = path
        .canonicalize()
        .map_err(|_| RevealRefusal::Missing(path.to_path_buf()))?;
    let is_file = std::fs::metadata(&canonical).is_ok_and(|meta| meta.is_file());
    if !is_file {
        return Err(RevealRefusal::NotAFile(canonical));
    }
    let admitted = home.is_some_and(|home| is_under(&canonical, home))
        || project_roots.iter().any(|root| is_under(&canonical, root));
    if admitted {
        Ok(canonical)
    } else {
        Err(RevealRefusal::OutsideStore(canonical))
    }
}

/// Whether the canonical `file` is under `root`, compared with `root` resolved
/// too (as written when it cannot be), component by component — so
/// `/dev/app-evil/notes.md` is not under `/dev/app`.
fn is_under(file: &Path, root: &Path) -> bool {
    let root = root.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| root.to_path_buf());
    file.starts_with(root)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;
```

  Then in `apps/openalpaca-gui/src-tauri/src/lib.rs` replace the doc comment and body of `reveal_path` — the block
  from `/// Show a file in its folder: Finder with the file selected on macOS` through the closing `}` of
  `async fn reveal_path` — with:

```rust
/// Show a file in its folder: Finder with the file selected on macOS
/// (`open -R`), Explorer with it selected on Windows (`explorer /select,`),
/// and the folder holding it in the file manager elsewhere (`xdg-open`).
///
/// The path comes from the webview — an artifact's `path` as the daemon served
/// it — so the shell does not take it on trust: `store::revealable_path`
/// resolves it, symlinks included, and admits only a regular file in an
/// OpenAlpaca store or under the root of a project `projects/` records, where
/// a file an agent wrote into the project lives (storage design §13, ST-18:
/// Reveal answers for such a file whatever its kind). The platform program
/// gets that resolved path as an argument of its own, never through a shell.
/// This shows the file; opening it stays the daemon's route
/// (`POST /v1/files/{id}/open`). An error is one sentence, which the webview
/// shows as it is.
///
/// The check (it reads `projects/`) and the program both run on the blocking
/// pool, so a slow disk or file manager never stalls another `invoke`.
#[tauri::command]
async fn reveal_path(path: String) -> Result<(), String> {
    tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || {
        let path =
            store::revealable_path(Path::new(&path)).map_err(|refusal| refusal.to_string())?;
        reveal_in_folder(&path)
    })
    .await
    .map_err(|e| format!("Could not show the file in its folder: {e}."))?
}
```

  `src/views/library/LibraryView.tsx`, whole file:

```tsx
/**
 * The Library view (DESIGN_SPEC §2.4, §5.3).
 *
 * Two columns with the third resizer between them (`libListW`, 326 / 260–480,
 * drag direction +1). The list is `GET /v1/artifacts`, paged, on one side —
 * by-products by default (`?in_project=false`), the files agents wrote into a
 * project behind `Results in the project` (`?in_project=true`, storage design
 * §13); the kind chips and the selection are client state. Nothing on screen
 * is invented: an empty list is the daemon's own empty list, and a failed one
 * says what failed.
 */

import { Resizer } from "@/components/shell";
import { useArtifactFeed } from "@/hooks/useArtifacts";
import { useUiStore } from "@/stores/ui";

import { LibraryDetail } from "./LibraryDetail";
import { LibraryList } from "./LibraryList";

export default function LibraryView() {
  const width = useUiStore((s) => s.paneWidths.libListW);
  const kind = useUiStore((s) => s.libraryKind);
  const setKind = useUiStore((s) => s.setLibraryKind);
  const results = useUiStore((s) => s.libraryResults);
  const setResults = useUiStore((s) => s.setLibraryResults);
  const openArtifactId = useUiStore((s) => s.openArtifactId);
  const openArtifact = useUiStore((s) => s.openArtifact);
  const pins = useUiStore((s) => s.pins);

  const feed = useArtifactFeed({ inProject: results });

  return (
    <section aria-label="Library" className="flex min-w-0 flex-1 bg-main">
      <LibraryList
        width={width}
        kind={kind}
        onKindChange={setKind}
        results={results}
        onResultsChange={setResults}
        artifacts={feed.artifacts}
        total={feed.total}
        loading={feed.loading}
        error={feed.error}
        selectedId={openArtifactId}
        onSelect={openArtifact}
        pins={pins}
        hasMore={feed.hasMore}
        loadingMore={feed.loadingMore}
        onLoadMore={feed.loadMore}
      />
      <Resizer paneKey="libListW" direction={1} label="library list" />
      <LibraryDetail artifactId={openArtifactId} />
    </section>
  );
}
```

  `src/views/library/LibraryList.tsx`, whole file:

```tsx
/**
 * The Library's left column (DESIGN_SPEC §2.4, §3.29, §3.30).
 *
 * The Library has two sides (storage design §13): by-products — drafts,
 * hand-offs, uploads, a file saved with no project — by default, and the files
 * agents wrote into a project behind the `Results in the project` chip. The
 * side is a *query* (`?in_project=`), so the header count is the daemon's own
 * unpaged `total` for that side rather than the size of this page. The kind
 * chips narrow what is *shown*: they are a view filter, not a query, because
 * two of the seven labels (`Media`, `Output`) cover more than one artifact
 * kind and `?kind=` takes exactly one — filtering here keeps every chip
 * behaving the same way and keeps `total` meaning one thing. `Load more` is
 * what walks the rest of the side.
 *
 * Presentational: the query lives in `LibraryView`, so every state below is a
 * prop and can be rendered without a daemon.
 */

import {
  KIND_FILTERS,
  KindFilterChip,
  PaneHeader,
  SectionEmpty,
  matchesKindFilter,
  toFileKind,
} from "@/components/ui";
import type { Artifact } from "@/lib/api/artifacts";

import { LibraryRow } from "./LibraryRow";

/** The chip that switches the list to the files agents wrote into a project. */
export const RESULTS_FILTER = "Results in the project";

/** The design's own empty sentence, for the by-products side. */
export const LIBRARY_EMPTY =
  "Nothing in the library yet. Files the agents produce land here.";

/** The results side's empty sentence. */
export const RESULTS_EMPTY =
  "No files written into a project yet. A file an agent writes in your project's folder is listed here.";

export interface LibraryListProps {
  width: number;
  kind: string;
  onKindChange: (kind: string) => void;
  /** The side shown: `false` by-products (the default), `true` results. */
  results: boolean;
  onResultsChange: (results: boolean) => void;
  /** Every row loaded so far, in server order. */
  artifacts: readonly Artifact[];
  /** The unpaged count, or `null` while it is unknown. */
  total: number | null;
  loading: boolean;
  error: Error | null;
  selectedId: string | null;
  onSelect: (artifactId: string) => void;
  /** The optimistic pin cache; a row falls back to the server's own field. */
  pins: Record<string, boolean>;
  hasMore: boolean;
  loadingMore: boolean;
  onLoadMore: () => void;
}

export function LibraryList({
  width,
  kind,
  onKindChange,
  results,
  onResultsChange,
  artifacts,
  total,
  loading,
  error,
  selectedId,
  onSelect,
  pins,
  hasMore,
  loadingMore,
  onLoadMore,
}: LibraryListProps) {
  const rows = artifacts.filter((artifact) =>
    matchesKindFilter(kind, toFileKind(artifact.kind)),
  );

  return (
    <div
      style={{ width }}
      className="flex shrink-0 flex-col border-r border-line-subtle"
    >
      <PaneHeader
        title="Library"
        meta={total === null ? undefined : `${total} files`}
      />

      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-[5px] border-b border-line-hair px-[14px] pt-[12px] pb-[8px]">
        {KIND_FILTERS.map((label) => (
          <KindFilterChip
            key={label}
            label={label}
            selected={kind === label}
            onSelect={onKindChange}
          />
        ))}
        <KindFilterChip
          label={RESULTS_FILTER}
          selected={results}
          onSelect={() => onResultsChange(!results)}
          className="ml-auto"
        />
      </div>

      <div className="sc min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto p-[8px]">
        {error !== null ? (
          <SectionEmpty note={error.message}>
            The library could not be loaded.
          </SectionEmpty>
        ) : loading && artifacts.length === 0 ? (
          <SectionEmpty>Loading the library…</SectionEmpty>
        ) : rows.length === 0 ? (
          <SectionEmpty>
            {artifacts.length === 0
              ? results
                ? RESULTS_EMPTY
                : LIBRARY_EMPTY
              : `No ${kind.toLowerCase()} files among the ${artifacts.length} loaded.`}
          </SectionEmpty>
        ) : (
          rows.map((artifact) => (
            <LibraryRow
              key={artifact.id}
              artifact={artifact}
              active={artifact.id === selectedId}
              pinned={pins[artifact.id] ?? artifact.pinned}
              onSelect={onSelect}
            />
          ))
        )}

        {hasMore && error === null && (
          <button
            type="button"
            onClick={onLoadMore}
            disabled={loadingMore}
            className="mt-[6px] w-full cursor-pointer rounded-xl border border-line bg-transparent px-[10px] py-[8px] font-mono text-2xs-plus text-muted-fg hover:bg-muted-2 disabled:cursor-default disabled:text-faint"
          >
            {loadingMore
              ? "Loading…"
              : `Load more — ${artifacts.length} of ${total ?? artifacts.length}`}
          </button>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement.** Append to `src/views/library/format.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * A project's folder name — the last component of its root, either separator
 * (`/Users/dev/app` → `app`, `C:\dev\app` → `app`) — for a result row's
 * subtitle and the detail's meta row (storage design §13). `null` for no root.
 */
export function projectName(root: string | null): string | null {
  if (root === null) return null;
  const parts = root.split(/[\\/]/).filter((part) => part !== "");
  return parts.at(-1) ?? null;
}
```

  `src/views/library/preview.ts`: replace `export function previewPlan(artifact: Artifact): PreviewPlan { … }` (through
  its closing `}`, before the `diffPair` doc comment) with — the markup, image and text branches unchanged, and the two
  notes reading for a by-product (always `openable`) exactly as before:

```ts
export function previewPlan(artifact: Artifact): PreviewPlan {
  if (artifact.missing) {
    return {
      mode: "none",
      note: artifact.in_project
        ? `This file is no longer at ${artifact.rel_path} in the project. Its row is kept, and the file is shown again once it is back.`
        : "This file is no longer on disk. The daemon kept its record, so the history below is still real.",
    };
  }

  const markup = artifact.kind === "html" || isSvg(artifact.mime_type);

  if (artifact.kind === "image" && !markup) return { mode: "image" };

  // `Open` is named only where it is drawn: a row the daemon opens (ST-18).
  const binaryNote = artifact.openable
    ? "Export or Open opens it in its own app."
    : "Export saves it.";
  const wholeNote = artifact.openable
    ? "Export or Open opens the whole file."
    : "Export saves the whole file.";

  if (artifact.kind === "binary") {
    return {
      mode: "none",
      note: `Binary file, ${formatFileSize(artifact.size_bytes)} — ${binaryNote}`,
    };
  }

  if (artifact.size_bytes > MAX_PREVIEW_BYTES) {
    return {
      mode: "none",
      note: `Too large to preview here (${formatFileSize(artifact.size_bytes)}) — ${wholeNote}`,
    };
  }

  if (markup) {
    return {
      mode: "text",
      kind: "code",
      note: "Shown as source: rendering agent-authored markup in the app is a separate security review.",
    };
  }

  return { mode: "text", kind: toFileKind(artifact.kind), note: null };
}
```

```ts
/**
 * The name `Export` saves under: the last component of a row's name, either
 * separator — a file written into the project, `src/main.rs`, saves as
 * `main.rs`, since a saved file's name holds no folder; any other row's name
 * is already one component and is kept as it is.
 */
export function baseName(name: string): string {
  const parts = name.split(/[\\/]/).filter((part) => part !== "");
  return parts.at(-1) ?? name;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement.** `src/components/chat/WrittenArtifactCard.tsx`, whole file:

```tsx
/**
 * `WrittenArtifactCard` — a file an agent just wrote, shown inline in the
 * transcript.
 *
 * The same house shape as `RunReportCard` (§3.12): a status strip over a body,
 * with the eyebrow saying what happened and the right-hand mono segment
 * carrying the identity. Deliberately smaller than an `ArtifactCard` (§3.13):
 * an `artifact_written` frame carries the name, kind and version and *no
 * content*, so this card links to the file rather than previewing lines it does
 * not have. Everything it shows came off the frame.
 *
 * Beside `Open in Library`: `Open` (the file in its default app, through the
 * daemon) and `Reveal in Finder` (the file in its folder, through the Tauri
 * shell — drawn only inside the app's window, `canReveal`).
 *
 * A file written into the project (storage design §13, ST-12) is the project's
 * own file with a pointer row, not an artifact: the eyebrow says `in the
 * project`, the name is its path there, no version is drawn (it has none,
 * R37), and `Open` is drawn only when the frame's `openable` says the daemon
 * opens that kind (ST-18) — a `.sh` or a `Makefile` gets Reveal alone.
 */

import { Button, FileBadge, type FileKind } from "@/components/ui";
import { canReveal, revealLabel } from "@/lib/reveal";

export interface WrittenArtifactCardProps {
  name: string;
  kind: FileKind;
  language?: string | null;
  version: number;
  /** A result file in the project: named there, with no version drawn. */
  inProject: boolean;
  /** ST-18: whether `Open` is drawn — the frame's `openable`. */
  openable: boolean;
  /** `13:41`, or `null` when the frame's stamp is unreadable. */
  time: string | null;
  /** Opens the file in its default app. */
  onOpen: () => void;
  /** Shows the file in its folder; drawn only when `canReveal()`. */
  onReveal: () => void;
  /** Opens the file in the Library. */
  onOpenInLibrary: () => void;
}

export function WrittenArtifactCard({
  name,
  kind,
  language = null,
  version,
  inProject,
  openable,
  time,
  onOpen,
  onReveal,
  onOpenInLibrary,
}: WrittenArtifactCardProps) {
  return (
    <section className="mb-[26px] overflow-hidden rounded-3xl border border-line bg-raised">
      <header className="flex items-center gap-[9px] border-b border-line-hair bg-sunken px-[14px] py-[10px]">
        <span
          aria-hidden
          className="block h-[6px] w-[6px] shrink-0 rounded-full bg-blue"
        />
        <span className="font-mono text-2xs-plus tracking-eyebrow text-blue uppercase">
          File written
          {inProject && " · in the project"}
          {time !== null && ` · ${time}`}
        </span>
        {!inProject && (
          <span className="ml-auto font-mono text-xs text-faint">
            v{version}
          </span>
        )}
      </header>

      <div className="flex items-center gap-[10px] px-[14px] py-[12px]">
        <FileBadge kind={kind} size={19} language={language} />
        <span className="min-w-0 flex-1 truncate text-md font-medium">
          {name}
        </span>
        {openable && (
          <Button variant="ghostXs" onClick={onOpen} className="shrink-0">
            Open
          </Button>
        )}
        {canReveal() && (
          <Button variant="ghostXs" onClick={onReveal} className="shrink-0">
            {revealLabel()}
          </Button>
        )}
        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={onOpenInLibrary}
          className="shrink-0 cursor-pointer rounded-md border border-line bg-transparent px-[9px] py-[4px] font-sans text-sm-plus leading-[normal] font-medium text-secondary hover:bg-muted-2 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-blue"
        >
          Open in Library
        </button>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}
```

```ts
  useServerEvent(ARTIFACT_EVENTS, (event) => {
    if (event.type !== "artifact_written") return;
    if (event.task_id !== null && !started.current.has(event.task_id)) return;
    // A daemon older than storage design Stage 2 sends neither field: its
    // frame is a by-product, which opens (the Rust side's serde defaults).
    const inProject = event.in_project === true;
    const openable = event.openable !== false;
    setArtifacts((current) =>
      current.some(
        (entry) =>
          entry.artifactId === event.artifact_id &&
          // A project file is always version 1, so a rewrite of it is told
          // apart by its stamp; a by-product by its version.
          (inProject ? entry.at === event.ts : entry.version === event.version),
      )
        ? current
        : [
            ...current,
            {
              artifactId: event.artifact_id,
              name: event.name,
              kind: event.kind,
              version: event.version,
              path: event.path,
              taskId: event.task_id,
              at: event.ts,
              inProject,
              openable,
            },
          ],
    );
  });
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement.** `src/views/work/OutputSection.tsx`, whole file:

```tsx
/**
 * The work detail's `Output` card (DESIGN_SPEC §5.2, §3.27 framed variant),
 * and under it, when the run wrote into its project, **Written in the
 * project** (storage design §13, R38).
 *
 * The rows are `GET /v1/artifacts?task_id=` — this run's files, with real ids,
 * kinds and stamps, so every row opens. `Output` lists the run's by-products
 * (`in_project=false`) — drafts, hand-offs, a file saved with no project —
 * which are what the run's count, its chips and a connector's delivery count
 * (R38). The files it wrote into the project (`in_project=true`) are the
 * project's own and are listed apart, one row each. `task.outcome.artifacts`
 * (free-form JSON the dispatcher writes) is the fallback for a run whose
 * by-products the list cannot answer for, and those entries carry no id, so
 * such a row states what the run reported without pretending to open it.
 */

import {
  FileBadge,
  languageFromName,
  SectionCard,
  SectionEmpty,
} from "@/components/ui";
import type { OutcomeArtifact } from "@/components/work/run-model";
import { cn } from "@/lib/cn";

/** The design's own empty sentence for this card. */
export const OUTPUT_EMPTY =
  "Nothing produced yet. Files land here and in the Library as the run works.";

/** Output's sentence when the run's only files are in its project. */
export const OUTPUT_EMPTY_BESIDE_PROJECT =
  "Nothing else produced. The files this run wrote are in the project, below.";

/** The second card's title (R38's "written in the project"). */
export const PROJECT_FILES_TITLE = "Written in the project";

/** The second card's sentence when its list could not be read. */
export const PROJECT_FILES_UNREADABLE =
  "The files this run wrote into the project could not be listed.";

export interface OutputSectionProps {
  /** The run's by-products. */
  artifacts: readonly OutcomeArtifact[];
  /** `task.artifact_count` — by-products only (R38) — which can exceed the number of readable entries. */
  count: number;
  /** Present only once artifacts have ids to open. */
  onOpen?: (artifact: OutcomeArtifact) => void;
  /** Why the list is short or absent — a failed request, never a gap. */
  note?: string | null;
  /** The files the run wrote into its project, one row each. */
  projectFiles?: readonly OutcomeArtifact[];
  /** Their unpaged count; past `projectFiles.length` the card says how many more the Library holds. */
  projectTotal?: number;
  /** Why the project files could not be listed. */
  projectNote?: string | null;
}

const ROW =
  "flex w-full items-center gap-[10px] border-b border-line-hair-2 px-[16px] py-[11px] text-left last:border-b-0";

function FileRows({
  artifacts,
  onOpen,
}: {
  artifacts: readonly OutcomeArtifact[];
  onOpen?: (artifact: OutcomeArtifact) => void;
}) {
  return (
    <div>
      {artifacts.map((artifact) => {
        const inner = (
          <>
            <FileBadge
              kind={artifact.kind}
              size={17}
              language={languageFromName(artifact.name)}
            />
            <span className="min-w-0 flex-1 truncate text-base-plus text-ink">
              {artifact.name}
            </span>
            {artifact.stamp !== null && (
              <span className="shrink-0 font-mono text-xs text-muted-fg">
                {artifact.stamp}
              </span>
            )}
          </>
        );

        if (onOpen === undefined || artifact.id === null) {
          return (
            <div key={artifact.name} className={ROW}>
              {inner}
            </div>
          );
        }
        return (
          <button
            key={artifact.id}
            type="button"
            onClick={() => onOpen(artifact)}
            className={cn(
              ROW,
              "cursor-pointer border-none bg-transparent hover:bg-sunken",
              "focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-blue",
            )}
          >
            {inner}
          </button>
        );
      })}
    </div>
  );
}

function CardNote({ text }: { text: string | null }) {
  if (text === null || text === "") return null;
  return (
    <p className="m-0 px-[16px] pt-[8px] pb-[12px] font-mono text-2xs-plus leading-[1.5] text-faint">
      {text}
    </p>
  );
}

export function OutputSection({
  artifacts,
  count,
  onOpen,
  note = null,
  projectFiles = [],
  projectTotal = projectFiles.length,
  projectNote = null,
}: OutputSectionProps) {
  const more = projectTotal - projectFiles.length;
  const showProject =
    projectFiles.length > 0 || (projectNote !== null && projectNote !== "");

  return (
    <>
      <SectionCard title="Output">
        {artifacts.length === 0 ? (
          <SectionEmpty note={note ?? undefined}>
            {count > 0
              ? `This run reported ${count} file${count === 1 ? "" : "s"}, but none of them can be listed.`
              : projectFiles.length > 0
                ? OUTPUT_EMPTY_BESIDE_PROJECT
                : OUTPUT_EMPTY}
          </SectionEmpty>
        ) : (
          <>
            <FileRows artifacts={artifacts} onOpen={onOpen} />
            <CardNote text={note} />
          </>
        )}
      </SectionCard>

      {showProject && (
        <SectionCard
          title={PROJECT_FILES_TITLE}
          action={
            <span className="font-mono text-xs text-muted-fg">
              {`${projectTotal} file${projectTotal === 1 ? "" : "s"}`}
            </span>
          }
        >
          {projectFiles.length === 0 ? (
            <SectionEmpty note={projectNote ?? undefined}>
              {PROJECT_FILES_UNREADABLE}
            </SectionEmpty>
          ) : (
            <>
              <FileRows artifacts={projectFiles} onOpen={onOpen} />
              <CardNote
                text={
                  more > 0
                    ? `${more} more are listed in the Library, under Results in the project.`
                    : null
                }
              />
              <CardNote text={projectNote} />
            </>
          )}
        </SectionCard>
      )}
    </>
  );
}
```

  `src/views/work/RunDetail.tsx`: after `import { useArtifacts } from "@/hooks/useArtifacts";` add
  `import type { Artifact } from "@/lib/api/artifacts";`; after the imports (before `export interface RunDetailProps`)
  add:

```tsx
/**
 * One page of the files a run wrote into its project (R38): the list route's
 * own cap, so a run that writes forty files draws forty rows; past it the
 * card says how many more the Library holds.
 */
const PROJECT_FILES_LIMIT = 500;

/** A `GET /v1/artifacts` row as the Output and project cards draw it. */
function outcomeRow(artifact: Artifact): OutcomeArtifact {
  return {
    id: artifact.id,
    name: artifact.name,
    kind: toFileKind(artifact.kind),
    stamp: formatClock(artifact.updated_at),
  };
}
```

  replace the block from `  // The run's own files, with ids that open. \`run.outcome.artifacts\` stays the` through the `outputs` memo's

```tsx
  // The run's by-products, with ids that open — what its count, its chips and
  // a connector's delivery count (R38). `run.outcome.artifacts` stays the
  // fallback for a run the list cannot answer for.
  const files = useArtifacts(
    { taskId: runId ?? "", inProject: false },
    { enabled: runId !== null },
  );
  // The files it wrote into its project, listed apart.
  const written = useArtifacts(
    { taskId: runId ?? "", inProject: true, limit: PROJECT_FILES_LIMIT },
    { enabled: runId !== null },
  );
  const outputs = useMemo<OutcomeArtifact[] | null>(
    () =>
      files.data === undefined ? null : files.data.artifacts.map(outcomeRow),
    [files.data],
  );
  const projectFiles = useMemo<OutcomeArtifact[]>(
    () => (written.data?.artifacts ?? []).map(outcomeRow),
    [written.data],
  );
```

```tsx
            : null
```

## Stage 2 — slice S6: wording, documents, the gate, the live check and the records

Draft for the Stage 2 plan. Read at `d484a56a` (`feat/markdown-memory`). The spec is `spec-stage2.md` (design rev 0.9:
§0 ST-1…ST-22 and the rulings shown, Part II §10–§15, §16's Stage 2 clause, §17, §18's Stage 0 item "For Stage 2's
wording pass", §21); the shared names are `interfaces.md` (§0's S6 row, §1.3, §1.6, §4.2, §5.4–§5.9, §7, §8.3, §8.4,
§10, §10.1, §11). Owner decisions (ST-n) are not reopened; the lead's rulings (Rn) and the interfaces' corrections
(C1–C13) are the spec too.

**Every other slice lands before this one; the text below describes the tree after S6a.** One earlier task edits a
document this slice edits too, and the anchors below are written against the text it leaves: S4a.1 rewrites
`CLAUDE.md`'s *Storage* migration sentences (four entries, version 4, the recipe moved to `005`, a Migration 4
sentence; its *Spec conflicts*, 2). No slice S1–S6a edits `docs/*.md`, `docs/tools/*.md`, the repository
`README.md`, `apps/openalpaca-gui/API_MAP.md`, `apps/openalpaca-gui/DESIGN_SPEC.md` (S6a.12 records only code-side
comments, the GUI `README.md`'s `reveal_path` line included; the two app documents are S6.3d's, interfaces §8.4), the
rest of `CLAUDE.md` or the records under `tasks/`, so an anchor quoted from one of those is HEAD's and holds. An anchor in a code file another slice edits — `store/mod.rs`
(S3 rewrites `ContentKind::Scratch`'s doc, S4a removes `is_the_home_root`), `runner/lead_agent/tools.rs` (S3 adds
`SpawnSubagentTool`'s parameter), `runner/lead_agent/mod.rs` (S3, S5) — is quoted from HEAD and located by content;
each such task says what to do when a slice already reworded it. Where this draft cannot know what a slice left
(S6.2), the task is a sweep: the grep that prints what is left, and the rule for each line it prints. The words the
documents use for the built behaviour are interfaces.md's; S6.3a Step 1 reads the code as landed for each of them and
corrects a sentence where a slice deviated (its draft's *Spec conflicts* say where).

### What this slice does

It makes every sentence Stage 2 turned false true again, then proves the stage and records it. In code: the seeded home
README's `projects/` and `scratch/` rows and the store module's doc (S6.1); `check_subagent_status`'s description and
the lead's prompt say what a run with no conversation log gets — design §18's Stage 0 item (S6.1b); `file_read`'s
recovery hint names `file_list`, which never asks, instead of the shell, which now always does (S6.1c); a sweep of the
comments that still describe the daemon's directory as the file tools' root or Stage 2 as future (S6.2). In the
documents: the Daemon Manual — a new *The Working Folder* section (ST-10, ST-14, ST-16, R26–R33, R44–R46) and
*Where an agent's files land* rewritten (S6.3a); the CLI Manual and the repository README (S6.3b); the Installation
Manual's switch-over note — migration 004, `writing_agent`'s `file_read` line, an explicit confirmation list and
`file_edit` (S6.3c); the GUI Manual, `API_MAP.md` and `DESIGN_SPEC.md` rev 30 — S6a's surfaces and the card previews (S6.3d); the developer documents
`docs/agent-loop.md`, `docs/Skill_Template_Reference.md`, `docs/tools/DESIGN.md` and `docs/tools/TECHNICAL.md`
(S6.3e). Then one gate pass (S6.4), the live check on a rebuilt daemon under `loopback-only.sb` from its first launch,
in a project folder made for the test (S6.5), and the records (S6.6). No migration, no route, no CLI verb, no config
key, no event variant.

### Slice gate

Each task's own tests and checks are in its steps; the slice is green when all of these hold, one cargo process at a
time (`pgrep -x cargo` prints nothing before each):

```bash
CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never cargo test -p openalpaca_storage store::tests > /tmp/stage2-s6/storage.log 2>&1; echo "exit $?"
CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never cargo test -p openalpaca_core lead_agent > /tmp/stage2-s6/lead.log 2>&1; echo "exit $?"
CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never cargo test -p openalpaca_core compose::tests::test_golden_lead_agent_byte_identical > /tmp/stage2-s6/golden.log 2>&1; echo "exit $?"
CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never cargo test -p openalpaca_core agentic_loop::tests::test_tool_error_hint > /tmp/stage2-s6/hint.log 2>&1; echo "exit $?"
python3 scripts/gen_api_docs.py --check; echo "exit $?"
for f in /tmp/stage2-s6/check_s6_3*.py; do python3 "$f" || echo "FAILED $f"; done
(cd apps/openalpaca-gui && bun run format:check); echo "exit $?"
```

Expected: every `exit 0`, no `FAILED` line; each `.log` holds `test result: ok` lines only (`grep -c 'test result:
FAILED'` → `0`). Clippy against the baseline of **78**, the workspace run, the live-eval compile, `cargo check -p
openalpaca_gui` and all four bun gates are S6.4's, once, after S6.3e: S6 adds no Rust warning (its code changes are
string literals, comments and tests), and S6.4 Step 5 proves it.

### Rules every task follows

- **One cargo process at a time** (`pgrep -x cargo` before each). A task's tests run as `cargo test -p <crate>
  <filter>`; the workspace run is S6.4's, once, followed by `pkill -f "sleep 3600"` (the MCP hang tests' orphans).
- **No test and no command touches `~/.openalpaca`, and none acts in the repository.** S6.1's tests read a constant;
  S6.1b's and S6.1c's call pure functions; S6.5 points `OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE` and `OPENALPACA_CONFIG_DIR` into a
  scratch root before anything runs, and its project is a scratch git repository beside that store. Never read, list
  or write `~/.openalpaca`, and never name it in a command.
- **Anchored edits only.** Code: the Edit tool, quoting the old text whole. Documents: the two helper scripts below,
  which refuse an anchor that does not occur exactly once — never BSD `sed -i`. A heredoc carrying code, Markdown or
  paths is quoted (`<<'EOF'`; `tasks/lessons.md`, 2026-09). The documents' new text is written to each file's own
  line width (the manuals wrap near 80 columns, some long table rows do not); a fenced block in this plan is exact,
  line for line.
- **Formatting.** rustfmt is not run on a file this slice edits (several carry drift); the code below is written in
  rustfmt's style. Before a Rust file is edited, record `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <file> 2>/dev/null | grep -c
  '^Diff in'`; after the edit the count is the same and no `Diff in` line falls inside the edited lines.
  `apps/openalpaca-gui/API_MAP.md` and `DESIGN_SPEC.md` are inside `bun run format:check`'s reach
  (`.prettierignore` excludes only `dist`, `node_modules`, `src-tauri/target`, `src-tauri/gen`, `static`): new table
  rows are written unpadded and `bunx prettier --write API_MAP.md DESIGN_SPEC.md` re-pads them (S6.3d).
- **`python3 scripts/gen_api_docs.py --check`** at the end of every task that edits Rust: a doc comment on a route's
  request struct or a storage re-export feeds `docs/api`. No S6 task is expected to change it; if `--check` reports
  drift, run `python3 scripts/gen_api_docs.py` and stage `docs/api/` in the same commit.
- **Manuals name no ruling id.** User-facing text says what happens; the records carry the ids (R…, ST-…, C…). `docs/`
  keeps the links it already has (T12, T22, T35 by its row in `tasks/api-fix-plan.md`).
- **Records.** A design document's status line and revision log are bumped on every edit; a `.md` under `tasks/` is
  checked with `git check-ignore -q <file>` (exit 1 = tracked; `tasks/storage-design/*.md` and
  `tasks/memory-redesign/*.md` are whitelisted in `.gitignore`'s *Markdown Documentation (Except Manuals)* block;
  `tasks/todo.md` is ignored and never staged). A range is written `first^..last`. Cite `path:line` only for a line
  opened in that session.
- **Commits** use a conventional prefix, a `Verified:` line naming the command and its result, and end with
  `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. `git add` names explicit paths: the tree carries an
  untracked `tasks/deps-upgrade/` that is another session's.
- **Never print the daemon's token** (S6.5): the driver reads it from `discovery.json` and passes it nowhere else.

**The two helper scripts** (scratch, outside the repository, never committed). Make them once, before S6.1:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/stage2-s6
cat > /tmp/stage2-s6/s6edit.py <<'EOF'
"""Anchored edits for S6's text tasks. Every anchor must occur exactly once."""
import sys


def _once(text, old, where):
    n = text.count(old)
    if n != 1:
        sys.exit(f"{where}: anchor occurs {n} times, expected 1: {old[:120]!r}")
    return text.index(old)


def edit(path, ops):
    """ops: ("once", old, new) | ("span", start, end, new) | ("before", anchor, new) | ("after", anchor, new).

    "span" replaces from the start anchor (included) up to the end anchor (kept), the end anchor being the
    first occurrence after the start.
    """
    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    for op in ops:
        kind = op[0]
        if kind == "once":
            i = _once(text, op[1], path)
            text = text[:i] + op[2] + text[i + len(op[1]):]
        elif kind == "span":
            i = _once(text, op[1], path)
            j = text.find(op[2], i + len(op[1]))
            if j < 0:
                sys.exit(f"{path}: end anchor not found after the start: {op[2][:120]!r}")
            text = text[:i] + op[3] + text[j:]
        elif kind == "before":
            i = _once(text, op[1], path)
            text = text[:i] + op[2] + text[i:]
        elif kind == "after":
            i = _once(text, op[1], path) + len(op[1])
            text = text[:i] + op[2] + text[i:]
        else:
            sys.exit(f"unknown op {kind!r}")
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(text)
    print(f"edited {path}: {len(ops)} edits")
EOF
cat > /tmp/stage2-s6/s6check.py <<'EOF'
"""Word checks for S6's text tasks: (path, must contain, must not contain)."""
import sys


def check(spec):
    failures = []
    for path, must, must_not in spec:
        text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
        failures += [f"{path}: missing {s[:100]!r}" for s in must if s not in text]
        failures += [f"{path}: still says {s[:100]!r}" for s in must_not if s in text]
    for line in failures:
        print("FAIL", line)
    print("PASS" if not failures else f"{len(failures)} failures")
    sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)
EOF
```

### Task S6.1b: `check_subagent_status` and the lead's prompt say what a run with no conversation log gets (design §18, Stage 0's item for this pass)

Design §18 (from Stage 0): "A lead run with no session log cuts a long completed subagent answer head-only, although
the lead's prompt and `check_subagent_status`'s description promise a stub to page with `read_result`." The cut is the
agentic loop's inline fallback (`truncate_tool_result_to`, `runner/agentic_loop/tool_helpers.rs:14`): with no session
log a result over `tool_result_inline_bytes` keeps its first part and ends `[... truncated: showing first N of M
bytes]`. Since S3.13 (the lead's ruling R-T2) the run the design named — one parked by `POST /v1/tasks` on a lane with no conversation — gets the lane's session, and its log, at dispatch; the cut is still met by a run in a daemon that booted without a session log (a home store the log's root could not be resolved in: `apps/openalpacad/src/services/mod.rs`, "the daemon runs without a log rather than not at all"), and both texts still promise the stub alone. The fix the design
asks for is wording: both texts say both cases. Three tests pin the old text — two in `runner/lead_agent/tests.rs`
(`:544`, `:570`) and the golden test `test_golden_lead_agent_byte_identical` (`compose/tests.rs:2681`), whose
reference copy of the prompt's `<tools>` block (`:2794-2808`) must match `build_lead_agent_prompt_from_templates`
byte for byte — so all four places change in one commit.

### Task S6.1c: `file_read`'s recovery hint names `file_list`, not the shell

When `file_read` fails with "not found", the loop appends `Hint: verify the path exists using shell_execute with
\`ls\`.` (`tool_recovery_hint`, `runner/agentic_loop/tool_helpers.rs:68-71`). From Stage 2 every `shell_execute`
command raises an approval card (ST-14) and an unattended turn has it refused, while `file_list` (S5, R40) lists a
folder of the working folder and never asks (ST-16) — so the hint sends the model to the tool that costs the person a
card. No slice owns this string (interfaces §8.3 does not list it); S6 takes it as the wording pass §15 asks for.

- Modify: `crates/openalpaca_core/src/runner/agentic_loop/tool_helpers.rs` — `tool_recovery_hint`'s first arm

- Consumes: `format_tool_error_with_hint(tool_name: &str, msg: &str) -> String` (unchanged); S5's `file_list` tool
  (name `file_list`, a path relative to the working folder, `.` the folder itself).

```bash
     """**Where an agent's files land.** It depends on whether the conversation has
a project ([The Working Folder](#the-working-folder) says which folder a turn
works in).

- **In a project**, `file_write` writes the real file at its path relative to
  the project folder (`notes/plan.md` is `<project>/notes/plan.md`), and
  `file_edit` changes part of one: the exact text to find and the text to put
  in its place, the rest of the file kept byte for byte, line endings
  included. Each asks first, and its card names the project folder and the
  file. Before either replaces or changes a file that is there, its current
  content is copied into the conversation's log
  (`~/.openalpaca/sessions/<id>/snapshots/`), kept until that log is swept; a
  file larger than `[orchestrator.sessions] snapshot_max_bytes` (10 MiB by
  default) is refused rather than replaced with no copy, and so is a write
  whose copy fails. Where no copy can be kept — inside a skill or a plugin
  agent, which keep no conversation log — `file_write` creates a new file but
  refuses to replace one, and `file_edit` refuses. A file written this way
  gets a **pointer row**: the Library lists it with the project's results, by
  its path relative to the project; it is the real file — no copy, no
  versions (git keeps its history) — and its record follows an edit you make
  yourself. The tool's result names the file's absolute path and tells the
  model to give the user that path; if the row could not be written, it says
  the file is written and the app could not list it. A run's completion
  report ends with a line naming the files it wrote into the project, and its
  file count and chips count its by-products only; a connector is never sent
  a project's files on its own.
- **`artifact_write` saves a by-product** — a draft, a picture, something one
  agent hands another — in the artifact store: the project's folder in the
  home store (`~/.openalpaca/projects/<name>/artifacts/`) when the
  conversation has a project, the home store's own
  (`~/.openalpaca/artifacts/`) otherwise. It never asks: it writes only under
  `~/.openalpaca`. `workspace_write`, a workflow's shared notes, never asks
  either. `artifact_read` reads a by-product back by its id — the one
  `artifact_write`'s result, a workspace entry or `task_status` names — for
  the turn's owner, from the turn's project or from no project, paged like
  `read_result`; it never asks, and it refuses a result file in the project,
  which `file_read` reads.
- **With no project**, `file_write` saves a by-product the way `artifact_write`
  does, and still asks: named after its path (`reports/pasta-night.md`
  becomes `01-reports-pasta-night.md`; a path the name cannot carry whole —
  any character outside ASCII, more than 60 bytes of name, an extension no
  kind keeps, or none — also gets the first eight hex digits of its SHA-256,
  so `文档.md` becomes `01-artifact-<hash>.md` and `笔记.md` another
  artifact, `go.mod` and `go.sum` are two artifacts, and so are two files deep
  in one directory), with the path as written for its summary (which
  `GET /v1/artifacts?q=` searches), its kind taken from the extension (text
  whose extension no kind takes — `build.sh`, `Makefile` — is `code`, stored
  as `.bin`), the same path written again in the same run — or, outside a
  run, on the same UTC day — its next version, announced as
  `artifact_written` and listed in the Library. Two paths the name carries
  whole that differ only in letter case or in characters that are not ASCII
  letters or digits (`Notes.md` and `notes.md`, `a/b.md` and `a-b.md`,
  `__main__.py` and `main.py`) still reach one name, so they are one
  artifact's versions. The tool's result tells the model the write is
  complete: which artifact and version, its absolute path — the path to give
  the user — that the Library lists it, that the file is the deliverable and
  is not to be copied elsewhere with the shell or any other tool, that
  `artifact_read` reads it back by its id, and that writing the same path
  again saves its next version. `file_edit` is refused with no project; its
  sentence names `file_write`.

A path that names no file (`''`, `.`, `reports/`, a blank name) is refused,
and a turn with no owner — `POST /v1/command {"command":"process"}` runs as
the system — cannot save a by-product; in a project its file is still
written, and the result says the app could not list it.

"""),
    # (f) DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}
    ("once",
     "- The session's log directory, `~/.openalpaca/sessions/<id>/`, is removed.",
     "- The session's log directory, `~/.openalpaca/sessions/<id>/`, is removed, and so is\n"
     "  its scratch folder, `~/.openalpaca/scratch/<id>/`, if it has one\n"
     "  ([The Working Folder](#the-working-folder))."),
    # (g) the new section, before Streaming Surfaces
    ("before",
     "## Streaming Surfaces",
     """## The Working Folder

Every file tool and every shell command of a turn acts in one folder, the
turn's **working folder**:

- **With a project**, the project's own folder — the git repository's top
  folder, or the folder you chose. `file_read`, `file_list`, `file_write`,
  `file_edit` and `send` take paths relative to it, and a `shell_execute`
  command starts in it. A command tool you defined under `config/tools` runs
  in it too; a skill's own scripts run in the skill's folder.
- **With no project** — a Telegram, iMessage or Discord conversation, a
  scheduled skill, a conversation that never named a folder, a run started
  by `POST /v1/tasks` with no project — it is the conversation's **scratch
  folder**, `~/.openalpaca/scratch/<conversation id>/`, made (`0700`) the
  first time a tool works there, so one conversation never sees another's
  files. It goes with the conversation: deleting the conversation, or deleting
  the data of the project it was later bound to, removes it. Clearing or
  archiving the conversation keeps it, the session-log size caps never touch
  it, and a factory reset leaves it on disk. There `file_write` saves a
  by-product ([Where an agent's files land](#files-artifacts-and-workspaces))
  and `file_edit` is refused.
- A run started by `POST /v1/tasks` on a lane that has no conversation yet
  is given one when it is dispatched — the lane's, opened then — so its
  file tools and commands work in that conversation's scratch folder. Only
  a call with neither a project nor a conversation is refused, with a
  sentence saying why.
- A project whose folder is gone (`missing`) is refused before any tool runs,
  and the sentence names the two ways out — re-point the project or delete its
  data ([Files, artifacts and workspaces](#files-artifacts-and-workspaces)).
  A turn whose project was re-pointed or deleted while the conversation ran
  is refused too, with a sentence saying no folder under `projects/` records
  that folder any more.
- The model is told its working folder in one line of each turn's context —
  the chat's, a skill's, a workflow's lead's and each subagent's.
- The daemon's own working directory stays where its launcher put it; only an
  MCP server whose entry names no `cwd`, and the CLI model fallback, start
  there (a plugin runs in its own folder).

**What the file tools refuse.** A path is relative, never holds `..`, and must
resolve — every link in it followed, the last part included — to a place inside
the working folder: a link that leads out of it is refused for reading and for
writing (`Path '<path>' resolves outside the workspace boundary`). In a
project, writing anything inside its `.git` folder is refused (run git through
`shell_execute` instead), and an `.openalpaca` folder inside a project — an
older OpenAlpaca's — is refused for reading and for writing. Nothing else is: a
project may hold a `state/` folder or a `SOUL.md` of its own, and the file tools
read and write them like any other file.

**Reading never asks.** `file_read`, `file_list`, `artifact_read` and
`read_result` raise no approval card. In a project an agent can read any file
under the project's top folder, secrets such as `.env` included, and what it
reads goes to the model that answers — to the provider's servers when that
model is not local. Keep secrets out of a project you work on with a remote
model, or use a local one.

**The shell is not confined.** A command starts in the working folder, and that
is all: an absolute path, `~` or `cd /` reaches anywhere, and an approved
command runs as you, anywhere you can — it can read
`~/.openalpaca/state/discovery.json` and answer the approval prompts that
follow it, edit `daemon.toml` to switch prompting off, and read the master key
file. So every `shell_execute` command asks first, its card names the folder it
runs in, and the card is the one place to stop it: read the command before you
approve it. Only an operating-system sandbox would change this, and none is used
in this version. A command, a command tool or a skill script that runs past its
time limit, or whose turn or run is cancelled, is killed, with the processes it
started (on Windows, the command alone).

**The `../` check.** Before a tool runs, its arguments are checked for `../`.
OpenAlpaca's own tools are exempt — their path arguments carry their own `..`
refusal, and their other arguments are content, such as a source file with a
relative import or a command for the shell — while a skill's script, a command
tool, an MCP tool and a plugin's tool are refused any argument holding `../`,
since it reaches a shell line or another program.

"""),
    # (h) Tool confirmations: which tools ask
    ("once",
     "A tool on the confirm list pauses until somebody answers.",

folder, a file over the size limit, or one whose old content cannot be kept."""),
```

### Task S6.4: The stage gate — one workspace run, clippy, the checks, all four bun gates, the sweeps

**Files:** none changed in the repository (Step 11 writes `tasks/todo.md`, which is git-ignored). **Interfaces:** none.

The gate runs once, after S6.3e's commit. Never two cargo processes at a time. Every cargo command runs with
`CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never`, its full output to a file (never a pipe: the MCP manager's hang tests leave orphaned
`sleep 3600` children holding a pipe open), and its own exit code recorded (`tasks/lessons.md`, 2026-09: "Cargo's
colour codes and a `tail` make a failed gate read as green"). Stage 2 adds two things to Stage 1's gate: from this
stage on the file tools and the shell act on real files, so the run must leave the repository exactly as it found it
(Step 3); and R45's tests spawn `sleep 30` grandchildren that must all be dead when the run ends (Step 3).

- [ ] **Step 1: The tree is the stage's.**

```bash
git status --short
git log --oneline <BASE>..HEAD | wc -l
mkdir -p /tmp/stage2-gate
pgrep -f 'sleep 30$' | wc -l > /tmp/stage2-gate/sleep30-before.txt; cat /tmp/stage2-gate/sleep30-before.txt
```

  Expected: `git status` lists only `?? tasks/deps-upgrade/` (another session's); the log counts the stage's commits
  (`<BASE>` is the commit S1's first task started from, recorded when the stage began — `d484a56a` if nothing landed
  between); the `sleep 30` count before the run is recorded (normally `0`; anything else is not this run's).

- [ ] **Step 2: The workspace tests, one run.**

```bash
pgrep -x cargo
CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never cargo test --workspace --exclude openalpaca_gui > /tmp/stage2-gate/test.log 2>&1; echo "exit $?"
pkill -f "sleep 3600"
grep -c 'test result: FAILED' /tmp/stage2-gate/test.log
awk '/^test result:/ {p+=$4; f+=$6; i+=$8} END {print p" passed, "f" failed, "i" ignored"}' /tmp/stage2-gate/test.log
```

  Expected: `exit 0`; `0`; `<N> passed, 0 failed, 16 ignored`. `<N>` is recorded, not predicted: Stage 1's gate was
  4,722 at `00f057fe`, and the slices add and delete tests. No draft adds an `#[ignore]` (each slice's drafts carry
  none; S6 adds none), so a count other than 16 is checked against `git diff <BASE>..HEAD | grep -c '^+.*#\[ignore'`
  before anything else. A failure is fixed in the task that broke it (a new commit), and the whole run repeats.

- [ ] **Step 3: The run touched no real file and left no process.**

```bash
git status --short
find . -path ./target -prune -o -path ./apps/openalpaca-gui/node_modules -prune -o -path ./apps/openalpaca-gui/src-tauri/target -prune -o \( -name scratch -o -name '.openalpaca' \) -newer /tmp/stage2-gate/sleep30-before.txt -print
sleep 3; pgrep -fl 'sleep 30$'; pgrep -f 'sleep 30$' | wc -l
```

  Expected: `git status` unchanged from Step 1 (only `?? tasks/deps-upgrade/`) — no test wrote, edited or ran a
  command in the repository (interfaces §0's rule; every such test runs in a `GuardedProject` tempdir); `find` prints
  nothing (no `scratch/` or `.openalpaca/` made in the tree during the run); the `sleep 30` count equals Step 1's
  (R45's tests kill their grandchildren, and `KillOnFail` covers a failed assertion). A process left over is a
  test's defect: `pgrep -fl` names it; kill it by pid and fix the test in its slice's area.

```bash
strings -a target/debug/openalpacad | grep -cF "take the crate's home-store guard"
```

  test` with storage's `test-home-guard`). This binary is not launched; S6.5 rebuilds with `cargo build` and expects

### Task S6.5: The live check — agents in a project folder made for the test, on the rebuilt daemon (and the app, where the session has screen access)

**Files:** Create `tasks/storage-design/stage2-live-report.md` (tracked: `tasks/storage-design/*.md` is whitelisted;
`git check-ignore -q` on it exits `1`). Everything else lives in a scratch root outside the repository and is not
committed.

**What it proves** (spec §16's Stage 2 clause, §0.4's two items, and the brief's list): in a project folder made for
the test — (a) a `file_write` of a real file: its card names the project folder, the file lands in the project, a
pointer row lists it (`in_project`, `openable`) and `artifact_written` says so; (b) a `file_edit`: its card shows the
file, the line and the two texts, the old content is kept under the conversation's `snapshots/`, and the same row is
updated; (b2) `openalpaca chat`'s inline prompt prints such a preview with its line breaks (interfaces §11's
UNVERIFIED item, live-only: this check is where it is answered); (c) a shell command's card names the folder, `openalpaca tasks confirmations list` shows that
preview, the CLI answers it, and the command runs there; (d) `file_list` and `file_read` — `.env` included — never
prompt; (e) a by-product of the project saved by a workflow's lead with `artifact_write` raises no card (ST-15) and is
read back from the main chat with `artifact_read` (R41, §0.4); (f) a path through a link that leaves the project is
refused, for writing and for reading, with no card; (g) a write into `.git` is refused, with no card; (h) a
conversation with no project works in its own scratch folder — the shell starts there, `file_read` reads there,
`file_write` saves a by-product read back with `artifact_read` — and the folder goes when the conversation is deleted;
(i) §0.4's stale approval card, only with screen access the owner granted: a prompt answered from the CLI while the
app shows its card, then the card clicked. Without screen access the report says so and names
`views/chat/approval-card-returns.test.tsx` (S6.4 Step 9 ran it) as the proof. Last, the repository's own files are
byte-identical but for the one file the agent was asked to write.

**Standing rules** (`tasks/lessons.md`, the four 2026-10 entries; Stage 1's S6.5; the owner):
- `~/.openalpaca` is the owner's real store: never read, list, write or name it in a command. Every command that
  starts or talks to a daemon has `OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE` and `OPENALPACA_CONFIG_DIR` pointing into the scratch root.
- The scratch root is canonical from the moment it is made (`realpath`; on macOS `/tmp` is `/private/tmp`): every
  expected path is built from it, never from `mktemp`'s spelling (lessons, 2026-10-08).
- The daemon runs under `scripts/eval/memory/loopback-only.sb` **from its first launch**, the profile proven before the
  first model turn. Nothing leaves the machine. The model is the local Ollama `qwen3.8:27b-mlx` (the owner's standing
  authorization for live checks).
- A fresh store's first turn is persona onboarding: one attended onboarding turn first; a refusal during onboarding is
  not an attempt. A daemon started by hand logs to stderr — read `daemon.out`, not `state/logs/daemon.log`.
- Attended turns go through the HTTP API with `unattended: false`; every pending confirmation is recorded — tool,
  arguments **and preview** — **before** it is answered, and only the tools a step names are approved; anything else is
  denied and recorded. A step that names `--hold` leaves its prompt for the CLI to answer. The token is read inside the
  driver and never printed.
- A model may word a tool call differently from the prompt (a path with `./`, other content). A check reads the call's
  own arguments from the confirmation or the session log and judges against them; a model that will not make the call
  is asked once more naming the tool, every attempt is recorded, and a model's refusal is not a FAIL of the daemon —
  that check is then "not exercised live", and its unit tests stand.
- `cargo build -p openalpacad -p openalpaca` runs immediately before the daemon is launched (Stage 1's R-S5).
- Never answer a macOS permission or keychain dialog: leave it on screen and say so in the report. No `git` command
  here may sign: every commit in the scratch repository passes `-c commit.gpgsign=false`.
- No `git status` inside the scratch repository before Step 15's hashes (it may rewrite `.git/index`).

- [ ] **Step 5: The driver.** Stage 1's driver (its S6.5 Step 5) with four additions: each confirmation is recorded
  with its `preview` and `per_call`; `--hold TOOL` records a prompt and leaves it pending, writing its id to
  `evidence/<label>.held`; a `delete` subcommand; and `turn` records the session the lane is on afterwards. Save as
  `$OA/driver.py` (scratch, not committed):

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stage 2 live-check driver over the daemon's HTTP API.

The port and the token come from $OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE/state/discovery.json;
the token is never printed or written. Every request and answer is appended to
evidence/<label>.jsonl beside this file.

  driver.py turn   <label> <message> [--workspace P] [--session ID] [--approve TOOL]... [--hold TOOL]...
  driver.py get    <label> <path> [--workspace P]          prints the JSON answer
  driver.py post   <label> <path> <json> [--workspace P]   prints the JSON answer
  driver.py delete <label> <path>                          prints the status
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import threading
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request

STORE = os.environ["OPENALPACA_HOME_STORE"]
EVIDENCE = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "evidence")
os.makedirs(EVIDENCE, exist_ok=True)
with open(os.path.join(STORE, "state", "discovery.json")) as f:
    _discovery = json.load(f)
BASE = f"http://{_discovery['listen']['host']}:{_discovery['listen']['port']}"
TOKEN = _discovery["auth"]["token"]


def call(method, path, body=None, workspace=None, timeout=120):
    data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}"}
    if data is not None:
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    if workspace:
        headers["x-workspace-path"] = urllib.parse.quote(workspace, safe="/")
    request = urllib.request.Request(BASE + path, data=data, method=method, headers=headers)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout) as response:
            status, payload = response.status, response.read()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        status, payload = e.code, e.read()
    try:
        return status, (json.loads(payload) if payload else None)
    except ValueError:
        return status, payload.decode(errors="replace")


def record(label, kind, **fields):
    row = {"t": time.strftime("%H:%M:%S"), "kind": kind, **fields}
    with open(os.path.join(EVIDENCE, f"{label}.jsonl"), "a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    shown = json.dumps(fields, ensure_ascii=False)
    print(f"[{row['t']}] {kind} {shown[:1200]}", flush=True)


def turn(args):
    allowed, held = set(args.approve), set(args.hold)
    stop = threading.Event()
    seen = set()

    def answer_prompts():
        while not stop.is_set():
            status, body = call("GET", "/v1/chat/confirmations")
            pending = body.get("confirmations", []) if status == 200 and isinstance(body, dict) else []
            for c in pending:
                rid = c.get("request_id")
                if rid in seen:
                    continue
                seen.add(rid)
                tool = c.get("tool_name")
                fields = dict(request_id=rid, tool_name=tool, agent_id=c.get("agent_id"),
                              task_id=c.get("task_id"), tool_arguments=c.get("tool_arguments"),
                              preview=c.get("preview"), per_call=c.get("per_call"))
                if tool in held:
                    record(args.label, "confirmation_held", **fields)
                    with open(os.path.join(EVIDENCE, f"{args.label}.held"), "a") as f:
                        f.write(rid + "\n")
                    continue
                ok = tool in allowed
                record(args.label, "confirmation", approved=ok, **fields)
                status2, _ = call("POST", f"/v1/chat/confirmations/{rid}", {"approved": ok})
                record(args.label, "confirmation_answered", request_id=rid, http=status2)
            time.sleep(1)

    body = {"content": args.message, "unattended": False}
    if args.session:
        body["session_id"] = args.session
        body["activate"] = True
    status, answer = call("POST", "/v1/chat", body, workspace=args.workspace)
    record(args.label, "post_chat", http=status, body=answer, message=args.message, workspace=args.workspace)
    if status != 200:
        return 2
    threading.Thread(target=answer_prompts, daemon=True).start()
    url = f"{BASE}/v1/chat/stream/{answer['stream_id']}?token={urllib.parse.quote(TOKEN)}"
    done, deltas, event, data = None, [], None, []
    with urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url), timeout=args.timeout) as stream:
        for raw in stream:
            line = raw.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip("\r\n")
            if line.startswith(":"):
                continue
            if line.startswith("event:"):
                event = line[6:].strip()
            elif line.startswith("data:"):
                data.append(line[5:].lstrip())
            elif line == "" and (event or data):
                payload = "\n".join(data)
                try:
                    obj = json.loads(payload)
                except ValueError:
                    obj = payload
                if event == "delta":
                    deltas.append(obj.get("content", "") if isinstance(obj, dict) else str(obj))
                elif event != "reasoning":
                    record(args.label, f"sse_{event}", data=obj)
                if event in ("done", "error"):
                    done = obj
                    break
                event, data = None, []
    record(args.label, "answer", text="".join(deltas))
    delegation = done.get("delegation") if isinstance(done, dict) else None
    task_id = delegation.get("task_id") if isinstance(delegation, dict) else None
    if task_id:
        started = time.time()
        while time.time() - started < args.run_timeout:
            status, task = call("GET", f"/v1/tasks/{task_id}")
            task = task if isinstance(task, dict) else {}
            state = task.get("status") or (task.get("task") or {}).get("status")
            if state in ("completed", "failed", "cancelled", "interrupted"):
                record(args.label, "run_end", task_id=task_id, status=state)
                break
            time.sleep(5)
    stop.set()
    return 0


def show(args, status, body, kind):
    record(args.label, kind, http=status, body=body)
    print(json.dumps({"http": status, "body": body}, ensure_ascii=False))
    return 0 if status < 400 else 1


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    t = sub.add_parser("turn")
    t.add_argument("label")
    t.add_argument("message")
    t.add_argument("--workspace")
    t.add_argument("--session")
    t.add_argument("--approve", action="append", default=[])
    t.add_argument("--hold", action="append", default=[])
    t.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=900)
    t.add_argument("--run-timeout", type=int, default=2700)
    for name in ("get", "delete"):
        g = sub.add_parser(name)
        g.add_argument("label")
        g.add_argument("path")
        g.add_argument("--workspace")
    p = sub.add_parser("post")
    p.add_argument("label")
    p.add_argument("path")
    p.add_argument("body")
    p.add_argument("--workspace")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.cmd == "turn":
        return turn(args)
    if args.cmd == "get":
        return show(args, *call("GET", args.path, workspace=args.workspace), "get")
    if args.cmd == "delete":
        return show(args, *call("DELETE", args.path, workspace=args.workspace), "delete")
    return show(args, *call("POST", args.path, json.loads(args.body), workspace=args.workspace), "post")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

  Check it parses: `python3 -m py_compile "$OA/driver.py"`. The session log is the evidence of every tool result —
  a refusal raised before any card included — so a second small script reads it, paging with `after_seq` (the route
  answers at most `MAX_EVENTS_LIMIT` = 500 records and 4 MiB a page, `apps/openalpacad/src/routes/sessions.rs:62`,
  `:70`, and returns `next_after_seq`). Save as `$OA/results.py`:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The records of one type in one conversation's session log, every page.

  results.py <session> <label> [type]   type defaults to tool_result: name, ok, and the error or the result's head
"""
import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import driver  # noqa: E402  (reads the port and token; its main() runs only as a script)

session, label = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
kind = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "tool_result"
after, rows = None, []
for _ in range(200):
    path = f"/v1/sessions/{session}/events?types={kind}&limit=500"
    if after is not None:
        path += f"&after_seq={after}"
    status, body = driver.call("GET", path)
    if status != 200 or not isinstance(body, dict):
        sys.exit(f"HTTP {status}: {body}")
    rows += body.get("events", [])
    nxt = body.get("next_after_seq")
    # The type filter runs over each scanned page, so a page can match nothing
    # and still not be the last: stop only when the cursor stops moving.
    if nxt is None or nxt == after:
        break
    after = nxt
driver.record(f"results-{label}", "results", session=session, kind=kind, count=len(rows))
for e in rows:
    d = e.get("data", {})
    if kind == "tool_result":
        text = d.get("error") or d.get("result") or ""
        print(d.get("name"), d.get("ok"), json.dumps(str(text)[:300], ensure_ascii=False))
    else:
        print(kind, json.dumps(d, ensure_ascii=False)[:300])
```

  and two shell helpers every later step uses (paste into the same shell):

```bash
python3 -m py_compile "$OA/results.py"
db() { sqlite3 -readonly "$STORE/state/openalpaca.db" "$1"; }
results() { python3 "$OA/results.py" "$@"; }
```

  The route filters `types` over each page it scans (`get_session_events`, `apps/openalpacad/src/routes/sessions.rs`:
  `next_after_seq` is the last seq **read**), so a page can hold no record of the type and not be the last — the loop
  ends only when the cursor stops moving. The record fields are `data.name`, `data.ok`, `data.error` (a refusal's
  text, `null` on success) and `data.result` (`null` when the result spilled to `results/`), as
  `runner/agentic_loop/mod.rs:1206-1216` writes them and `LoggedRecord` (`session_log/reader.rs:35-50`) serves them.
